1. Amphan — 2020 — Kolkata urban floods
2. Michaung — 2023 — Gujarat offshore infrastructure
3. Fengal — 2024 — Tamil Nadu–Puducherry coast
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
19.x: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct as per the notes. Pair 2 is wrong: Michaung (2023, Bay of Bengal) caused Chennai floods and hit the AP coast; Gujarat's offshore infrastructure was hit by Tauktae (2021, Arabian Sea). So '1 only' misses pair 3, while '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the wrong pair 2.
19.tq: Bay of Bengal storms hit the east coast; Gujarat means an Arabian Sea storm.

19.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the cyclone with its basin and principal impact?
o: Tauktae — Arabian Sea — Gujarat and offshore infrastructure
Biparjoy — Bay of Bengal — Chennai floods
19.x: Tauktae occurred in the Arabian Sea in 2021, affected Gujarat and damaged offshore infrastructure. Biparjoy was also an Arabian Sea cyclone, while Michaung affected Chennai in 2023.
19.tq: Start from the basin-impact pair and reject basin swaps among recent cyclones.

19.s: Which cyclone was described as the longest-lived cyclone of the Arabian Sea?
19.x: Biparjoy, which affected Gujarat in 2023, was described as the longest-lived Arabian Sea cyclone.
19.tq: Identify the superlative associated with the correct named event.

19.s: Which cyclone made landfall on the Kakinada coast of Andhra Pradesh in October 2025?
19.x: Cyclone Montha occurred in October 2025 in the Bay of Bengal and made landfall on the Kakinada coast of Andhra Pradesh.
19.tq: Use the precise landfall location to discriminate among similarly dated cyclones.

19.s:
Consider the following statements about selected tropical cyclones:
1. Idai occurred in 2019 in the south-west Indian Ocean and affected Mozambique.
2. Shakti was an Arabian Sea cyclone in 2025 and its name was assigned by Sri Lanka.
3. Ditwah occurred in the south-western Bay of Bengal in November 2025 and was associated with India’s Operation Sagar Bandhu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: All three statements are correct. Idai affected Mozambique in 2019; Shakti was an Arabian Sea cyclone named by Sri Lanka in 2025; and Ditwah was linked with Operation Sagar Bandhu in November 2025.
19.tq: Verify each cyclone through its year, basin and associated fact before choosing the coded option.

19.s: The low over the Andaman Sea around 19–21 September 2026 was expected to potentially become:
o: The first cyclone of the North-East monsoon season, moving towards Gujarat
The first cyclone of the South-West monsoon season, moving towards Odisha
A temperate cyclone moving towards Kerala
A heat dome moving towards the Arabian Peninsula
19.x: The low over the Andaman Sea around 19–21 September 2026 was expected to become the first cyclone of that South-West monsoon season and head towards the Odisha coast.
19.tq: Combine the date, originating region, seasonal description and projected track without reversing the direction.

19.s:
With reference to Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. Its coastline is about 1,053 km long.
2. It is described as the third-longest coastline among Indian States.
3. Cyclone impacts occur mostly during October–December.
4. North coastal districts and Nellore/Bapatla suffer the most.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
19.x: Andhra Pradesh has a 1,053 km coastline, ranked third-longest, and is affected mostly in October–December; north coastal districts and Nellore/Bapatla are especially vulnerable.
19.tq: Combine the numerical, ranking, seasonal and spatial clues instead of treating them as alternatives.

19.s: Which of the following set contains only cyclones cited in relation to Andhra Pradesh's October–December cyclone impacts?
19.x: Hudhud, Titli, Michaung and Montha are the cyclones cited in relation to Andhra Pradesh's mainly October–December impacts.
19.tq: Eliminate sets containing storms associated with other examples or contexts.

19.s: India's “zero casualty” approach to cyclones has been followed since which cyclone?
19.x: The zero-casualty approach to cyclones in India is stated to have been followed since Phailin.
19.tq: Match the disaster-management approach with its stated starting event.

19.s: During Cyclone Montha (October 2025), Andhra Pradesh auto-triggered evacuations and alerts using which RTGS system?
19.x: RTGS AWARE 2.0 auto-triggered evacuations using 423 drones and sent alerts to 3.60 crore people, keeping deaths to only 15. Damini is the lightning-alert app, Sagar Bandhu was India's operation for Cyclone Ditwah in Sri Lanka, and 'Mausam 2.0' is not in the notes.
19.tq: Montha → AWARE 2.0, 15 deaths.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT an element of climate listed in climatological analysis?
20.x: The listed elements of climate are temperature, pressure, winds, humidity, precipitation and cloudiness. Lithology is not an element of climate in this list.
20.tq: Identify the outsider from the standard set of climatic elements.

20.s: Weather is best defined as:
o: The state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time
The long-term distribution of vegetation over a region
The average atmospheric condition over a period of 30 years
The seasonal variation in ocean currents only
20.x: Weather refers to the state of the atmosphere at a particular place and time. Climate refers to average weather over a long period.
20.tq: Distinguish the short-term weather definition from the long-term climate definition.

20.s: The World Meteorological Organization’s standard period for describing climate normals is:
20.x: The WMO standard describes climate using average weather conditions over a period of 30 years.
20.tq: Test the standard numerical period directly.

20.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A climograph represents monthly temperature and rainfall of a station on one chart.
2. Temperature is generally represented by a line in a climograph.
3. Rainfall is generally represented by bars in a climograph.
4. A climograph can assist in identifying the climate type of a place.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: A climograph combines monthly temperature, shown by a line, and rainfall, shown by bars, and is used to interpret the climate type of a station.
20.tq: Combine the chart components and their use before selecting the coded answer.

20.s: The current IMD rainfall normal for the southwest monsoon season, based on the 1971–2020 period, is:
20.x: The IMD normal rainfall for June–September, based on the 1971–2020 base period, is 868.6 mm.
20.tq: Separate the precise normal value from nearby numerical distractors.

20.s: Which one of the following is NOT regarded as a control of climate?
20.x: Distance from a river is not a recognised control of climate. Latitude, altitude and distance from the sea influence climatic conditions.
20.tq: Find the factor that does not belong to the standard climatic controls.

20.s: The mainland of India lies approximately between which latitudes?
20.x: India’s mainland extends approximately from 8°N to 37°N. Insolation generally decreases towards the poles.
20.tq: Recall the precise geographical range rather than the broader regional location.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding latitude as a climatic control:
1. The angle of the Sun’s rays varies with latitude.
2. Insolation generally decreases poleward.
3. Areas south of the Tropic of Cancer in India are broadly tropical.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All three statements are correct. Latitude affects the angle of solar rays and the amount of insolation received.
20.tq: Test the linked effects of latitude through a coded combination.

20.s: The normal rate at which temperature decreases with increase in altitude is approximately
20.x: Temperature falls at approximately 6.5°C for every 1,000 metres of ascent under the normal lapse rate.
20.tq: Use the standard numerical value associated with altitude and temperature.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the climatic contrast produced by distance from the sea?
o: Distance from the sea affects rainfall but not temperature
Coastal areas have continental extremes, while interiors are equable
Coastal areas are generally equable, while interiors experience greater extremes
Both coasts and interiors have identical seasonal ranges
20.x: The sea moderates temperatures near the coast, whereas inland areas tend to experience greater temperature extremes and a continental climate.
20.tq: Identify the correctly reversed coastal–continental comparison.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about relief and climate:
1. Windward slopes generally receive more rainfall.
2. Leeward slopes may lie in a rain-shadow region.
3. The Himalayas keep northern India about 3–8°C warmer in winter than places on the same latitude.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All three statements are correct. Relief causes windward rainfall and leeward rain-shadow conditions, while the Himalayas moderate winter temperatures in northern India.
20.tq: Combine the direct and comparative effects of relief in a coded option.

20.s: Which of the following statements regarding ocean currents and climate is correct?
o: Ocean currents have no effect on coastal climates
Warm currents make tropical western coasts permanently arid
Cold currents make tropical western coasts cool and dry
Cold currents make eastern continental coasts warm and rainy
20.x: Cold currents cool and dry adjacent coasts, particularly on the western margins of tropical continents. Warm currents tend to make coasts warmer and wetter.
20.tq: Discriminate between the contrasting effects of cold and warm currents.

20.s: Which of the following is a set of climatic influences associated with winds and pressure belts?
o: Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones
Tides, ocean trenches, glaciers and earthquakes
River capture, folding, faulting and weathering
Volcanoes, soil horizons, deltas and plateaus
20.x: Monsoons, westerlies, western disturbances and cyclones are atmospheric circulation features associated with winds and pressure systems.
20.tq: Select the group belonging to atmospheric circulation rather than geomorphic processes.

20.s: The Tropic of Cancer crosses how many Indian states?
20.x: The Tropic of Cancer crosses eight Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
20.tq: Test a fixed geographical count and its associated list.

20.s: Shimla is considerably cooler than Amritsar despite their similar latitude primarily because of:
o: The influence of the north-east monsoon
The absence of the Himalayas near Shimla
20.x: Altitude is the major factor making Shimla much cooler than Amritsar at a similar latitude.
20.tq: Apply the altitude control of climate to a paired-location example.

20.s: The climate of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is generally:
o: Semi-arid with a large annual temperature range
20.x: The maritime influence gives the Andaman and Nicobar Islands an equable and humid climate.
20.tq: Use the island-versus-interior climate contrast.

20.s: What would be the most significant climatic consequence for northern India if the Himalayas did not exist?
o: The southwest monsoon would reverse permanently into a north-easterly wind.
The region would receive heavier monsoon rainfall because cold air would enter freely.
Northern India would tend to become a desert because the Himalayas would no longer block cold Central Asian air or trap the monsoon.
The Tibetan Plateau would become a permanent oceanic low-pressure centre.
20.x: The Himalayas block cold Central Asian air and help trap the monsoon over the subcontinent. Without them, northern India would tend to become a desert.
20.tq: Apply the barrier and trapping functions of a major relief feature to a hypothetical situation.

20.s: In India, the climatic type corresponding to Koeppen’s As classification is associated with the
20.x: Koeppen’s As climate, characterised by dry summers and winter rainfall, occurs on the Coromandel Coast of Tamil Nadu.
20.tq: Match the Koeppen symbol with its Indian regional occurrence.

20.s: Who proposed the empirical climatic classification scheme based on mean temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation?
20.x: Wladimir Koeppen proposed an empirical climatic classification based on mean temperature and precipitation, with climate types linked to natural vegetation.
20.tq: Use the direct name-and-contribution recall method.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the major groups of Koeppen’s classification:
1. Group B represents dry climates in which evaporation exceeds precipitation.
2. Group C represents warm temperate climates with the coldest month between -3°C and 18°C.
3. Group D represents cold snow-forest climates with the coldest month below -3°C.
4. Group E represents polar climates with the warmest month below 10°C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: All four statements correctly state the criteria for Koeppen groups B, C, D and E.
20.tq: Check each numerical boundary before selecting the coded combination.

20.s: In Koeppen’s classification, the letter ‘H’ denotes:
20.x: H denotes a highland climate in which low temperatures are controlled mainly by altitude.
20.tq: Discriminate the exact classification letter from similar-sounding alternatives.

20.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in respect of the second letters used in Koeppen’s classification?
20.x: The second letter f indicates that there is no dry season. The letters m, w and s indicate monsoon, dry winter and dry summer respectively.
20.tq: Use the confusable-pair method for the letters w and s.

20.s: Thornthwaite first proposed his climatic classification in 1931 and revised it in:
20.x: Thornthwaite proposed the classification in 1931 and revised it in 1948.
20.tq: Use the date-pair recall method and distinguish the revision year from the original year.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with its climatic criterion in the classification table?
20.x: Group D has the coldest month below -3°C, not above 18°C. The criteria stated for Groups A, B and E are correct.
20.tq: Find the one reversed temperature criterion.

20.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Code)
a. Amw
b. As
c. BWhw
d. Dfc

List-II (Area)
i. Arunachal Pradesh
ii. Extreme western Rajasthan
iii. West coast south of Goa
iv. Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu
20.x: Amw occurs on the west coast south of Goa, As on the Coromandel coast, BWhw in extreme western Rajasthan and Dfc in Arunachal Pradesh.
20.tq: Start from the sure code-area pair and eliminate the remaining combinations.

20.s: The Koeppen code 'Aw' represents which climatic type and area in India?
o: Monsoon with dry summer; Coromandel coast
Tropical savanna; most of the Peninsular Plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer
20.x: Aw denotes tropical savanna and covers most of the Peninsular Plateau south of the Tropic of Cancer.
20.tq: Pair the code with both its exact climate meaning and area.

20.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the climatic type of Andhra Pradesh under Koeppen's classification?
o: The State is predominantly classified as Aw.
The State is predominantly classified as Cwg.
The State is predominantly classified as BWhw.
The State is predominantly classified as Dfc.
20.x: Andhra Pradesh is predominantly Aw, representing a tropical wet-and-dry or tropical savanna climate.
20.tq: Apply a broad regional classification to the State rather than a local exception.

20.s: A place where the warmest month has a temperature below 10°C is generally classified as having
20.x: A warmest-month temperature below 10°C is a defining descriptive feature of the tundra climate.
20.tq: Use the temperature threshold as the decisive classification clue.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Thornthwaite’s classification from Koeppen’s classification?
o: Thornthwaite used only natural vegetation, whereas Koeppen used only altitude.
Thornthwaite emphasised precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, whereas Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
Thornthwaite was based exclusively on pressure, whereas Koeppen was based on winds.
Both classifications used exactly the same criteria and symbols.
20.x: Thornthwaite’s scheme is based on precipitation effectiveness and thermal efficiency, including potential evapotranspiration. Koeppen used temperature, precipitation and natural vegetation.
20.tq: Identify the reversed-criteria trap in a comparison question.

20.s:
Match List-I (Koeppen code) with List-II (Area in India):

List-I
a. Amw
b. As
c. Cwg
d. BShw

List-II
i. Ganga plain
ii. North-west India
iii. West coast south of Goa
iv. Coromandel coast of Tamil Nadu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: As in APPSC-G1 2024: Amw is the west coast south of Goa, As the Coromandel coast (dry summer, winter rain), Cwg the Ganga plain (monsoon with dry winter) and BShw north-west India. The other codes swap Amw with As, Cwg with BShw, or Amw with Cwg.
20.tq: Amw west coast; As Coromandel; Cwg Ganga plain; BShw NW.

20.s: Which one of the following climatic regions is characterised by dense evergreen hardwoods such as mahogany and ebony, with rain almost every day?
20.x: The equatorial region, including the Amazon, Congo and Indonesia, has dense evergreen hardwood forests and almost daily rainfall.
20.tq: Directly link the vegetation and rainfall pattern with the climatic region.

20.s: The Llanos and Campos are principally associated with which type of natural vegetation and climate?
20.x: Llanos and Campos are tropical grasslands associated with the savanna or tropical wet-dry climate.
20.tq: Discriminate between tropical and temperate grassland categories.

20.s: The tropical monsoon region of India and South-East Asia is chiefly associated with which vegetation?
20.x: Tropical monsoon forests in India and South-East Asia include teak and sal; the trees shed their leaves during the dry season.
20.tq: Match the climatic region with its representative vegetation.

20.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
o: Mediterranean region — winter rainfall and evergreen shrubs
Taiga — deciduous trees and summer drought
20.x: The Mediterranean climate occurs mainly on western margins between 30° and 45° latitude and has winter rain with evergreen shrubs, olives and citrus.
20.tq: Find the pair containing both the correct climate and vegetation characteristics.

20.s:
Consider the following statements about temperate deciduous forests:
1. They occur in the mid-latitudes between the tropics and polar regions.
2. North-West Europe is associated with the British type of this forest.
3. Their trees generally shed leaves in autumn.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Temperate deciduous forests occur in mid-latitudes, include the British type of north-west Europe, and shed leaves in autumn.
20.tq: Combine distribution, regional subtype and seasonal adaptation.

20.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the taiga biome?
o: Tall grass and scattered acacia only
Evergreen conifers such as spruce, fir and pine
Mosses and lichens with no trees everywhere
Olives and citrus with winter rainfall
20.x: Taiga or boreal forests of northern North America and Eurasia are dominated by evergreen conifers such as spruce, fir and pine.
20.tq: Use a representative vegetation clue to identify the biome.

20.s: Which one of the following statements about the taiga biome is NOT correct?
o: It is the largest land biome.
It has the highest productivity of all forests.
It has a wide range of temperature between winter and summer.
20.x: Taiga is the largest land biome, has a wide seasonal temperature range and moderate precipitation, but it has the lowest productivity of all forests.
20.tq: Find the statement that reverses a specific comparison.

20.s: The acidic podzol soils are characteristically associated with which biome?
20.x: Taiga regions are associated with evergreen conifers and acidic podzol soils.
20.tq: Link a distinctive soil type to its biome.

20.s:
Which of the following is characteristic of the tundra biome?
1. Permafrost
2. Mosses and lichens
3. Absence of trees
4. Dense evergreen hardwood canopy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: Tundra has permafrost, mosses and lichens, and generally no trees. A dense evergreen hardwood canopy is not a tundra feature.
20.tq: Eliminate the vegetation statement belonging to another biome.

20.s: The tree line refers to the altitude or latitude beyond which:
20.x: The tree line is the altitude or latitude beyond which trees cannot grow; alpine tundra lies above it.
20.tq: Test the exact definition of a geographical term.

20.s: Which of the following regions is associated with the China-type climate?
o: Sudan belt and East Africa only
20.x: The China-type climate is associated with central and southern China, as well as areas such as the south-eastern United States, southern Brazil and eastern Australia.
20.tq: Identify the representative area from a climate classification list.

20.s: The British-type climate is characterised by which combination?
o: Westerlies, rainfall throughout the year and mild conditions
Summer drought, winter rain and evergreen shrubs
Wet summer, dry winter and tall grass
Permafrost, no trees and very low precipitation
20.x: The British type is influenced by westerlies and has rainfall throughout the year with mild conditions.
20.tq: Distinguish the British type from Mediterranean and savanna climates by rainfall seasonality.

20.s: Which one of the following statements about tropical rainforests is correct?
o: They receive less than 25 cm of rain and have a high diurnal range.
They are dominated by mosses and lichens over permafrost.
They receive approximately 50–260 inches of rain and contain dense canopies, epiphytes and lianas.
They consist mainly of grasses with very few trees.
20.x: Tropical rainforests occur in the equatorial belt, receive about 50–260 inches of rain, and have dense canopies, epiphytes and lianas.
20.tq: Use the distinctive rainfall range and structural features to identify the biome.

20.s: Tropical rainforests are notable for containing approximately what share of all known species?
20.x: Tropical rainforests contain more than half of all known species.
20.tq: Test a quantitative ecological comparison without confusing ‘more than half’ with ‘all’.

20.s:
Arrange the following climatic regions from the Equator towards the polar region, in the broad order indicated by their characteristic belts:
A. Tundra
B. Equatorial
C. Temperate deciduous
D. Tropical monsoon
Select the correct answer.
20.x: Moving broadly from the Equator towards the poles, the sequence is equatorial, tropical monsoon, temperate deciduous and tundra.
20.tq: Use latitudinal progression from the Equator towards the poles.

20.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Savanna — Sudan belt and East Africa
Taiga — northern North America and Eurasia
Tundra — central tropical Brazil and the Congo Basin
20.x: Tundra occurs mainly along Arctic coasts and above the tree line in high mountains, not in central tropical Brazil or the Congo Basin.
20.tq: Find the wrong location by comparing each biome with its climatic belt.

20.s: Hot deserts are generally concentrated between approximately
20.x: Hot deserts commonly occur between 15° and 30° north and south, especially on the western margins of continents.
20.tq: Recall the latitudinal belt associated with subtropical hot deserts.

20.s: Which combination best explains the occurrence of hot deserts on the western margins of continents?
o: Subtropical high pressure, offshore trade winds and cold currents
Polar easterlies, glaciers and high humidity
Equatorial low pressure, onshore trade winds and warm currents
Monsoon depressions, warm currents and rising air
20.x: Subtropical high pressure suppresses rainfall, offshore trade winds reduce moisture supply, and cold currents further stabilise and dry the air.
20.tq: Match the desert location with the combined pressure, wind and current conditions.

20.s: A biome is best described as which one of the following?
o: A transition zone between two adjacent ecosystems
An artificial ecosystem maintained only by human beings
A small community containing only one species
A large natural community of flora and fauna over a major habitat, shaped mainly by climate
20.x: A biome is a large natural community of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat and shaped by climate. It contains many habitats.
20.tq: Distinguish the definition of a biome from community, ecosystem and ecotone.

20.s: Anthropogenic biomes, also called anthromes, are ecological units shaped by which of the following?
o: Sustained human use such as croplands, villages and cities
20.x: Anthropogenic biomes are ecological units shaped by sustained human use and include croplands, villages and cities.
20.tq: Apply the definition to examples of human-shaped ecological units.

20.s: Alpine tundra is generally found in which situation?
o: In the humid equatorial belt below 10° latitude
Above the tree line in mountains such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps
Below the tree line in tropical lowlands
20.x: Alpine tundra occurs above the tree line in high mountain systems such as the Himalayas, Andes and Alps.
20.tq: Apply the definition of alpine tundra to altitude and location.

20.s: Mediterranean climate receives most of its rainfall during winter because
o: the subtropical high-pressure belt dominates in winter
cold ocean currents produce continuous monsoon rainfall
westerly depressions and cyclonic systems affect the region in winter
the trade winds reverse and produce convection throughout winter
20.x: In winter, the seasonal shift of pressure belts allows westerly depressions to bring cyclonic rainfall to Mediterranean regions.
20.tq: Connect the seasonal pressure-belt shift with the timing of rainfall.

20.s: Mediterranean climate is generally found between approximately
20.x: Mediterranean climate occurs mainly between 30° and 45° north and south, particularly on the western margins of continents.
20.tq: Recall both the latitude belt and the western-margin setting.

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with Mediterranean climate?
20.x: Darwin is not among the listed Mediterranean climatic locations. Mediterranean conditions occur in places such as Santiago, Cape Town and Perth.
20.tq: Find the location outside the recognised Mediterranean-climate regions.

20.s: The Mediterranean climatic region is popularly known for the cultivation of
20.x: Mediterranean regions are known as orchard lands and are associated with citrus fruits, grapes and wine production.
20.tq: Use the characteristic crop association to identify the climate.

20.s: Which grassland is found in the Eurasian region extending from Ukraine towards Central Asia?
20.x: The Steppes are the temperate grasslands of Eurasia, extending from Ukraine towards Central Asia.
20.tq: Directly match a named grassland with its continental location.

20.s: The Steppe belt is significant because it separates:
20.x: The Eurasian Steppe belt separates Cold Asia from Dry Asia.
20.tq: Test the geographical relationship associated with a named region.

20.s:
Consider the following pairs:
Grassland — Region
1. Prairies — USA and Canada
2. Pampas — Argentina and Uruguay
3. Veld — Australia
4. Canterbury — New Zealand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
20.x: Pair 1 is correct: the Prairies lie in both the USA and Canada. Pair 2 is correct: the Pampas are in Argentina and Uruguay. Pair 3 is wrong: the Veld is in South Africa; the Downs are the Australian grassland. Pair 4 is correct: Canterbury is in New Zealand. So 1, 2 and 4 only (B); A leaves out the true pair 4, while C and D include the wrong pair 3.
20.tq: Veld = South Africa, Downs = Australia; swapping these two is the usual trap.

20.s: Which one of the following is a tropical grassland rather than a temperate grassland?
20.x: Llanos is a tropical grassland of the Orinoco basin, whereas Pampas, Steppes and Veld are temperate grasslands.
20.tq: Separate the tropical category from the group of temperate grasslands.

20.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Savanna — Sudan belt and East Africa
20.x: Pampas are located in Argentina. Venezuela and Colombia are associated with the Llanos grasslands.
20.tq: Use a nearby grassland as the trap for a swapped location.

20.s: Which set of conditions is most characteristic of temperate grassland or steppe climate?
o: Rain almost every day and dense evergreen forest
Hot summers, chilly winters and 25–50 cm of rainfall
Permafrost and no trees throughout the year
Rainfall throughout the year and mild temperatures
20.x: Temperate grasslands have hot summers, chilly winters, annual rainfall of about 25–50 cm, and grasses with few trees.
20.tq: Identify a climatic region from its temperature, rainfall and vegetation profile.

20.s: Which of the following animals is associated with temperate grasslands?
o: Reindeer, musk-ox and arctic fox only
20.x: Temperate grasslands support animals such as bison, prairie dogs and antelope.
20.tq: Match characteristic fauna with the correct grassland type.

20.s: Which one of the following statements about savanna vegetation is correct?
o: It consists exclusively of mosses and lichens over permafrost.
It is dominated by spruce, fir and pine in acidic podzol soils.
It includes elephant grass, guinea grass, baobab and acacia, and is naturally fire-prone.
It is composed mainly of olives and citrus receiving winter rain.
20.x: Savanna vegetation includes tall grasses such as elephant and guinea grass, along with baobab and acacia; it is naturally prone to fire.
20.tq: Use the vegetation list and ecological adaptation to identify the savanna.

20.s: Which of the following statements about rangelands is correct?
o: They include grasslands, savannas and shrublands.
They cover less than one-tenth of Earth's land.
They occur only in the polar regions.
They consist exclusively of natural forests.
20.x: Rangelands include grasslands, savannas and shrublands and cover about half of Earth's land.
20.tq: Reject absolute and restricted descriptions in favour of the inclusive classification.

20.s: The United Nations has declared 2026 as the International Year for:
20.x: The UN declared 2026 the International Year for Rangelands and Pastoralists. Rangelands (grasslands, savannas, shrublands) cover about half of Earth's land. The other options are not the 2026 theme given in the notes.
20.tq: 2026 = Rangelands and Pastoralists.

20.s: The lowest temperature ever recorded on Earth is associated with
20.x: Vostok in Antarctica recorded the lowest known temperature, about −89.2°C. Oymyakon and Verkhoyansk are associated with the cold pole among inhabited places.
20.tq: Separate the absolute recorded extreme from the coldest inhabited locations.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly explains the exceptional rainfall of Mawsynram and Cherrapunji?
o: Funnelling of moist air and orographic lifting
Cold currents and subtropical high pressure
20.x: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji receive more than 1,100 cm of annual rainfall because moist air is funnelled and forced to rise over the terrain.
20.tq: Link the climatic extreme to the physical mechanism producing it.

20.s: The Atacama Desert is regarded as one of the driest regions of the world and is located in
o: central Australia, west of the Great Dividing Range
southern Argentina, east of the Andes
the interior of the Arabian Peninsula
northern Chile, west of the Andes
20.x: The Atacama Desert lies in northern Chile, west of the Andes, and is recognised for extreme aridity.
20.tq: Combine the climatic superlative with the correct location.

20.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Ganganagar — approximately 50°C in 1935
2. Dras — approximately −45°C in 1908
3. Ruyli, Jaisalmer — about 8.33 cm annual rainfall
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
20.x: All three pairs are correct. Ganganagar represents India’s highest noted temperature, Dras its lowest noted temperature, and Ruyli its driest location in the cited records.
20.tq: Verify each numerical place–record pair before selecting the coded combination.

20.s: The highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth, 56.7 °C (1913), is associated with:
20.x: Death Valley in California holds the record of 56.7 °C (1913); the WMO rejected Al Aziziya, Libya. Ganganagar's ~50 °C (1935) is India's highest, and the Atacama is the driest place, not the hottest.
20.tq: Hottest = Death Valley (Al Aziziya rejected).

20.s: The Bedouins are traditionally associated with which natural region and way of life?
o: Arabian and Saharan deserts and nomadism
Equatorial forests and hunting of forest animals
Central Asian steppes and settled cultivation
20.x: Bedouins are traditionally nomadic people of the hot deserts of Arabia and the Sahara.
20.tq: Match the people with both their natural region and characteristic livelihood.

20.s: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are traditionally associated with the
20.x: The Kirghiz and Kazakh peoples are associated with the grasslands and steppes of Central Asia.
20.tq: Use the natural-region association to distinguish steppe peoples from desert and tundra groups.

20.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
20.x: The Yakuts are associated with Siberia and the taiga or Arctic environment. The Tuareg are associated with the Sahara, while the Bedouin are associated with Arabia and the Sahara.
20.tq: Start from the complete three-part match and reject swapped environments.

20.s: A region has a very small annual temperature range of 2–3°C and receives rainfall in every month. Which climate does it most likely represent?
20.x: A very small annual temperature range and year-round rainfall are characteristic of the equatorial climate.
20.tq: Identify the climate from its strongest temperature-range and rainfall clues.

20.s: A region experiences a hot, wet summer followed by a long dry winter. This description most closely corresponds to
20.x: Hot wet summers and long dry winters are characteristic of savanna or monsoon climatic conditions.
20.tq: Distinguish summer-rain climates from the winter-rain Mediterranean type.

20.s: A climate with very high temperatures, a very large daily range and annual rainfall below 25 cm is characteristic of
20.x: Extreme heat, a large diurnal temperature range and rainfall below 25 cm indicate a hot desert climate.
20.tq: Combine rainfall amount with daily temperature range to identify the desert type.

20.s: Which climatic description correctly represents the taiga climate of Siberia?
o: Warm dry summer and mild wet winter
Long severe winter, short cool summer and very large annual range
Warmest month below 10°C with no seasonal contrast
Very small annual temperature range and rainfall every month
20.x: The taiga climate has a long severe winter, a short cool summer and a very large annual temperature range.
20.tq: Select the description containing the decisive seasonal-range features of taiga.

20.s:
Match List-I (People) with List-II (Natural region):

List-I
a. Masai
b. Pygmies
c. Bushmen (San)
d. Inuit

List-II
i. Kalahari hot desert
ii. Arctic tundra
iii. Savanna of Kenya and Tanzania
iv. Equatorial forest of the Congo basin

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
20.x: The Masai are herders of the Kenya-Tanzania savanna, the Pygmies hunter-gatherers of the Congo equatorial forest, the Bushmen (San) live in the Kalahari desert, and the Inuit in the Arctic tundra. The other codes swap Masai with Pygmies, Bushmen with Inuit, or Masai with Bushmen.
20.tq: Masai-savanna; Pygmies-Congo; San-Kalahari; Inuit-tundra.

20.s: Magnetic minerals preserved in the sediments of Bakhira Lake are significant because they provide a record of Indian monsoon variability extending approximately:
20.x: Magnetic minerals in Bakhira Lake sediments provide an approximately 25,000-year record of Indian monsoon variability.
20.tq: Use the distinctive large-number recall technique.

20.s: Bakhira Lake, associated with the palaeoclimatic record of Indian monsoon variability, is located in:
20.x: Bakhira Lake is in Uttar Pradesh, and its sediments preserve the long-term monsoon record.
20.tq: Match the named geographical feature with its state.

20.s: Which of the following statements about projected coastal climatic conditions is correct?
o: About 40 coastal districts may warm by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu receiving excess southwest-monsoon rain.
About 15 coastal districts may cool by over 1°C by 2040, with Andhra Pradesh receiving deficient monsoon rain.
All coastal districts are projected to warm by exactly 1°C by 2040.
Only inland districts of Andhra Pradesh are projected to experience excess southwest-monsoon rain.
20.x: The projection concerns about 40 coastal districts warming by more than 1°C by 2040, while Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are expected to receive excess southwest-monsoon rain.
20.tq: Reject extreme words such as ‘all’ and ‘exactly’ while retaining the precise projection.

20.s: Which statement correctly describes the geographical and climatic setting of Andhra Pradesh?
o: It lies between 19°07′ N and 25°41′ N and is classified as E/ET.
It lies between 8°41′ N and 15°07′ N and is classified as Amw.
It lies entirely north of 20° N and is classified as BWhw.
It lies between 12°41′ N and 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, or tropical wet and dry climate.
20.x: Andhra Pradesh extends from 12°41′ N to 19°07′ N and is classified as Aw, representing a tropical wet and dry climate.
20.tq: Combine latitude limits with the correct Koeppen code and reject reversed ranges.

20.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four climatic regions identified in Andhra Pradesh?
20.x: The four regions are humid coastal, deltaic, semi-arid Rayalaseema and hill micro-climates. Ladakh is not an Andhra Pradesh climatic region.
20.tq: Find the geographically misplaced regional description.

20.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the number of agro-climatic zones in Andhra Pradesh and India?
o: Andhra Pradesh has fifteen, while India has six.
Andhra Pradesh has four, while India has fifteen.
Andhra Pradesh has six, while India has fifteen.
Both Andhra Pradesh and India have seven.
20.x: The current figures stated are six agro-climatic zones for Andhra Pradesh and fifteen for India.
20.tq: Use the direction of comparison to avoid interchanging state and national figures.

20.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the global ocean climate in 2025:
1. Oceans held more than 90% of the excess heat.
2. Approximately 90% of the ocean surface experienced marine heatwaves.
3. Less than 10% of the excess heat was held by the oceans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
20.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the oceans held more than 90%, not less than 10%, of the excess heat.
20.tq: Spot the numerical reversal in the false statement.

21.s: Which of the following correctly represents the recent global temperature ranking?
o: 2019 was the hottest year globally, while 2000–2010 comprise the eleven warmest years.
2024 was the hottest year on record, while 2015–2025 comprise the eleven warmest years.
2025 was the hottest year on record and 2024 was the second warmest.
Only the years after 2020 entered the list of the eleven warmest years.
21.x: 2024 was the hottest year on record, and the period 2015–2025 contains the eleven warmest years in the record.
21.tq: Check the ranking and the complete year range rather than accepting a partly familiar claim.

21.s:
With reference to global temperature records, consider the following statements:
1. The temperature in 2024 was about 1.55°C above the pre-industrial level.
2. The temperature in 2025 was approximately 1.43°C above the pre-industrial level.
3. 2025 was the warmest La Niña year on record.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct: 2024 was about 1.55°C above the pre-industrial level, 2025 about 1.43°C, and 2025 was the warmest La Niña year recorded.
21.tq: Verify each numerical and ranking statement before selecting the complete combination.

21.s: Which of the following correctly compares warming in India with warming over global land areas?
o: India has warmed about 1.59°C since 1900, compared with about 0.7°C for global land.
India has experienced cooling since 1900, while global land has warmed about 0.7°C.
India has warmed about 0.7°C since 1900, compared with about 1.59°C for global land.
Both India and global land have warmed exactly 2°C since 1900.
21.x: India has warmed approximately 0.7°C since 1900, whereas global land areas have warmed about 1.59°C.
21.tq: Watch for reversal of the two values in a comparison question.

21.s: The Gangotri Glacier has retreated by approximately how much since 1935?
21.x: Gangotri Glacier has retreated approximately 1,700 metres since 1935, with global warming identified as the cause of its melting.
21.tq: Use the exact distance and reference year together to avoid range-based guessing.

21.s: According to the global temperature record (as of February 2026), the year 2019 ranks as the:
21.x: 2019 is the seventh warmest year on record (APPSC GS 2019 asked it). 2024 is the hottest; 2025 is second or third warmest; 2019 lies inside the 2015-2025 run of the eleven warmest years, so it cannot be the coldest of all years and is not the hottest or second warmest.
21.tq: 2024 hottest; 2019 seventh.

21.s:
With reference to evidence of global warming, consider the following statements:
1. Global sea level has risen by about 11 cm since 1993.
2. According to WMO 2025, Arctic sea ice is near record lows.
3. According to WMO 2025, Antarctic sea ice is at its highest extent on record.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: sea level is up about 11 cm since 1993. Statement 2 is correct: WMO 2025 puts Arctic sea ice near record lows. Statement 3 is wrong: Antarctic sea ice was the 3rd lowest, not the highest. So 1 and 2 only; option A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
21.tq: Both poles low: Arctic near record low, Antarctic 3rd lowest.

21.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Precession — wobble of the rotational axis
21.x: Precession refers to the wobble of Earth’s axis. Eccentricity concerns orbital shape and obliquity concerns axial tilt.
21.tq: Separate the three easily confusable components of the Milankovitch cycles.

21.s: The Little Ice Age is generally placed approximately between:
21.x: The Little Ice Age is placed approximately in the period 1500–1850.
21.tq: Use the historical range as the discriminator among overlapping climate periods.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about solar output and recent global warming:
1. Satellite observations since 1978 show no net increase in solar output.
2. Recent warming can therefore not be explained by an increasing solar output.
3. Satellite observations establish that solar output has continuously declined since 1978.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The evidence indicates no net increase, not a continuous decline, in solar output since 1978.
21.tq: Reject the stronger but unsupported word ‘continuously’ in the third statement.

21.s:
Which of the following natural factors are identified as possible influences on climate?
1. Volcanic activity
2. Continental drift
3. Ocean currents
4. Fertiliser use
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
21.x: Volcanic activity, continental drift and ocean currents are natural climate influences. Fertiliser use is an anthropogenic cause associated with nitrous oxide emissions.
21.tq: Classify each factor as natural or human-induced before using the code.

21.s: Volcanic eruptions can produce a short-term cooling effect mainly because:
o: Volcanic gases permanently remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Sulphur dioxide and ash form aerosols that reflect sunlight
Volcanic dust increases the absorption of solar radiation by the surface
Lava directly lowers ocean temperatures worldwide
21.x: Sulphur dioxide and ash generate cooling aerosols that reflect incoming sunlight.
21.tq: Connect the natural event with its atmospheric mechanism and radiative effect.

21.s:
With reference to the IPCC, consider the following statements:
1. It has 195 members.
2. It conducts original climate research as its principal activity.
3. It assesses the existing scientific literature on climate change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: The IPCC has 195 members and assesses available scientific literature. It does not conduct research of its own as its principal activity.
21.tq: Separate the assessment function from the research function before selecting the coded combination.

21.s: The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to the IPCC in 2007 was shared with which of the following persons?
21.x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.
21.tq: Test the person-organisation association directly, using nearby climate personalities as distractors.

21.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (IPCC Working Group)
A. Working Group I
B. Working Group II
C. Working Group III

List-II (Subject)
1. Mitigation
2. Physical science basis
3. Impacts, adaptation and vulnerability
21.x: Working Group I deals with the physical science basis, Working Group II with impacts, adaptation and vulnerability, and Working Group III with mitigation.
21.tq: Start from the sure pair: Working Group I is associated with the physical science basis.

21.s:
Consider the following statements about the IPCC Special Report on Global Warming of 1.5°C (SR1.5):
1. It was published in 2018.
2. It stated that, at the current rate, warming is likely to reach 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052.
3. It stated that limiting warming to 1.5°C requires global CO2 emissions to fall about 45% from 2010 levels by 2050.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
21.x: Statement 1 is correct: SR1.5 came out in 2018. Statement 2 is correct: it put the 1.5°C crossing between 2030 and 2052 at the current rate. Statement 3 is wrong: the 45% cut from 2010 levels is needed by 2030; 2050 is the date for net zero. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses the true statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
21.tq: SR1.5: 45% cut by 2030, net zero around 2050 — watch for the two dates being swapped.

21.s: In the context of climate policy, 'net zero' means that:
o: All greenhouse-gas emissions are stopped permanently.
Natural emissions are completely eliminated from the atmosphere.
Human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through sinks or capture.
Only carbon dioxide emissions are reduced to zero without removals.
21.x: Net zero is achieved when human-caused emissions are balanced by removals through natural sinks or technological capture, resulting in zero net addition.
21.tq: Apply the definition to distinguish net emissions from gross emissions.

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) Synthesis Report:
1. It was released on 20 March 2023.
2. Warming during 2011–2020 had already reached about 1.1°C.
3. It indicated that 1.5°C warming is likely to be breached in the early 2030s.
4. It stated that emissions may peak after 2035 without affecting the mid-century net-zero objective.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. AR6 indicated that emissions must peak before 2025; therefore statement 4 is incorrect.
21.tq: Find the single time-related reversal in the final statement.

21.s: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 projects that continuation of current policies would result in global warming of approximately:
21.x: The UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025 estimates approximately 2.8°C of warming under current policies.
21.tq: Use the distinctive report-specific figure rather than the familiar 1.5°C or 2°C targets.

21.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2025:
1. Emissions must fall by 35% from 2019 levels by 2035 to limit warming to 2°C.
2. Emissions must fall by 55% from 2019 levels by 2035 to limit warming to 1.5°C.
3. An overshoot of 1.5°C is described as very likely during this decade.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
21.x: All three statements are correct: the stated reductions are 35% for the 2°C pathway and 55% for the 1.5°C pathway, while a 1.5°C overshoot is considered very likely this decade.
21.tq: Check each numerical statement separately before selecting the coded combination.

21.s: The WMO publication titled State of the Global Climate 2025 was released on:
21.x: The report was released on World Meteorological Day, 23 March 2026.
21.tq: Link the named international report with its stated release occasion and date.

21.s: Which phrase was associated with the climate indicators in the WMO State of the Global Climate 2025 report?
21.x: The report described the climate indicators as “flashing red.”
21.tq: Test the exact official expression rather than a general paraphrase.

21.s: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2021 was awarded in part to which scientists for the physical modelling of Earth's climate?
21.x: Syukuro Manabe and Klaus Hasselmann shared the 2021 Physics Nobel (with Giorgio Parisi) for physical modelling of Earth's climate. Al Gore shared the 2007 Peace Prize with the IPCC, and Pachauri chaired the IPCC; Hansen, Mann, Arrhenius and Keeling are climate scientists who did not receive this prize.
21.tq: 2021 Physics = Manabe + Hasselmann (+ Parisi).

21.s:
Which of the following is a direct physical cause of sea-level rise associated with climate change?
1. Thermal expansion of seawater
2. Melting of ice
3. Increased snow albedo
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
21.x: Sea-level rise results from thermal expansion of seawater and melting of ice. Increased snow albedo would reflect more radiation and is not a cause of sea-level rise.
21.tq: Identify the two established mechanisms and reject the reversed albedo effect.

21.s: Which pair of South Pacific islets was reported to have been submerged in 1999?
21.x: The uninhabited South Pacific islets Tebua Tarawa and Abanuea were reported to have been submerged in 1999. Kiribati and Tuvalu are countries at risk from sea-level rise.
21.tq: Distinguish submerged islets from countries identified as being at risk.

21.s: Which one of the following statements about climate-related coral bleaching is correct?
o: Large-scale warm-water reef collapse begins only above 3°C, and reefs recover within two years.
Reefs recover immediately once the atmospheric temperature falls for one season.
The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and reefs need more than 15 years to recover.
Coral reefs are unaffected by warming below 4°C.
21.x: The approximately 1.2°C threshold for large-scale warm-water reef collapse has already been crossed, and coral reefs require more than 15 years to recover.
21.tq: Combine the threshold and recovery-period figures while rejecting exaggerated alternatives.

21.s: Which one of the following statements regarding ocean and mountain ecosystem impacts is correct?
o: Ocean acidity has increased by about 30% since the Industrial Revolution, and up to 25% of mountain species may face extinction.
Ocean acidity has fallen by 30% since the Industrial Revolution, while no mountain species face extinction risk.
Ocean acidity has remained unchanged, while exactly 50% of mountain species face extinction.
Ocean acidity has increased by 3%, and mountain species are unaffected because of altitude.
21.x: Ocean acidity has increased by about 30% since the Industrial Revolution, and AR6 estimates that up to 25% of mountain species may face extinction.
21.tq: Watch for reversed trends and altered percentages in the paired-impact statement.

21.s: Warmer and wetter conditions can widen the geographical range of which category of diseases?
o: Only genetic disorders such as haemophilia
Only deficiency diseases such as scurvy
Non-infectious diseases exclusively caused by ageing
Vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue
21.x: Warmer and wetter conditions can expand the range of vectors and thereby increase the spread of diseases such as malaria and dengue.
21.tq: Link the environmental change to the disease category and examples it affects.

21.s: Which of the following statements regarding climate tipping points is correct?
o: The 1.2°C threshold for warm-water coral reef collapse has already been crossed, while beyond about 2°C parts of the Amazon may turn into savanna.
Coral reef collapse begins only after 4°C warming, while the Amazon becomes a carbon sink beyond 2°C.
The Amazon turns into savanna below 1°C, while coral reefs remain unaffected above 2°C.
Both thresholds are unrelated to ecosystem changes and refer only to atmospheric pressure.
21.x: The 1.2°C threshold for warm-water coral reef collapse has already been crossed. Beyond about 2°C, parts of the Amazon could shift towards savanna and become a carbon source.
21.tq: Compare the two ecosystem thresholds and their distinct consequences.

21.s: According to WMO's State of the Global Climate 2025, extreme weather in India in 2025 caused approximately:
o: 4,419 deaths and damage to 17.4 million ha of crops
441 deaths and damage to 1.74 million ha of crops
44,190 deaths and damage to 174 million ha of crops
21.x: WMO 2025 recorded about 4,419 deaths and 17.4 million ha of crops damaged by extreme weather in India in 2025. Options B and C shift both figures by a factor of ten, and D wrongly denies the crop damage.
21.tq: India 2025: 4,419 deaths, 17.4 Mha crops.

21.s: Stratospheric aerosol injection is proposed as a form of geoengineering because it seeks to:
o: Increase the absorption of sunlight by the stratosphere
Reflect sunlight by forming sulphuric-acid aerosols
Increase the concentration of greenhouse gases in the upper atmosphere
Remove all water vapour from the troposphere
21.x: In this proposal, sulphur dioxide forms sulphuric-acid aerosols that reflect sunlight, imitating the cooling effect of volcanic eruptions.
21.tq: Identify the intended physical process rather than the name of the intervention alone.

21.s: In the context of stratospheric aerosol injection, the term ‘termination shock’ refers to:
o: Rapid warming if aerosol injection is abruptly stopped
The destruction of the ozone layer by volcanic ash alone
A sudden cooling caused by stopping fossil fuel use
The permanent cessation of solar radiation
21.x: Termination shock denotes rapid warming that could occur if the cooling intervention were stopped suddenly.
21.tq: Discriminate between the proposed intervention and the risk created by terminating it.

21.s: Cirrus cloud thinning is intended to cool the Earth by:
o: Seeding high cirrus clouds so that more outgoing heat escapes
Spraying sea salt into low marine clouds
Making high cirrus clouds thicker so that they reflect more sunlight
Increasing the amount of sulphur dioxide in volcanic plumes
21.x: Cirrus cloud thinning seeks to reduce the insulating effect of high cirrus clouds and allow more outgoing heat to escape.
21.tq: Match the geoengineering proposal with the direction of its radiative effect.

21.s: Marine cloud brightening involves the use of sea-salt spray primarily to:
o: Absorb infrared radiation in the stratosphere
Suppress all forms of cloud formation
Reduce the salinity of the surface ocean
Act as cloud condensation nuclei and brighten clouds
21.x: Sea-salt spray can act as cloud condensation nuclei, potentially making marine clouds brighter.
21.tq: Identify the material used and its immediate atmospheric function.

21.s: COP31 is scheduled to meet in which country and month?
21.x: COP31 is scheduled to meet in Türkiye in November 2026.
21.tq: Combine the host location and month to avoid confusing the event with another climate meeting.

21.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the CMIP7 scenarios mentioned in current climate assessments?
o: They place the world below 1°C by 2100 under current policies.
They exclude all scenarios involving human emissions and project no warming.
They retain SSP5-8.5 as the only scenario and project 1.5°C by 2100.
They drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 scenario and place the world near 2.8°C by 2100.
21.x: The CMIP7 scenarios drop the worst-case SSP5-8.5 pathway and place projected warming near 2.8°C by 2100.
21.tq: Test both parts of a current-affairs statement: the scenario change and the projected temperature.

21.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with climate-related concerns in Andhra Pradesh?
21.x: Palnadu, Kurnool and Anantapur are identified in connection with heatwaves. Uppada in the Kakinada region is associated with coastal erosion.
21.tq: Match each environmental hazard with its geographical locations before comparing the options.

21.s: APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under which Sustainable Development Goal?
21.x: APSES 2024–25 tracks climate action under SDG 13.
21.tq: Recall the exact SDG number associated with climate action.

22.s: Which is the correct order of the oceans from largest to smallest by area?
22.x: The order by area is Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic; the Arctic Ocean is the smallest.
22.tq: Recall the complete size ranking and use the smallest ocean as a final check.

22.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Oceans cover approximately 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface.
2. Oceans contain approximately 97 per cent of Earth's water.
3. Oceans constitute the largest part of the hydrosphere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Oceans cover about 70–71 per cent of Earth's surface, contain about 97 per cent of its water, and form the largest component of the hydrosphere.
22.tq: Verify whether all quantitative and comparative statements refer consistently to oceans.

22.s: According to the stated broad division of Earth's water, approximately what proportions are represented by ice and usable fresh water, respectively?
o: About 1 per cent and about 2 per cent
About 70 per cent and about 27 per cent
About 2 per cent and about 1 per cent
About 97 per cent and about 2 per cent
22.x: About 2 per cent of Earth's water is represented as ice and about 1 per cent as usable fresh water in the stated broad division.
22.tq: Keep the small percentages distinct from the approximately 97 per cent oceanic share.

22.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the distribution of fresh water among its major stores?
o: Lakes and rivers together far exceed groundwater.
Groundwater far exceeds the water stored in lakes and rivers.
Groundwater, lakes and rivers contain equal amounts of fresh water.
Rivers contain nearly all usable fresh water, whereas groundwater is negligible.
22.x: Groundwater far exceeds the amount of fresh water stored in lakes and rivers.
22.tq: Identify the correct comparative relationship rather than choosing an absolute claim.

22.s: One fathom is equal to:
22.x: A fathom is a unit of depth equal to 6 feet, or approximately 1.83 metres.
22.tq: Distinguish the exact unit conversion from nearby length values.

22.s: Which one of the following correctly explains echo sounding or sonar as a method of determining ocean depth?
o: Depth is calculated by dividing the speed of sound by the full round-trip time.
Depth is obtained by multiplying the speed of sound in water by half the round-trip time of the echo.
Depth is calculated from the salinity and temperature of surface water alone.
Depth is measured by observing the colour of the sea surface.
22.x: Echo sounding measures the time taken by a sound pulse to travel to the sea floor and return; depth equals speed multiplied by half the round-trip time.
22.tq: Apply the physical principle and identify why the return journey is divided by two.

22.s: Isobaths are lines joining places having equal:
22.x: Isobaths join points of equal depth, especially on maps of submerged relief.
22.tq: Separate depth contours from lines representing equal pressure, temperature or salinity.

22.s: A hypsometric curve represents the:
o: Share of Earth's surface occurring at different land heights and sea depths
Variation of salinity with distance from the coast
Distribution of marine deposits according to grain size
Variation of ocean currents with latitude
22.x: A hypsometric curve shows the proportion of Earth's surface at different elevations on land and depths in the sea.
22.tq: Identify the graph by its complete subject coverage—both land heights and sea depths.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about CTD instruments:
1. They measure conductivity, which is related to salinity.
2. They measure temperature.
3. They measure depth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: CTD instruments measure conductivity, temperature and depth; conductivity is used to determine salinity.
22.tq: Check all three components of the standard CTD abbreviation and instrument function.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about the mesopelagic zone of the ocean:
1. It extends from about 200 m to 1,000 m depth.
2. It is popularly called the 'twilight zone'.
3. It is characterised mainly by coral reefs and mangroves.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: the mesopelagic zone lies at about 200-1,000 m. Statement 2 is correct: it is called the twilight zone. Statement 3 is wrong: its typical life is lanternfishes and deep-sea shrimps, and it drives the biological carbon pump; coral reefs and mangroves are shallow-water features. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
22.tq: Mesopelagic = 200-1,000 m = twilight zone = lanternfishes, carbon pump.

22.s: The measurement of ocean depth and the study and mapping of the sea floor is called:
22.x: Bathymetry is the measuring of ocean depth and the study and mapping of the sea floor (APPSC GS 2018). Hypsometry relates to the share of surface at each height and depth (hypsometric curve); 'isobathymetry of salinity' is not a term (isobaths join equal depths, not salinity); stratigraphy studies rock layers.
22.tq: Bathy = depth; bathymetry maps the sea floor.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about the margins of the ocean floor:
1. The continental shelf generally extends to a depth of about 200 m.
2. The continental shelf is a gently sloping, submerged prolongation of the continent.
3. The continental rise is the steep drop from the shelf edge towards the deep floor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
22.x: Statement 1 is correct: the shelf reaches about 200 m. Statement 2 is correct: it is the gently sloping, shallowest submerged edge of the continent. Statement 3 is wrong: the steep drop from the shelf edge is the continental slope; the continental rise is an apron of sediment at the foot of the slope. So 1 and 2 only (B); A misses statement 2, and C and D include the false statement 3.
22.tq: Shelf (gentle, to 200 m) → slope (steep, canyons) → rise (sediment apron) → abyssal plain.

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the continental shelf:
1. It contains some of the richest fishing grounds.
2. It is an important zone for oil and natural gas resources.
3. It is the deepest and steepest part of the ocean floor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: The continental shelf is important for fisheries, oil and gas. It is not the deepest and steepest part of the ocean floor; that description relates to oceanic deeps and trenches.
22.tq: Find the statement that reverses the comparison between the shallow shelf and the deepest relief.

22.s:
Arrange the following ocean-floor divisions in descending order of their usual depth:
A. Continental shelf
B. Continental slope
C. Deep-sea plain
D. Oceanic deeps
Select the correct sequence.
22.x: Oceanic deeps are deepest, followed by deep-sea plains, continental slopes and continental shelves.
22.tq: Apply the depth sequence from the continental margin towards the deepest oceanic relief.

22.s: Which one of the following statements about the deep-sea or abyssal plain is correct?
o: It is generally confined to the first 200 metres below sea level.
It forms the flattest and smoothest extensive surface on the Earth's surface.
It is the steepest section between the shelf and the continental rise.
It consists exclusively of active volcanoes and earthquake zones.
22.x: The deep-sea plain, generally about 3,000–6,000 metres deep, is the flattest and smoothest extensive surface on Earth and is the most extensive part of the ocean floor.
22.tq: Reject extreme words such as ‘exclusively’ and identify the defining comparison.

22.s: Polymetallic nodules are particularly associated with which part of the ocean floor?
22.x: Polymetallic nodules occur on the deep-sea plains.
22.tq: Link a resource to its characteristic ocean-floor environment.

22.s:
With reference to oceanic deeps and trenches, consider the following statements:
1. They are generally long, narrow and steep-sided.
2. They are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
3. They occur mostly in the Pacific Ocean.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Oceanic deeps or trenches are long, narrow and steep-sided, commonly occur at plate-convergence zones, and are associated with volcanoes and strong earthquakes. Most are located in the Pacific Ocean.
22.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only when each characteristic belongs to the same relief feature.

22.s: The deep sea below about 200 metres is described as the:
22.x: The deep sea below 200 metres is described as the oldest and largest biome, occupying about 90–95 per cent of Earth's habitable space.
22.tq: Pair the numerical extent with the correct superlative description.

22.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Ocean-floor feature)
a. Continental shelf
b. Continental slope
c. Deep-sea plain
d. Oceanic deeps

List-II (Characteristic)
i. Active volcanoes and strong earthquakes
ii. Canyons and trenches
iii. Rich fishing grounds and oil and gas
iv. Flattest and smoothest extensive surface

Codes:
22.x: The continental shelf is rich in fisheries and hydrocarbons; the slope has canyons and trenches; the deep-sea plain is the flattest surface; and oceanic deeps are associated with volcanoes and earthquakes.
22.tq: Start from the sure pair—shelf with fishing grounds and oil—and eliminate incompatible codes.

22.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the continental shelf along the Indian coast?
o: It is broad along the east coast and narrow off Gujarat.
It is uniformly broad along both the eastern and western coasts.
It is broadest off Gujarat and parts of Maharashtra and narrow along the eastern coast.
It is absent off the western coast because of deep ocean trenches.
22.x: India's continental shelf is broadest off Gujarat and parts of Maharashtra, while it is relatively narrow along the east coast.
22.tq: Use the east-versus-west comparison instead of treating the coastline as uniform.

22.s: The Mumbai High oil field is situated on:
o: The continental slope off the Bay of Bengal
22.x: Mumbai High lies on the wide western continental shelf, particularly in the Gujarat-Mumbai sector.
22.tq: Associate the resource location with the correct coastal shelf sector.

22.s: Under the Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976, minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ are vested in the:
22.x: The Constitution (Fortieth Amendment) Act, 1976 vests minerals of the continental shelf and the EEZ in the Union.
22.tq: Apply the authority-identification method to a constitutional resource provision.

22.s: Which of the following is NOT a resource associated with India's continental shelf?
o: Coal deposits of the Himalayan ranges
22.x: Oil and gas, placer minerals and fisheries are resources associated with the continental shelf. Himalayan coal deposits are not listed as a shelf resource.
22.tq: Find the geographically unrelated resource among shelf-based resources.

22.s: In 2025, India added approximately how much area in the central Arabian Sea to its extended-shelf claim before the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf?
22.x: In 2025, India added about 10,000 square kilometres in the central Arabian Sea to its extended-shelf claim before the UN CLCS.
22.tq: Separate the newly added claim from the much larger total EEZ area.

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding guyots:
1. A guyot is a flat-topped seamount.
2. Its top is planed by waves before the feature sinks below the sea surface.
3. It is a ring-shaped coral reef around a central lagoon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A ring-shaped coral reef around a central lagoon is an atoll, not a guyot.
22.tq: Separate the correct statements from a swapped definition of an atoll.

22.s: An atoll is best described as a:
o: Ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef enclosing a central lagoon
Deep gorge cut across the continental slope
Flat-topped submarine mountain formed only by tectonic uplift
Submarine volcanic peak with a pointed summit
22.x: An atoll is a ring- or horseshoe-shaped coral reef surrounding a central lagoon. Lakshadweep and Maldives provide examples.
22.tq: Apply the characteristic-shape clue to identify the landform.

22.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Submarine canyon — Deep, steep-sided valley cut across the shelf and slope
Guyot — Coral reef surrounding a lagoon
Atoll — Flat-topped seamount planed by waves
Seamount — Valley formed off a river mouth
22.x: A submarine canyon is a deep, steep-sided valley that cuts across the continental shelf and slope, often near river mouths.
22.tq: Start with the sure definition and eliminate the options with swapped landforms.

22.s: The Mahadevan Canyon, mentioned in relation to submarine canyons, is located off the coast of:
22.x: Mahadevan Canyon is a submarine canyon located off Visakhapatnam.
22.tq: Test the location attached to a named geographical feature.

22.s: Which one of the following was declared a critical habitat by CMS COP15?
22.x: CMS COP15 declared seamounts to be critical habitat.
22.tq: Use the named-organisation and feature association to avoid a location-based distractor.

22.s: Which one of the following best describes a seamount?
o: A flat-topped submarine mountain planed by waves
A submarine volcanic mountain that does not reach the sea surface
A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon
A deep, steep-sided valley cut across the continental slope
22.x: A seamount is an undersea volcanic mountain or peak that does not reach the surface; seamounts carry cobalt-rich crusts. A flat-topped, wave-planed seamount is a guyot; a ring reef around a lagoon is an atoll; a steep valley across the shelf and slope is a submarine canyon.
22.tq: Seamount pointed and submerged; guyot flat-topped.

22.s: Trenches in the ocean floor primarily mark:
o: Locations where ocean water freezes permanently
The margins of stable continental interiors
Zones where one tectonic plate dives beneath another
22.x: Oceanic trenches commonly occur at subduction zones, where one plate descends beneath another.
22.tq: Apply the landform-process relationship rather than recalling only a name.

22.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
22.x: The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean. The Mariana, South Sandwich and Sunda trenches belong to the Pacific, Southern and Indian Oceans respectively.
22.tq: Use ocean-wise elimination of wrongly paired trenches.

22.s: The deepest point on Earth, the Challenger Deep, is located in the:
22.x: The Challenger Deep lies in the Mariana Trench in the Pacific Ocean and is about 11 km deep.
22.tq: Match the superlative with its exact geographical feature.

22.s: The Tonga and Kermadec trenches are situated in the:
22.x: Both the Tonga and Kermadec trenches occur in the south-western Pacific Ocean.
22.tq: Discriminate between nearby trench groups by their oceanic sector.

22.s: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is characterised by which one of the following features?
o: It is S-shaped, with Iceland and the Azores rising above it.
It is a straight ridge extending only along the eastern Pacific.
It lies south of Iceland and carries transatlantic cables.
It is situated off Namibia in the South Atlantic.
22.x: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is S-shaped, and Iceland and the Azores rise above parts of it. The other descriptions refer to different features.
22.tq: Use the distinctive shape and associated islands as identifying clues.

22.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Cocos Ridge — East Pacific, off Central America
Walvis Ridge — South Atlantic, off Namibia
Carlsberg Ridge — South Atlantic, off Namibia
22.x: The Carlsberg Ridge is located in the north-western Indian Ocean, in the Arabian Sea. The Walvis Ridge is the feature off Namibia.
22.tq: Find the swapped location among otherwise familiar ridge-ocean pairs.

22.s: The Telegraph Plateau is located in the North Atlantic, south of Iceland, and is associated with:
o: The deepest point of the Atlantic Ocean
22.x: The Telegraph Plateau lies south of Iceland in the North Atlantic and was used as a route for transatlantic cables.
22.tq: Link a geographical feature with its distinctive human-use association.

22.s: India sought exploration rights in 2024 in respect of the:
22.x: India sought exploration rights in the Carlsberg Ridge in 2024.
22.tq: Connect the policy action with the correct marine geographical feature.

22.s:
With reference to the floor of the Indian Ocean, consider the following statements:
1. The Sunda (Java) Trench is the deepest trench of the Indian Ocean.
2. The Ninety East Ridge runs along about 90 degrees East longitude.
3. India's application for the Afanasy-Nikitin Seamount is contested by Sri Lanka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: All three are correct: the Sunda (Java) Trench is the Indian Ocean's deepest trench, the Ninety East Ridge runs along 90 degrees E, and India's claim to the Afanasy-Nikitin Seamount is contested by Sri Lanka. Options A, B and C each leave out one true statement.
22.tq: Indian Ocean: Sunda Trench deepest; Ninety East Ridge on 90 deg E.

22.s:
Consider the following statements about terrigenous deposits:
1. They may include gravel, sand, silt and mud.
2. Their coarseness generally decreases away from the shore.
3. They become coarser as the distance from the shore increases.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
22.x: Terrigenous material may consist of gravel, sand, silt and mud. Coarser material is deposited near the coast, while finer material settles farther offshore; therefore statement 3 is false.
22.tq: Spot the reversed trend in a comparison statement about distance from the coast.

22.s: Which one of the following is NOT a pelagic deposit?
22.x: Calcareous ooze, siliceous ooze and red clay are pelagic deposits. Coastal gravel is a land-derived terrigenous deposit.
22.tq: Find the exception by separating deep-sea deposits from coarse coastal material.

22.s: Calcareous ooze is primarily composed of:
o: Fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust alone
Gravel and sand transported from continental rivers
Silica skeletons of diatoms and radiolarians
Lime shells of tiny organisms such as globigerina and pteropods
22.x: Calcareous ooze consists mainly of the lime shells of tiny organisms, including globigerina and pteropods.
22.tq: Match each ooze type with its distinctive biological composition.

22.s: Which one of the following statements about red clay is correct?
o: It is restricted to river mouths and estuaries.
It is the most widespread deep-sea deposit and is largest in the deep Pacific.
It is formed exclusively from lime shells in warm shallow seas.
It occurs only on continental shelves and consists mainly of gravel.
22.x: Red clay consists of fine inorganic clay and volcanic dust. It is the most widespread deep-sea deposit and is particularly extensive in the deep Pacific.
22.tq: Use the superlative and location together to identify the correct deposit.

22.s: Terrigenous deposits derived from the land are laid down mainly on the:
22.x: Terrigenous deposits (gravel, sand, silt, mud from land) settle mainly on the continental shelves and slopes (APPSC G1 2024, statement I correct). Deep-sea plains and deeps, including trench floors, are covered by pelagic oozes and red clay; mid-ocean ridges are far from land-derived supply.
22.tq: Terrigenous = shelf/slope; pelagic = deep plains.

22.s: Which one of the following statements best explains the temperature contrast between the western and eastern sides of tropical oceans?
o: The western side is warmer because warm currents generally flow along the eastern coasts of continents, whereas the eastern side is cooled by cold currents and upwelling along western continental coasts.
The western side is cooler because cold currents flow along the eastern coasts of continents.
The eastern side is warmer because upwelling brings warm deep water to the surface.
Both sides have the same temperature because ocean currents do not affect tropical waters.
22.x: In the tropics, the western side of an ocean is warmer because warm currents flow along the eastern coasts of continents. The eastern side is cooler due to cold currents and upwelling along western continental coasts.
22.tq: Use the reversed coast and current relationships as the principal trap.

22.s: The higher-latitude reversal of the usual tropical ocean-temperature pattern is associated with the:
22.x: At higher latitudes, the usual tropical west–east temperature contrast is reversed, a pattern associated with the North Atlantic Drift.
22.tq: Match the exceptional higher-latitude pattern with its named current.

22.s: Oceans absorb approximately what proportion of the excess heat associated with current global warming?
22.x: Oceans take up more than 90% of the excess heat. Ocean heat content reached a record in 2025, increasing by 23 zettajoules.
22.tq: Use the magnitude distinction between a minor and overwhelming share.

22.s: A marine heatwave is conventionally identified when sea-surface temperature remains approximately how much above average for at least five days?
22.x: A marine heatwave is defined here as sea-surface temperature about 3–4°C above average for at least five days.
22.tq: Identify the event using both its temperature threshold and duration.

22.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the temperature of ocean water:
1. Surface temperature generally falls from the equator towards the poles.
2. Northern Hemisphere oceans are generally warmer than Southern Hemisphere oceans.
3. Greater land area in the Northern Hemisphere contributes to this temperature difference.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
