38.tq: Recall the location linked with a distinctive historical temperature record.

38.s: Dust aerosols over the Indo-Gangetic Plain assist the advance of the monsoon inland because they:
o: Reverse the direction of ocean currents
Heat the mid-troposphere and help pull the monsoon inland
Cool the lower troposphere and suppress convection
Eliminate pressure differences between land and sea
38.x: Dust aerosols heat the mid-troposphere over the Indo-Gangetic Plain. This heating helps pull the monsoon inland.
38.tq: Apply the stated cause-and-effect relationship rather than merely recalling a definition.

38.s: ‘Nautapa’ refers to:
o: A prolonged break in the northeast monsoon
A nine-day period of winter rainfall in south India
The first week of the southwest monsoon in Kerala
A nine-day period of peak summer heat in north India before the monsoon
38.x: Nautapa is the traditional nine-day peak of summer heat in north India and occurs just before the arrival of the monsoon.
38.tq: Identify a traditional climatic term by its duration, season and region.

38.s: Kaal Baisakhi (Nor'westers), the violent evening thunderstorms of the hot-weather season, are associated mainly with
38.x: Kaal Baisakhi strikes West Bengal (also Odisha and Assam) in the hot season (APPSC GS 2025 key). Kerala gets mango showers, while Rajasthan and Punjab get the Loo and Andhi dust storms.
38.tq: Kaal Baisakhi = West Bengal; mango showers = Kerala/Karnataka.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the normal onset and advance of the south-west monsoon:
1. It normally sets in over Kerala on 1 June.
2. It reaches the Andaman and Nicobar Islands about 25 May, roughly a week before Kerala.
3. As per IMD's revised normal dates, it covers the whole country by 15 June.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: normal onset over Kerala is 1 June. Statement 2 is correct: the A&N Islands get it around 25 May, about a week earlier. Statement 3 is wrong: IMD's revised normal date for covering the whole country is 8 July (15 June is roughly when it reaches Bhopal). So 1 and 2 only (B); A leaves out true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
38.tq: A&N 25 May -> Kerala 1 June -> whole country 8 July.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the duration of the southwest monsoon in India:
1. It lasts for less than 75 days in western Rajasthan.
2. It lasts for more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula.
3. Its duration is uniform throughout the country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The duration is less than 75 days in western Rajasthan and more than 120 days in the south-western peninsula. It is not uniform throughout India.
38.tq: Compare regional extremes and reject the absolute statement about uniformity.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the approximate advance of the southwest monsoon?
o: Bhopal by 15 June and Delhi by 25 June
Bhopal by 25 May and Delhi by 1 June
Bhopal by 1 July and Delhi by 8 July
Bhopal by 25 June and Delhi by 15 July
38.x: The southwest monsoon normally reaches Bhopal around 15 June and Delhi around 25 June.
38.tq: Use the sequence and paired dates to distinguish advance dates from onset and withdrawal dates.

38.s: During a ‘break’ in the southwest monsoon, which one of the following conditions generally occurs?
o: The Arabian Sea branch reverses into a winter monsoon over the west coast.
The tropical easterly jet disappears and the westerly jet moves south of the Himalayas.
The monsoon trough shifts permanently to the Indian Ocean and all rainfall stops.
The monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, leaving the plains relatively dry.
38.x: During a monsoon break, the trough shifts towards the Himalayan foothills. The plains consequently experience dry conditions while the Himalayan region receives heavy rainfall.
38.tq: Apply the cause-and-effect relationship between trough position and regional rainfall.

38.s: The withdrawal of the southwest monsoon from India normally:
o: Begins in the south in May and ends in August
Begins in the north-west in October and ends by the end of November
Begins in the east in September and ends by mid-October
Begins simultaneously throughout India in November
38.x: Withdrawal begins from north-western India in October and is generally complete by the end of November.
38.tq: Remember the direction and time span of withdrawal rather than the onset sequence.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bay of Bengal branch — moves north along the western coast after crossing the Western Ghats
Arabian Sea branch — Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall
Arabian Sea branch — first strikes the Meghalaya hills
Bay of Bengal branch — produces a rain-shadow region immediately east of the Western Ghats
38.x: Agumbe and Hulikal receive very heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch. The other descriptions interchange the paths and effects of the two branches.
38.tq: Use branch-specific routes and locations to eliminate swapped descriptions.

38.s: The rain-shadow region associated with the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon lies mainly:
o: To the west of the Malabar Coast
To the east of the Western Ghats
38.x: The Western Ghats force uplift on their windward side, leaving a rain-shadow region to their east.
38.tq: Use the windward-leeward comparison to identify the rain-shadow location.

38.s: The southwest monsoon season contributes approximately what proportion of India's annual rainfall?
38.x: The southwest monsoon season provides about 75 per cent of India's annual rainfall.
38.tq: Select the stated national share without confusing it with regional rainfall percentages.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon:
1. It strikes the Myanmar and north-eastern hills at nearly right angles.
2. It is subsequently turned westward by the Himalayas along the Ganga plain.
3. It produces an east-to-west decline of rainfall over the northern plains.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements correctly describe the path and rainfall effect of the Bay of Bengal branch.
38.tq: Follow the sequence of wind movement before judging the resulting rainfall pattern.

38.s: The long-period average (LPA) of south-west monsoon rainfall over India, based on 1971–2020, is
38.x: The LPA of the south-west monsoon for 1971–2020 is 868.6 mm (about 87 cm). 668.6 and 768.6 mm are distractors, and about 1,187 cm (not mm) is Mawsynram's mean annual rainfall.
38.tq: SW monsoon LPA = 868.6 mm ~ 87 cm.

38.s: Which one of the following places is recognised as the wettest place in India, receiving a mean annual rainfall of approximately 1,187 cm?
38.x: Mawsynram in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya receives a mean annual rainfall of approximately 1,187 cm and is the wettest place in India.
38.tq: Use the exact place–figure association rather than confusing nearby high-rainfall places.

38.s:
Consider the following statements regarding exceptionally high rainfall locations in India:
1. Mawsynram is located in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya.
2. Cherrapunji is also known as Sohra.
3. Agumbe and Hulikal are wettest locations on the crest of the Western Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: All three statements are correct. Mawsynram and Cherrapunji are in Meghalaya, while Agumbe and Hulikal in Karnataka are notable wet locations on the Western Ghats crest.
38.tq: Check each place–region pair separately before selecting the combination.

38.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the states with the highest and lowest rainfall in India respectively?
38.x: Meghalaya is identified as the highest-rainfall state, whereas Rajasthan is the lowest-rainfall state in the stated comparison.
38.tq: Split the pair and verify the direction of the comparison.

38.s:
Which of the following regions are included in the low-rainfall zone receiving less than 60 cm of rainfall?
1. Thar Desert
2. Punjab-Haryana region
3. Kutch
4. Ladakh-Karakoram
5. Interior Peninsula
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The low-rainfall zone receiving less than 60 cm covers the Thar, Punjab-Haryana, Kutch, Ladakh-Karakoram and the interior peninsula.
38.tq: Treat a listed geographical classification as a checklist and test every member.

38.s:
Which of the following areas are situated in rain-shadow regions associated with the Western Ghats or the Himalayas?
1. Interior Maharashtra
2. Karnataka interior
3. Telangana
4. Rayalaseema
5. Ladakh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The lee of the Western Ghats includes interior Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, Rayalaseema and parts of Tamil Nadu; Ladakh lies in the rain shadow behind the Himalayas.
38.tq: Use the physical barrier and its lee-side effect to identify all applicable regions.

38.s: Why does Rajasthan receive very little rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon?
o: The Aravalli Range lies parallel to the branch and therefore does not provide significant uplift.
The branch is diverted completely towards the Bay of Bengal by the Himalayas.
The branch loses all its moisture over the Western Ghats before reaching Rajasthan.
The branch reaches Rajasthan only after crossing the Khasi Hills.
38.x: The Arabian Sea branch runs parallel to the Aravallis, so the range does not act as a barrier to force the air upward and produce substantial rainfall.
38.tq: Ask whether the mountain range is perpendicular or parallel to the moisture-bearing winds.

38.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
38.x: Ruyli in Jaisalmer district receives about 8.33 cm of rainfall and is identified as the driest place in India. Bellary and Leh are low-rainfall areas, whereas Cherrapunji is in Meghalaya.
38.tq: Start from the sure place–attribute pair and reject reversed extremes.

38.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Leeward Deccan—rain shadow of the Western Ghats
2. Ladakh—region behind the Great Himalaya and cold desert
3. Hagari valley—lowest rainfall region in Andhra Pradesh
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: The leeward Deccan lies in the Western Ghats’ rain shadow, Ladakh lies behind the Great Himalaya and is a cold desert, and the Hagari valley has the lowest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, below 51 cm.
38.tq: Verify each region–cause pair, paying special attention to the Andhra Pradesh exception.

38.s:
Which of the following phenomena are associated with the retreating southwest monsoon?
1. The Sun moves southward and the north-western low-pressure area weakens.
2. The westerly jet returns south of the Himalayas.
3. The tropical easterly jet disappears.
4. Clear skies and ‘October heat’ are experienced.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
38.x: All four conditions accompany the retreating monsoon. The weakening of the north-western low, jet-stream changes and clear, hot weather are characteristic of October–November.
38.tq: Test a complete cluster of associated seasonal characteristics.

38.s: The bimodal rainfall received by parts of southern India during the retreating monsoon is mainly associated with:
o: The permanent high over the South Indian Ocean
38.x: Bay of Bengal cyclones bring bimodal rainfall to the south during the October–November retreating monsoon season.
38.tq: Match the seasonal rainfall feature with its immediate weather system.

38.s: Western disturbances affecting north-western India are best described as:
o: Mediterranean temperate cyclones reaching India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan
Tropical cyclones originating in the Bay of Bengal
Local convectional storms originating over the Thar Desert
Retreating monsoon winds originating over the Arabian Sea
38.x: Western disturbances are temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region and reaching north-western India through Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
38.tq: Identify the origin and pathway of the weather system.

38.s: The term ‘October heat’ refers to:
o: A heat wave occurring exclusively in north-western India in April
Extreme heat caused by western disturbances
Hot and humid weather during the retreat of the monsoon
Cold and dry weather after the winter monsoon
38.x: October heat denotes the hot and humid conditions experienced in October as the south-west monsoon retreats.
38.tq: Discriminate between a named climatic phenomenon and nearby seasonal conditions.

38.s: The relative dryness of the Tamil Nadu coast during the south-west monsoon is mainly due to:
o: The permanent dominance of western disturbances
Its location on the leeward side and the winds blowing parallel to the coast
Its location north of the Tropic of Cancer
The absence of the Bay of Bengal
38.x: The Tamil Nadu coast lies in a rain-shadow position during the south-west monsoon, while the winds largely blow parallel to the coast.
38.tq: Apply the rain-shadow and wind-direction concepts to a regional example.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the north-east monsoon:
1. Its retreating winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.
2. It brings rain to the Coromandel (Tamil Nadu) coast during October-December.
3. Because of this winter rain, the Coromandel coast falls under the Köppen climate type Aw.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: retreating winds gain Bay of Bengal moisture. Statement 2 is correct: the NE monsoon (Oct-Dec) rains on the Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam. Statement 3 is wrong: the Coromandel coast is 'As' (monsoon with dry summer); Aw is tropical savanna of most of the peninsula, including AP. So 1 and 2 only (B); A leaves out true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
38.tq: As = dry Summer, wet winter -> Coromandel.

38.s: Which group of regions is specifically identified as receiving rainfall from the north-east monsoon?
o: Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Kashmir
Gujarat, western Rajasthan, Punjab and Ladakh
Konkan, Malabar, Goa and coastal Karnataka
38.x: The north-east monsoon brings rainfall to the Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam.
38.tq: Test the complete regional distribution rather than a single location.

38.s: Western disturbances originating from the Mediterranean are associated with:
o: 3–8 cm rain in coastal Andhra Pradesh and snowfall in the Nilgiris
South-west monsoon rain over the entire Indian peninsula
10–15 cm rain in north-west India and snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand
Only dry winds over north-west India without agricultural significance
38.x: Mediterranean western disturbances bring about 10–15 cm of rain to north-west India, benefit rabi crops and produce snowfall in Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
38.tq: Keep the rainfall range, crop effect and snowfall region together.

38.s: Which of the following climate-type codes is correctly matched with its region?
o: Amw — West coast south of Goa
BWhw — Most of the peninsula south of the Tropic of Cancer
38.x: Amw denotes a monsoon climate with a short dry season and occurs on the west coast south of Goa.
38.tq: Start from the sure climate-code and region pair.

38.s: The climate type BShw is associated with:
o: A cold humid climate with a short summer in Arunachal Pradesh
A semi-arid steppe climate in north-western Gujarat, western Rajasthan and parts of Punjab
A monsoon climate with dry summer on the Coromandel coast
A hot desert climate in extreme western Rajasthan
38.x: BShw represents a semi-arid steppe climate found in north-western Gujarat, western Rajasthan and parts of Punjab.
38.tq: Distinguish between similar Koppen climate codes by region and climate character.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Aw — Most of the peninsula south of the Tropic of Cancer
As — Coromandel coast and Tamil Nadu
Cwg — Ganga plain, eastern Rajasthan and northern Madhya Pradesh
38.x: ET denotes a polar or tundra climate found in the highlands of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, not coastal Andhra Pradesh.
38.tq: Find the wrong location attached to an otherwise familiar climate code.

38.s: The climate type Dfc is characteristic of:
o: The west coast south of Goa
38.x: Dfc denotes a cold humid climate with a short summer and is associated with Arunachal Pradesh.
38.tq: Use the distinctive climate-region association.

38.s:
Match the Koeppen climate code with its region:
a. As
b. Cwg
c. BWhw
d. Amw

i. Ganga plain
ii. Coromandel coast
iii. Extreme western Rajasthan
iv. West coast south of Goa
38.x: As (monsoon with dry summer) is the Coromandel coast; Cwg (monsoon with dry winter) is the Ganga plain; BWhw (hot desert) is extreme western Rajasthan; Amw (short dry season) is the west coast south of Goa. B swaps As and Cwg, C swaps the desert and west-coast codes, and D is wrong throughout.
38.tq: Dry summer = Coromandel (As); dry winter = Ganga plain (Cwg).

38.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Monsoon Mission:
1. It was launched in 2012 by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
2. It is implemented through IITM Pune and the IMD.
3. Its second phase ran from 2017 to 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: MoES launched it in 2012. Statement 2 is correct: IITM Pune and IMD run it. Statement 3 is wrong: Phase 1 was 2012-17 and Phase 2 was 2017-25. So 1 and 2 only (B); A leaves out true statement 2, C and D include the false statement 3.
38.tq: 2012 launch, 2017 and 2025 phase ends.

38.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. SEFS statistical ensemble — 2007
2. Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System — 2012
3. Multi-Model Ensemble — 2021
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
38.x: SEFS was associated with 2007, the Monsoon Mission Coupled Forecasting System with 2012 and the Multi-Model Ensemble with 2021.
38.tq: Match each technical model with its introduction year.

38.s:
Consider the following statements about Mission Mausam:
1. It was launched on 14 January 2025 along with IMD Vision 2047.
2. It is implemented by the IMD, NCMRWF and ISRO.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
38.x: Statement 1 is correct: Mission Mausam was launched on 14 January 2025 with IMD Vision 2047. Statement 2 is wrong: it is implemented by the IMD, NCMRWF and IITM, not ISRO. So 1 only (A); B and C accept the false statement 2, D rejects the true statement 1.
38.tq: Same MoES trio as always: IMD, NCMRWF, IITM.

38.s: The Bharat Forecast System developed under Mission Mausam provides:
o: 10 km resolution and one-year drought forecasts
26 km resolution and seasonal snowfall forecasts
1 km resolution and one-month temperature forecasts
38.x: The Bharat Forecast System provides forecasts at 6 km resolution, including 10-day rainfall forecasts.
38.tq: Match the technical system with both its resolution and forecast period.

38.s: The number of Doppler weather radars in India increased from 14 in 2014 to approximately:
38.x: India had 47 Doppler weather radars, compared with 14 in 2014.
38.tq: Test a before-and-after infrastructure figure.

38.s: Ocean Mean Temperature is measured as the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean up to the:
38.x: OMT is the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean down to the 26°C isotherm.
38.tq: Recall the defining threshold of a specialised ocean indicator.

38.s: Which statement about Ocean Mean Temperature is correct?
o: It is measured in January-March and predicts monsoon rainfall better than SST.
It is measured in June-September and is less useful than SST for monsoon prediction.
It is measured only in October and predicts snowfall in the Himalayas.
It refers to the temperature of the entire Indian Ocean basin throughout the year.
38.x: OMT is measured during January-March and has been identified as a better predictor of monsoon rainfall than sea-surface temperature.
38.tq: Distinguish a specialised indicator from the related SST concept.

38.s: In 2026, the southwest monsoon set in over Kerala on
38.x: In 2026, the monsoon reached Kerala on 4 June, which was three days later than the normal date.
38.tq: Distinguish the Kerala onset date from the later Andhra Pradesh onset date.

38.s: Which phenomenon was being watched in 2026 as a possible offset to El Nino's adverse influence on the Indian monsoon?
38.x: The Indian Ocean Dipole was being monitored as a possible offset to the influence of El Nino.
38.tq: Identify the associated climate oscillation rather than a general atmospheric circulation feature.

38.s:
With reference to the 2026 monsoon forecast, consider the following statements:
1. The IMD forecast was about 90% of the long-period average.
2. A June rainfall deficit of 43% led the Centre to activate contingency plans.
3. The forecast was issued in the absence of any El Nino concern.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
38.x: The forecast was about 90% of the long-period average, and the 43% June deficit led to contingency planning. Statement 3 is false because a developing super El Nino was a concern.
38.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the reported climate concern.

38.s: The rainfall deficit in Andhra Pradesh during 1 June–25 August 2026 was reported as
38.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded a 51.2% rainfall deficit during 1 June–25 August 2026.
38.tq: Match the percentage with its period and geographical unit before considering district figures.

38.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to rainfall extremes in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Sileru-Sabari valleys — 140–152 cm; Hagari valley — less than 51 cm
Sileru-Sabari valleys — less than 51 cm; Hagari valley — 140–152 cm
Sileru-Sabari valleys — about 966 cm; Hagari valley — 75.9 cm
Sileru-Sabari valleys — 51–75 cm; Hagari valley — 90–100 cm
38.x: The Sileru-Sabari valleys are the wettest parts of Andhra Pradesh, receiving about 140–152 cm, while the Hagari valley is the driest, receiving less than 51 cm.
38.tq: Use the wettest–driest contrast and verify both the region and range.

38.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the hottest and the coolest places are respectively
38.x: Rentachintala (Palnadu) is the hottest place in AP and Lambasingi the coolest. Option A reverses them; the Hagari and Sileru valleys are AP's rainfall extremes (driest and wettest), not temperature extremes, and Antarvedi is the Godavari's mouth.
38.tq: Hot Rentachintala, cool Lambasingi.

39.s: Which of the following correctly represents the east-to-west decrease of rainfall across the northern plains?
39.x: Rainfall decreases eastward to westward across the northern plains in the sequence Kolkata, Patna, Prayagraj, Delhi and Bikaner.
39.tq: Read the spatial gradient as a directional sequence rather than a time sequence.

39.s: The broad pattern of rainfall distribution across the northern plains and the peninsular region is respectively
o: from east to west and from west to east
uniform from east to west and from west to east
from west to east and from east to west
from north to south and from south to north
39.x: Rainfall decreases from east to west along the northern plains, while across the peninsula it generally decreases from west to east.
39.tq: Compare the two directional trends without reversing their order.

39.s: The south-west monsoon lasts less than 75 days in ____ and more than 120 days in ____.
39.x: The monsoon lasts less than 75 days in western Rajasthan, where it arrives late and leaves early, and more than 120 days in the south-west peninsula, where it arrives first. Option B reverses the two; the others name regions the notes do not give for these limits.
39.tq: <75 days W Rajasthan; >120 days SW peninsula.

39.s: Which of the following regions generally have a high coefficient of variation of rainfall, above 50 percent?
39.x: Western Rajasthan, Kutch and Ladakh generally have a high rainfall coefficient of variation above 50 percent. The west coast, Western Ghats, north-east and eastern peninsula generally have low variability below 25 percent.
39.tq: Separate high-variability dry regions from low-variability humid regions.

39.s: Which statement about Indian rainfall variability is correct?
o: Only the withdrawal date varies, while onset is fixed
The onset and withdrawal dates are fixed every year
Only the onset date varies, while withdrawal is fixed
The dates of monsoon onset and withdrawal show large inter-annual variability
39.x: There is large inter-annual variability in both the onset and withdrawal dates of the monsoon.
39.tq: Watch for reversed or exclusive wording when two linked dates are involved.

39.s: A district records rainfall 65 percent above its normal rainfall. Under the IMD departure classification, it would be placed in which category?
39.x: Rainfall departure of +60 percent or more is classified as large excess for a state or district. The separate all-India season categories use different percentage bands.
39.tq: Apply the correct state or district departure band rather than the all-India seasonal band.

39.s: Which of the following correctly represents the IMD rainfall departure bands for a state or district?
o: Large excess: +50% or more; Excess: +10% to +49%; Normal: 0% to +20%
Large excess: +60% or more; Excess: +20% to +59%; Normal: -19% to +19%
Large excess: above +110%; Excess: +60% to +100%; Normal: -20% to +20%
Large excess: -60% to -99%; Excess: -20% to -59%; Normal: -19% to +19%
39.x: For a state or district, large excess is +60 percent or more, excess is +20 to +59 percent, and normal is -19 to +19 percent. Deficient is -20 to -59 percent and large deficient is -60 to -99 percent.
39.tq: Compare adjacent departure bands and detect reversed positive and negative ranges.

39.s: For the all-India season, rainfall below 90 percent of the Long Period Average is classified as:
39.x: For the all-India season, rainfall below 90 percent of the LPA is classified as deficient. Below normal is 90–95 percent, normal is 96–104 percent, above normal is 105–110 percent and excess is above 110 percent.
39.tq: Keep the all-India seasonal classification separate from state and district departure categories.

39.s: The coefficient of variation (CV) used to measure rainfall variability is calculated as
39.x: CV = (standard deviation / mean) x 100. Option A inverts the ratio, and the range or mean deviation are other measures of spread. A higher CV means more variable rainfall, as in western Rajasthan (>50%).
39.tq: CV = SD/mean x 100; high CV = unreliable rain.

39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. El Niño is identified when the central/east equatorial Pacific is at least 0.5°C warmer for five consecutive overlapping 3-month periods.
2. Every El Niño year has produced a weak Indian monsoon.
3. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset the effect of El Niño.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: Statement 1 is correct: that is the stated El Niño threshold. Statement 2 is wrong: only about 6 of 10 El Niño years brought weak Indian monsoons. Statement 3 is correct: a positive IOD can offset El Niño. So 1 and 3 only (B); A leaves out true statement 3, C and D include the false statement 2.
39.tq: 'Every' / 'always' with El Niño is a trap - it is 6 out of 10.

39.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. La Niña generally strengthens the Indian monsoon.
2. La Niña is associated with colder winters.
3. La Niña can bring more Bay of Bengal cyclones.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: La Niña generally strengthens the monsoon and is associated with colder winters and more Bay of Bengal cyclones. All three statements are correct.
39.tq: Test the complete set of effects associated with La Niña.

39.s: Which pair of years is cited as deficient southwest monsoon years in the stated rainfall record?
39.x: The cited deficient years are 2015, when actual rainfall was 86 percent of LPA, and 2023, associated with the 2023–24 El Niño.
39.tq: Link the years with the deficient-rainfall description instead of inferring from a general climate cycle.

39.s: About what proportion of India’s agricultural or cultivable land is drought-prone in varying degrees?
39.x: About 68 percent of India’s agricultural or cultivable land is drought-prone in varying degrees.
39.tq: Use the numerical figure directly and distinguish cultivable land from total geographical area.

39.s:
Which of the following regions are identified as chronically drought-prone?
1. Western Rajasthan and Gujarat
2. The rain-shadow Deccan
3. Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: Chronic drought-prone regions include western Rajasthan, Gujarat, the rain-shadow Deccan, Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam. In Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam, failure of the north-east monsoon and groundwater depletion contribute to chronic drought.
39.tq: Combine the national and Andhra Pradesh examples before selecting the inclusive code.

39.s:
Consider the following pairs (type of drought : basis):
1. Meteorological drought : rainfall deficit
2. Agricultural drought : river flow and groundwater levels
3. Flash drought : sudden heat with no rain
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
39.x: Pair 1 is correct: meteorological drought = rain deficit. Pair 2 is wrong: agricultural drought is about soil moisture; river and groundwater define hydrological drought. Pair 3 is correct: flash drought = sudden heat plus no rain. So 1 and 3 only (B); A leaves out pair 3, C and D include the wrong pair 2.
39.tq: Meteorological-rain, agricultural-soil, hydrological-water bodies.

39.s: The Manual for Drought Management, 2016, revised in 2020, uses which combination of indicators for drought declaration?
o: Rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators
Cloud cover, humidity, pressure and sunshine duration only
River length, crop export, population and forest area
Temperature, latitude, altitude and wind speed only
39.x: The Manual for Drought Management uses rainfall deficit, vegetation, soil moisture and water indicators for declaring drought. Exact current trigger thresholds are not specified here.
39.tq: Identify the responsible indicators instead of assuming rainfall alone determines declaration.

39.s: Approximately what share of India’s land is prone to floods and river erosion?
39.x: Approximately 12 percent of India’s land is prone to floods and river erosion.
39.tq: Recall the area proportion and distinguish it from drought-prone cultivable land.

39.s:
Which of the following areas are among the worst affected by floods in India?
1. Brahmaputra valley
2. Kosi and Ganga plains of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh
3. Coastal deltas of the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Odisha and West Bengal
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
39.x: The Brahmaputra valley, the Kosi and Ganga plains, and several eastern and southern coastal deltas are major flood-affected areas. The Brahmaputra valley is popularly associated with the ‘sorrow of Assam’.
39.tq: Group the major flood basins and deltas without omitting the Himalayan valley.

39.s: Which one of the following is NOT a flood-mitigation measure identified for flood-prone areas?
o: Complete removal of all river channels
39.x: Embankments, drainage channels, sea dykes and real-time flood forecasting are recognised mitigation measures. Complete removal of river channels is not a flood-mitigation measure.
39.tq: Find the option that is not a practical mitigation measure among the listed interventions.

39.s: Why do Himalayan rivers frequently cause floods during the monsoon season?
o: They are unaffected by intense rainfall events
They flow only through desert regions
They swell during the monsoon, while cloudburst flash floods are also increasing in the Himalaya and the north-east
They receive no monsoon rainfall but are fed only by groundwater
39.x: Himalayan rivers swell during the monsoon, and cloudburst-induced flash floods are increasing in the Himalaya and the north-east.
39.tq: Connect the physical cause with the resulting flood hazard.

39.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rainfall deficiency reported by 16 September 2026:
1. Meghalaya recorded the highest rainfall deficiency among the regions mentioned.
2. Manipur recorded a rainfall deficiency of 43 per cent.
3. Andhra Pradesh recorded a rainfall deficiency of 42 per cent and was the third worst-affected region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
39.x: All three statements are correct. Meghalaya recorded the worst deficiency at 59 per cent, Manipur recorded 43 per cent deficiency, and Andhra Pradesh recorded 42 per cent deficiency, ranking third worst.
39.tq: Check each percentage independently before selecting the coded combination.

39.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the broad rainfall pattern of Andhra Pradesh?
o: The State receives about 278.7 mm of average annual rainfall, with almost all rainfall from the Northeast Monsoon.
The State receives about 681.6 mm of average annual rainfall, divided equally between the two monsoons.
The State receives about 966 mm of average annual rainfall, of which the Southwest Monsoon contributes about two-thirds and the Northeast Monsoon about one-third.
The State receives about 966 mm of average annual rainfall, of which the Northeast Monsoon contributes about two-thirds and the Southwest Monsoon about one-third.
39.x: Andhra Pradesh has an average annual rainfall of about 966 mm. Approximately two-thirds is received from the Southwest Monsoon and one-third from the Northeast Monsoon.
39.tq: Use the relative-share comparison to distinguish the dominant monsoon from the subordinate one.

39.s: The highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh, ranging from approximately 140 to 152 cm, is associated with which of the following areas?
39.x: The highest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh occurs in the Sileru–Sabari valleys, where it ranges from about 140 to 152 cm.
39.tq: Identify the precise geographical location linked with the stated rainfall range.

40.s: The classification of Indian forest types associated with H.G. Champion and G.S. Puri comprises how many major types and sub-types?
40.x: The classification associated with H.G. Champion and G.S. Puri recognises 5 major types and 15 sub-types.
40.tq: Directly distinguish the paired numerical classification figures.

40.s: Which one of the following forest types is correctly matched with its characteristic rainfall?
o: Tropical wet evergreen — less than 25 cm
40.x: Tropical thorn forests occur in areas receiving about 25–75 cm of rainfall. Wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm, semi-evergreen forests 200–250 cm, and dry deciduous forests 75–100 cm.
40.tq: Use the rainfall range to eliminate reversed forest-type pairs.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding tropical wet evergreen forests:
1. They generally occur in areas receiving more than 250 cm of rainfall.
2. They are found in parts of the Western Ghats and North-Eastern India.
3. They account for approximately 37% of India’s forest area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: Tropical wet evergreen forests require more than 250 cm of rainfall and occur in the Western Ghats, Assam, Meghalaya, Manipur, Tripura, Nagaland and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Their share is about 8%, not 37%.
40.tq: Identify the false percentage while retaining the correct distribution statements.

40.s: Which of the following groups contains only important species of tropical wet evergreen forests in India?
40.x: Rosewood, ebony, mahogany, gurjan and ironwood are among the important species of tropical wet evergreen forests.
40.tq: Group species by the forest type in which they naturally occur.

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the lists:

List-I (Forest type)
a. Moist deciduous
b. Dry deciduous
c. Thorn

d. Littoral or tidal

List-II (Characteristic species)
i. Rhizophora and Avicennia
ii. Teak, sal and mahua
iii. Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis
iv. Teak, sandalwood and Terminalia

Codes:
40.x: Moist deciduous forests include teak, sal and mahua; dry deciduous forests include teak, sandalwood and Terminalia; thorn forests include Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis; tidal forests include Rhizophora and Avicennia.
40.tq: Start from the sure mangrove pair and complete the species associations.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about the distribution of natural vegetation in India:
1. Dry deciduous forests of Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Nallamala and Eastern Ghats.
2. Tropical thorn forests occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema.
3. Desert (xerophytic) vegetation is found in areas receiving 25-75 cm of rainfall.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
40.x: Statement 1 is correct: AP's dry deciduous forests lie in the Nallamala and Eastern Ghats. Statement 2 is correct: thorn forests occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema. Statement 3 is wrong: desert vegetation occurs below 25 cm; 25-75 cm is the thorn-forest range. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' wrongly include statement 3.
40.tq: Thorn = 25-75 cm; desert = below 25 cm.

40.s: Shola forests are best described as:
o: Temperate forests of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills
Alpine meadows above the Himalayan tree line
Tropical thorn forests of the north-western plains
40.x: Sholas are temperate forest formations of the Nilgiris, Anaimalai and Palani hills, generally occurring as stunted evergreen patches with grasslands in the Western Ghats.
40.tq: Discriminate the regional meaning of the term ‘Shola’ from alpine and mangrove formations.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about alpine vegetation in India:
1. It occurs above the tree line in the Himalaya.
2. Alpine meadows may extend up to about 4,750 metres.
3. It is principally a tidal-coast formation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: Alpine vegetation occurs above the tree line in the Himalaya, and alpine meadows may extend up to about 4,750 metres. It is not a tidal-coast formation.
40.tq: Reject the geographically incompatible statement.

40.s:
Arrange the following forest types in descending order of their share in India’s forest area:
A. Tropical dry deciduous
B. Tropical wet evergreen
C. Tropical moist deciduous
40.x: Tropical moist deciduous forests account for about 37%, tropical dry deciduous forests about 28.6%, and tropical wet evergreen forests about 8%.
40.tq: Rank the categories by percentage before selecting the sequence.

40.s: The tropical deciduous forests of India together account for approximately what share of the country’s forest area?
40.x: Tropical moist deciduous and tropical dry deciduous forests together account for approximately 65.6% of India’s forest area.
40.tq: Add the two deciduous forest shares rather than selecting the larger individual category.

40.s: Tidal forests in India are found not only in deltaic and creek regions but also in the:
40.x: Tidal or mangrove forests occur in deltas and creeks and also in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
40.tq: Use the coastal-island association to identify the additional distribution area.

40.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its Himalayan altitude zone?
40.x: Sub-tropical chir pine occurs around 1,000–1,800 metres. Moist temperate forests occur around 1,500–3,000 metres, alpine meadows around 2,900–6,000 metres, and dry alpine scrub above 4,000 metres.
40.tq: Match the vegetation zone with its altitude range without reversing the sequence.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about Himalayan altitude zones:
1. Moist temperate forests include oak, deodar and fir.
2. Sub-alpine vegetation includes fir, birch and rhododendron.
3. Dry alpine scrub dominated by juniper occurs above about 4,000 metres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All three statements correctly describe Himalayan vegetation zones and their characteristic species or altitude.
40.tq: Verify each altitude-zone and species association separately.

40.s:
Arrange the following Himalayan vegetation zones from lower to higher elevation:
A. Temperate forests
B. Alpine meadows
C. Tropical sal forests
D. Subtropical chir-pine forests
E. Subalpine birch-rhododendron forests
40.x: The sequence upward is tropical sal foothills, subtropical chir pine, temperate forests, subalpine birch-rhododendron forests and alpine meadows.
40.tq: Use the lower-to-higher elevation sequence and check the first and last zones.

40.s: Which one of the following combinations is associated with temperate Himalayan forests?
o: Mangrove, sundari, stilt root and knee root
Oak, deodar, blue pine and silver fir
40.x: Temperate Himalayan forests include oak, deodar, blue pine and silver fir.
40.tq: Identify a vegetation belt from its characteristic species.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about Himalayan vegetation:
1. Eastern Himalayan forests include oaks, laurels, maples, rhododendrons, alder and birch.
2. The tree line is lower in the Eastern Himalaya than in the Western Himalaya.
3. The northern slopes generally carry denser forests than the southern slopes.
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the southern or windward slopes generally carry denser forests than the northern slopes.
40.tq: Use a reversed-slope comparison as the main distractor.

40.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sal — Moist deciduous forests of the Terai and Indo-Gangetic plains
Jackfruit — Alpine meadows of the Himalaya
40.x: Jackfruit is an evergreen tree associated with the Western Ghats, not with Himalayan alpine meadows. Sal, teak and deodar are correctly matched with their stated regions.
40.tq: Find the species placed in a clearly unsuitable ecological region.

40.s:
Which of the following statements regarding sal and teak is correct?
1. Sal is associated with moist deciduous forests.
2. Sal occurs in the Terai, Indo-Gangetic plain, Chota Nagpur and parts of the Northeast.
3. Teak is associated with central and peninsular India and also occurs in the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh.
40.x: Sal is a moist deciduous species with the listed distribution, while teak occurs in central and peninsular India, including the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh. All three statements are correct.
40.tq: Test a species through a combined type-and-distribution statement set.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the tree with its forest type and region?
o: Sandalwood — Dry deciduous forests of South India
Deodar — Tropical mangrove forests of Odisha
40.x: Sandalwood is associated with dry deciduous forests of South India. Deodar occurs in the Western Himalaya, mahua in Central India and jackfruit in the Western Ghats.
40.tq: Use the forest-type and region pair together to reject mismatches.

40.s:
Which of the following statements regarding mangrove vegetation is correct?
1. Mangroves commonly possess stilt and knee roots.
2. Their roots may remain submerged during high tide.
3. They generally occur at the fringes of river deltas on both coasts of India.
40.x: Mangroves possess specialised stilt and knee roots, occur in intertidal deltaic areas and may be submerged during high tide. All three statements are correct.
40.tq: Combine related ecological adaptations and distribution facts in a statement-based question.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about mangrove cover in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh had 421.43 sq km of mangrove cover according to ISFR 2023.
2. Its mangrove cover increased by 13.01 sq km.
3. The mangrove cover includes a very dense class.
40.x: Andhra Pradesh had 421.43 sq km of mangrove cover in ISFR 2023, showing an increase of 13.01 sq km. It had no very dense mangrove class.
40.tq: Use a numerical statement pair with one reversed or unsupported classification.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the conflicting claims regarding the rank of Andhra Pradesh in mangrove cover?
o: The State Economic Survey places Andhra Pradesh third, whereas ISFR 2023 places Odisha second.
AP State Economic Survey describes Andhra Pradesh as having the second-largest mangrove cover, whereas ISFR 2023 places Gujarat second.
ISFR 2023 places Andhra Pradesh first, whereas the State Economic Survey places West Bengal second.
Both sources place Andhra Pradesh first in mangrove cover.
40.x: The Andhra Pradesh SES 2025–26 describes AP as having the second-largest mangrove cover, while ISFR 2023 places Gujarat second. This is identified as a data discrepancy.
40.tq: Compare two authorities instead of relying on a single rank claim.

40.s: According to the older distributional estimate cited for India’s mangroves, which of the following is the correct descending order of shares?
o: West Bengal, Gujarat, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Gujarat, West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Andaman and Nicobar Islands, West Bengal, Gujarat
West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Gujarat
40.x: The older estimate gives West Bengal about 50%, Gujarat about 21% and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands about 14% of India’s mangroves.
40.tq: Use the relative percentages to establish descending order.

40.s:
Consider the following pairs (mangrove site : State):
1. Bhitarkanika : Odisha
2. Pichavaram : Tamil Nadu
3. Coringa : Andhra Pradesh
4. Sundarbans : Gujarat
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
40.x: Pairs 1-3 are correct: Bhitarkanika (saltwater crocodiles) is in Odisha, Pichavaram near Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu, and Coringa WLS near Kakinada in AP. Pair 4 is wrong: the Sundarbans, India's largest mangrove, is in West Bengal. So 1, 2 and 3 only.
40.tq: Sundarbans WB, Bhitarkanika Odisha, Pichavaram TN, Coringa AP.

40.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Grass type)
a. Sehima-Dichanthium
b. Phragmites-Saccharum
c. Deschampsia-Deyeuxia
d. Bothriochloa

List-II (Habitat)
i. Alpine region
ii. High-rainfall paddy tracts
iii. Black-soil regions
iv. Marshy localities

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
40.x: Sehima-Dichanthium occurs on black soils; Phragmites-Saccharum in marshy localities; Deschampsia-Deyeuxia in alpine regions; and Bothriochloa in high-rainfall paddy tracts.
40.tq: Start with the sure habitat association and eliminate incompatible codes.

40.s: Banni grassland, one of the vast tropical grasslands of India, is located in:
40.x: Banni is a vast tropical grassland situated in the Kutch region of Gujarat.
40.tq: Use a distinctive landscape-place association.

40.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Sabai grass — rope and paper manufacture
Banni — alpine meadow of Himachal Pradesh
40.x: Sabai grass is used for making rope and paper. Bugyals are alpine meadows of Uttarakhand, while margs are associated with Kashmir; Banni is in Kutch, Gujarat.
40.tq: Find the correctly matched item among closely related grassland terms.

40.s: For the purpose of the India State of Forest Report, forest cover refers to land of more than one hectare having canopy density of at least:
40.x: Forest cover includes land exceeding one hectare with canopy density of 10% or more, regardless of ownership.
40.tq: Separate the area criterion from the canopy-density criterion.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the density classes used in the India State of Forest Report?
o: Very Dense Forest: 40% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 20–40%; Open Forest: below 20%
Very Dense Forest: 80% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 50–80%; Open Forest: 20–50%
Very Dense Forest: 60% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 30–60%; Open Forest: 10–30%
Very Dense Forest: 70% or more; Moderately Dense Forest: 40–70%; Open Forest: 10–40%
40.x: The classes are Very Dense Forest at 70% or more, Moderately Dense Forest at 40–70%, and Open Forest at 10–40% canopy density.
40.tq: Compare the adjacent canopy-density ranges without reversing their order.

40.s: Which one of the following statements regarding scrub is correct?
o: Scrub has canopy density below 10% and is not counted as forest cover.
Scrub has canopy density between 40% and 70% and is counted as moderately dense forest.
Scrub has canopy density of 70% or more and is counted as very dense forest.
Scrub has canopy density between 10% and 40% and is counted as open forest.
40.x: Scrub is assigned to areas with canopy density below 10% and is excluded from the forest-cover category.
40.tq: Distinguish the lower threshold of scrub from the open-forest range.

40.s: According to ISFR 2023, which of the following combinations is correct for India’s forest cover, tree cover and their combined extent?
o: Forest cover 25.17%, tree cover 3.41%, combined cover 28.58%
Forest cover 21.76%, tree cover 3.41%, combined cover 25.17%
Forest cover 24.62%, tree cover 2.14%, combined cover 26.76%
Forest cover 20.00%, tree cover 5.17%, combined cover 25.17%
40.x: ISFR 2023 reported forest cover of 7,15,343 sq km or 21.76%, tree cover of 1,12,014 sq km or 3.41%, and combined forest and tree cover of 25.17%.
40.tq: Match the three related percentages rather than treating them as interchangeable.

40.s: What was the net gain in India’s forest and tree cover between 2021 and 2023 as reported in ISFR 2023?
40.x: The net gain in forest and tree cover between 2021 and 2023 was reported as 1,445.81 sq km.
40.tq: Distinguish the net gain from its separate forest-cover and tree-cover components.

40.s: Which State had the third-largest forest cover in India according to the figures provided for ISFR 2023?
40.x: Chhattisgarh had the third-largest forest cover, measuring about 55,812 sq km. Odisha had about 61,204 sq km, while Meghalaya was notable for the share of its geographical area under forest.
40.tq: Separate ranking by absolute forest area from ranking by percentage of geographical area.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly states Meghalaya’s position in relation to forest cover?
o: About 56% of its geographical area is under forest
About 36% of its geographical area is under forest
About 96% of its geographical area is under forest
About 76% of its geographical area is under forest
40.x: Approximately 76% of Meghalaya’s geographical area is under forest, according to the figures cited.
40.tq: Test percentage of geographical area rather than absolute forest-cover ranking.

40.s: Which type of forest is considered most vulnerable to forest fires?
40.x: Dry deciduous forests are especially vulnerable to fires because of their seasonal dryness and accumulation of dry biomass.
40.tq: Associate fire vulnerability with the seasonally dry forest type.

40.s: With reference to forest fires during 2023–24, which one of the following is correct regarding Andhra Pradesh?
o: It had the smallest fire-affected area and ranked first in large-fire events.
It had the largest fire-affected area, about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.
It ranked third in fire-affected area, with about 2,856.76 sq km affected.
It had the largest fire-affected area, but recorded no large-fire events.
40.x: Andhra Pradesh had the largest fire-affected area in 2023–24, measuring about 5,286.76 sq km, and ranked third in large-fire events.
40.tq: Check both the absolute area figure and the separate event ranking.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about the Forest Survey of India:
1. ISFR is published biennially.
2. The Forest Survey of India was established in 1981.
3. Its headquarters is at Dehradun.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: ISFR is a biennial assessment by the Forest Survey of India, established in 1981 and headquartered at Dehradun.
40.tq: Verify the periodicity, establishment year and location separately.

40.s: Which State has the highest forest cover percentage among the following?
40.x: Mizoram has the highest forest cover percentage mentioned, at 84.53%; Andhra Pradesh is reported at 18.28%.
40.tq: Use the highest-value comparison rather than the state-specific figure.

40.s: According to ISFR 2015, about what share of India's forest cover is prone to frequent forest fires?
40.x: About 36% of India's forest cover is prone to frequent fires (ISFR 2015; APPSC 2025 key), and dry deciduous forests are the most vulnerable. 16%, 26% and 46% are distractors.
40.tq: ~36% fire-prone; dry deciduous most at risk.

40.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 envisages forest and tree cover over what percentage of India’s total area?
40.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 set a target of 33% of the total area under forest and tree cover.
40.tq: Distinguish the national target from the separate hill-and-mountain target.

40.s: Under the National Forest Policy, 1988, the target for forest and tree cover in hills and mountains is:
40.x: The National Forest Policy, 1988 prescribed a target of 66% forest and tree cover in hills and mountains.
40.tq: Compare the general 33% target with the higher physiographic-region target.

40.s: The Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires which of the following before forest land is diverted for non-forest purposes?
o: Approval only of the district collector
Approval only of the State Legislature
Approval of the National Tiger Conservation Authority
40.x: Diversion of forest land under the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires central approval.
40.tq: Ask which authority exercises the decisive approval power.

40.s: Which institution manages the compensatory afforestation funds generated under the forest conservation framework?
40.x: CAMPA manages the compensatory afforestation funds.
40.tq: Match the environmental institution with its specific financial function.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding forest classifications:
1. In a protected forest, rights are recorded and activities are allowed unless specifically prohibited.
2. A village forest is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.
3. In a reserved forest, all activities are freely permitted unless prohibited by a specific notification.
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because activities in reserved forests are barred unless expressly permitted.
40.tq: Test the reversal between permitted activities in protected and reserved forests.

40.s: What was the approximate distribution of Andhra Pradesh forests among Reserved, Protected and Unclassed categories respectively?
40.x: In Andhra Pradesh, approximately 85.8% of forests are Reserved, 13.6% Protected and 0.6% Unclassed.
40.tq: Recall the three-part percentage distribution in the stated order.

40.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the applicable law or regime?
o: National Park — Indian Forest Act, 1927 only
Conservation reserve — Wildlife Protection Act amendment, 2002
40.x: Conservation and community reserves were provided under the Wildlife Protection Act amendment of 2002. Reserved, protected and village forests are categories under the Indian Forest Act, 1927.
40.tq: Identify the correct statute attached to each legal category.

40.s: With reference to mining near protected areas, which of the following statements is correct?
o: Mining is prohibited only within 100 metres of a National Park.
The 1 km restriction applies only to Biosphere Reserves.
The Supreme Court has barred mining within 1 km of every National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
Mining is permitted inside every National Park if approved by the State Government.
40.x: Mining is banned inside National Parks and Sanctuaries, and the Supreme Court has barred mining within 1 km of every such area unless a larger eco-sensitive zone is notified.
40.tq: Apply the legal rule to a protected-area boundary scenario.

40.s: Regeneration from stool shoots after felling, generally maintained on a short rotation for fuelwood, is known as:
40.x: Coppice regeneration arises from stool shoots after felling and is generally managed on a short rotation, particularly for fuelwood.
40.tq: Discriminate silvicultural terms by their regeneration method.

40.s: In the selection system of silviculture, the forest is maintained as:
o: A plantation harvested completely at one time
An uneven-aged forest by removing mature trees singly or in groups
An even-aged crop regenerated only by stool shoots
40.x: The selection system removes mature trees singly or in groups and maintains an uneven-aged forest.
40.tq: Apply the definition to identify the correct forest-management outcome.

40.s: A forest manager wants a long-rotation timber crop raised from seed, while avoiding complete clearance of the forest and retaining trees of different ages. Which combination of silvicultural concepts is most appropriate?
o: Village forest and protected forest classification
Coppice and short-rotation fuelwood management only
40.x: High forest provides a seed-raised, long-rotation timber crop, while the selection system retains an uneven-aged forest by removing mature trees singly or in groups.
40.tq: Combine two definitions in a practical forest-management scenario.

40.s: Jim Corbett National Park was originally established in 1936 under which name?
40.x: Jim Corbett National Park was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park and is recognised as India’s first national park.
40.tq: Use the direct year–name association for the first national park.

40.s: Keoladeo National Park, also known as Bharatpur, is located in which State?
40.x: Keoladeo National Park is situated at Bharatpur in Rajasthan and is also a Ramsar site.
40.tq: Test the protected-area–State association directly.

40.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kanha Tiger Reserve — Madhya Pradesh
2. Askot Wildlife Sanctuary — Uttarakhand
3. Palamau Tiger Reserve — Jharkhand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
40.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh, Askot is in Uttarakhand, and Palamau is in Jharkhand.
40.tq: Check each protected-area–State pair independently before selecting the code.

40.s: Madhav Tiger Reserve, recognised as India’s 58th tiger reserve, is located in which State?
40.x: Madhav Tiger Reserve is situated in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh, and is the 58th tiger reserve.
40.tq: Link the ordinal number with the corresponding reserve and State.

40.s: Which State has the highest number of tiger reserves in India?
40.x: Madhya Pradesh has 9 tiger reserves, the highest number among Indian States.
40.tq: Use the superlative State–number association.

40.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is correctly described as which of the following?
o: A constitutional body headed by the Chief Justice of India
A statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, headed by the Environment Minister
A non-statutory body headed by the Prime Minister
A statutory body under the Forest Conservation Act, 1980, headed by the Home Minister
40.x: The NTCA is a statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and is headed by the Environment Minister.
40.tq: Ask who created the body and who heads it to avoid authority-based traps.

40.s: Satkosia Tiger Reserve comprises which of the following protected areas?
o: Satkosia Gorge and Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary
Satkosia Gorge and Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary
40.x: Satkosia Tiger Reserve comprises Satkosia Gorge and Baisipalli Wildlife Sanctuary; Debrigarh is not part of its stated composition.
40.tq: Use a composition question to distinguish the correct protected-area combination from a nearby name.

40.s: Which of the following tiger reserves is located in Uttar Pradesh and forms the buffer of Corbett Tiger Reserve?
40.x: Amangarh Tiger Reserve is in Uttar Pradesh and serves as the buffer of Corbett Tiger Reserve.
40.tq: Test the reserve–State–functional relationship as a three-part association.

40.s:
Arrange the following tiger reserves in chronological order of their designation as the 56th, 57th and 58th reserves:
A. Madhav
B. Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla
C. Ratapani

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
40.x: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla was the 56th, Ratapani the 57th in 2024, and Madhav the 58th in 2025.
40.tq: Anchor the sequence to the reserve numbers before arranging the dates.

40.s: Which one of the following statements about Palamau Tiger Reserve is correct?
o: It was the 58th tiger reserve and lies in Madhya Pradesh.
It is located in Chhattisgarh and is linked to Kanha.
It was one of the original nine Project Tiger reserves and Betla National Park forms its core.
It was India's first tiger reserve, established in 1973.
40.x: Palamau in Jharkhand was one of the original nine reserves, and Betla National Park forms its core.
40.tq: Distinguish an original reserve from recently created reserves and compare their States.

40.s: Panna Tiger Reserve was declared a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in which year?
40.x: Panna became a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2020.
40.tq: Test the precise year attached to a conservation-status milestone.

40.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India had 58 Tiger Reserves as of 2026.
2. The number of Tiger Reserves increased from 9 in 1973 to 58.
3. Tiger Reserves constituted approximately 30% of India's land area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The area of Tiger Reserves was approximately 2.6% of India's land, not 30%, making statement 3 false.
40.tq: Reject the exaggerated percentage while retaining the correct count and historical comparison.

40.s: India's wild tiger population in 2022 and its approximate share of the world's wild tigers were
40.x: The tiger count rose from 1,411 in 2006 to 3,682 in 2022, over 70% of the world's wild tigers. 1,411 is the 2006 figure; the other combinations are distractors.

40.s: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary, noted as the smallest wildlife sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh, is located in:
40.x: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is in Andhra Pradesh and is noted as the State’s smallest wildlife sanctuary.
40.tq: Use the State-specific qualifying description to identify the sanctuary.

40.s: Project Cheetah was launched in India on 17 September 2022 and involved which distinctive conservation activity?
o: The world’s first intercontinental translocation of a large carnivore
The first captive breeding of the Great Indian Bustard
The first reintroduction of tigers into India
The first translocation of elephants from Africa to India
40.x: Project Cheetah was the world’s first intercontinental large-carnivore translocation and began in India on 17 September 2022.
40.tq: Link the project date to its distinctive objective rather than a generic wildlife activity.

40.s: Which of the following correctly represents the additional sites associated with the expansion of Project Cheetah after Kuno National Park?
o: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the third home and Kanha Tiger Reserve as the second
Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the second home and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve as the third
Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve as the second home and Palamau Tiger Reserve as the third
Kanha Tiger Reserve as the second home and Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary as the third
40.x: Gandhi Sagar Wildlife Sanctuary is the second home for cheetahs and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve is the third.
40.tq: Preserve the sequence of locations rather than merely recognising the names.

40.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Great Indian Bustard:
1. Its principal States mentioned are Rajasthan and Gujarat.
2. Its population is fewer than 150 birds.
3. The Supreme Court’s 2024 position retained underground power lines in priority habitats and allowed bird diverters elsewhere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: All three statements are correct. The Great Indian Bustard is associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat, numbers fewer than 150, and is protected through the modified power-line directions.
40.tq: Check the species range, numerical estimate and modified legal measure separately.

40.s: The Great Indian Bustard power-line case before the Supreme Court is identified as:
o: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India
Wildlife First v. State of Rajasthan
T.N. Godavarman v. Union of India
M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India
40.x: The case is M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India. It concerned measures to reduce power-line threats to the Great Indian Bustard.
40.tq: Use the exact litigant name and case title as the discriminating fact.

40.s: The first artificial-insemination breeding of the Great Indian Bustard was conducted at:
40.x: The first artificial-insemination breeding of the Great Indian Bustard was conducted at Jaisalmer.
40.tq: Test the specific location associated with the conservation intervention.

40.s: The “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” campaign claimed the planting of approximately how many saplings?
40.x: The campaign claimed that 140 crore saplings had been planted.
40.tq: Use numerical discrimination among closely related figures.

40.s: Which one of the following best describes the dominant natural vegetation and principal forest tract of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Tropical evergreen forests, with the Eastern Ghats as the largest forest tract
Alpine forests, with the Papikonda hills as the biggest forest tract
Mangrove forests, with the Godavari delta as the biggest forest tract
Dry deciduous forests, with Nallamala as the biggest forest tract
40.x: Andhra Pradesh forests are mainly dry deciduous, and Nallamala is the biggest forest tract in the State.
40.tq: Use the paired identification of vegetation type and major forest tract.

40.s: The proposed translocation programme for Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) includes
o: gaur from Maharashtra and tigresses from Gujarat and Rajasthan
gaur from Central India and tigresses from Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh
elephants from Central India and lions from Gujarat
blackbuck from Madhya Pradesh and tigers from Karnataka
40.x: The plan proposes bringing gaur from Central India and tigresses from Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh to NSTR.
40.tq: Match each species with its stated source region.

40.s:
Consider the following statements about protected areas in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The State has three National Parks.
2. It has thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries.
3. It has one Tiger Reserve and one Biosphere Reserve.
4. The Koundinya Elephant Reserve is also located in the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
40.x: Andhra Pradesh has three National Parks, thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries, one Tiger Reserve, one Biosphere Reserve and the Koundinya Elephant Reserve.
40.tq: Verify every numerical and categorical component before choosing the inclusive option.

40.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the three National Parks of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Sri Venkateswara was the first, Rajiv Gandhi is the largest and Papikonda is the smallest.
Rajiv Gandhi was the first, Sri Venkateswara is the largest and Papikonda is the smallest.
Sri Venkateswara was the first, Papikonda is the largest and Rajiv Gandhi is the smallest.
Papikonda was the first, Rajiv Gandhi is the largest and Sri Venkateswara is the smallest.
40.x: Sri Venkateswara National Park was the first, established in 1989; Papikonda is the largest and Rajiv Gandhi is the smallest among the three.
40.tq: Test a three-way comparison using first, largest and smallest attributes.

40.s: Which of the following environmental issues is associated with the Satpura–Melghat tiger corridor?
o: Translocation of gaur from Central India
Expansion of mangrove vegetation into the corridor
Eviction of tribal communities by a biosphere-reserve order
Construction of railway lines through the corridor
40.x: Railway lines have been identified as cutting through the Satpura–Melghat tiger corridor.
40.tq: Associate the infrastructure activity with its ecological impact.

40.s: The Supreme Court-ordered eviction in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve has raised concerns primarily relating to
40.x: The eviction issue in Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve has raised concerns regarding tribal rights.
40.tq: Identify the social dimension linked to a conservation action.

40.s: As per ISFR 2023, Andhra Pradesh's forest cover (VDF + MDF + OF) is about 30,085 sq km. The figure of 38,436.58 sq km (23.59%) sometimes quoted is wrong as 'forest cover' because it
o: adds tree cover outside recorded forests
adds about 8,351.62 sq km of scrub, which ISFR does not count as forest cover
40.x: 38,436.58 sq km = 30,084.96 sq km of forest cover + 8,351.62 sq km of scrub. Scrub (canopy below 10%) is not forest cover in ISFR, so the right figure is about 30,085 sq km (~18.46%). The other options do not account for the difference.
40.tq: AP forest cover ~30,085 sq km; scrub is not forest cover.

41.s:
With reference to protected areas under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, consider the following statements:
1. A National Park provides the highest degree of protection among the categories listed.
2. Grazing and private rights are not permitted in a National Park.
3. Some activities and rights may be regulated but allowed in a Wildlife Sanctuary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: National Parks provide the highest protection, with no grazing or private rights. Wildlife Sanctuaries permit some regulated activities and rights; hence all three statements are correct.
41.tq: Combine closely related provisions and identify the option containing all correct statements.

41.s: A Conservation Reserve under Section 36A of the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, is generally established on:
o: Land located exclusively inside a National Park
Government-owned land adjoining or linking protected areas
Any urban land notified by a municipal body
Private land volunteered by a community
41.x: A Conservation Reserve is declared by the State on government-owned land next to or linking protected areas, after consultation with local people.
41.tq: Test the location and ownership condition attached to a statutory category.

41.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding Conservation Reserves?
o: Declared by the State; local rights remain unaffected; managed through committees involving panchayats
Declared by local communities; all customary rights are extinguished
Declared only by the Union Government; grazing is automatically prohibited
Declared by the State on private land; the land must be outside all protected areas
41.x: Conservation Reserves are declared by the State on government land, local rights remain unaffected, and management committees include panchayats. Private or community land is relevant to Community Reserves.
41.tq: Use ownership, authority and rights as separate elimination clues.

41.s: A Community Reserve differs from a Conservation Reserve in that a Community Reserve is declared on:
o: Land acquired compulsorily by the Union Government
Private or community land voluntarily offered by the community
Wetlands situated within a National Park
Government land adjoining a National Park
41.x: A Community Reserve is established by the State on private or community land voluntarily offered by the community. Its rights remain unaffected, and the land cannot already be inside a National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary or Conservation Reserve.
41.tq: Discriminate between the two reserve categories by comparing land ownership.

41.s: Which recent judicially noted measure applies to wetland Conservation Reserves?
o: A 1-kilometre prohibition on all tourism activities
A complete ban on local rights
41.x: The Supreme Court extended a 10-kilometre mining buffer to all wetland Conservation Reserves. This is distinct from the ordinary 1-kilometre buffer around National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries.
41.tq: Separate the exceptional buffer from the ordinary protected-area rule.

41.s: Tsarap Chu, noted as India's largest high-altitude protected area, is located in:
41.x: Tsarap Chu is in Spiti, Himachal Pradesh. It is described as India's largest high-altitude protected area and Himachal Pradesh's fifth Conservation Reserve.
41.tq: Link the protected area with its state and distinctive superlative.

41.s: According to the stated 2026 counts, the number of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries in India is respectively:
41.x: The stated counts are 109 National Parks and 573 Wildlife Sanctuaries. The figure 688 refers to the combined number of National Parks and Wildlife Sanctuaries in another cited count.
41.tq: Keep category-wise figures separate from combined totals.

41.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its stated count?
41.x: The stated counts are 127 Conservation Reserves, 75 Community Reserves, 33 Elephant Reserves and 18 Biosphere Reserves.
41.tq: Match each category with its exact count and reject the shifted figures.

41.s: According to the cited 29 July 2026 figure, Tiger Reserves span approximately what share of India’s area?
41.x: The cited figure states that Tiger Reserves span about 84,488 square kilometres, approximately 2.6 per cent of India’s area.
41.tq: Use the percentage attached to the stated area rather than confusing it with another dataset.

41.s: Which one of the following National Parks is located in Maharashtra and is associated with the Chandrapur district?
41.x: Tadoba-Andhari National Park is located in Maharashtra’s Chandrapur district and has a dry deciduous landscape.
41.tq: Use the state–district pair to identify the protected area.

41.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Corbett National Park — Shivalik-terai landscape
2. Dudhwa National Park — Terai grassland
3. Dachigam National Park — Hangul
4. Campbell Bay National Park — Tropical evergreen island forest
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
41.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Corbett lies in the Shivalik-terai landscape, Dudhwa is a terai grassland park, Dachigam is known for Hangul, and Campbell Bay has tropical evergreen island forest.
41.tq: Verify each landscape or flagship-species association before selecting the coded combination.

41.s: Pench National Park, extending across Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, is associated with which literary work?
o: Around the World in Eighty Days
41.x: Pench National Park, located in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, inspired Rudyard Kipling’s The Jungle Book.
41.tq: Link the distinctive cultural association with the geographical location.

41.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Neora Valley National Park — Kalimpong, West Bengal
41.x: Keoladeo National Park is in Bharatpur, Rajasthan, not Alwar. Sariska National Park is associated with Alwar.
41.tq: Detect the wrong location by separating the two Rajasthan parks.

41.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Balpakram National Park : Manipur
2. Betla National Park : Jharkhand
3. Pitti Bird Sanctuary : Lakshadweep
4. Corbett National Park : Uttarakhand
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
41.x: Pair 1 is wrong: Balpakram is in Meghalaya, not Manipur (PYQ 2023). Pairs 2-4 are correct: Betla is in Jharkhand, Pitti bird sanctuary is in Lakshadweep, and Corbett is in Uttarakhand (PYQ 2025). So 2, 3 and 4 only.
41.tq: Balpakram = Meghalaya (not Manipur).

41.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Musk deer — Kedarnath and Askot Wildlife Sanctuaries
41.x: Musk deer habitat includes Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary and Askot Wildlife Sanctuary in Uttarakhand. Hangul is associated with Dachigam, Barasingha with Kanha, and snow leopard with Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve and Kibber.
41.tq: Start with the sure species-habitat pair and eliminate the swapped associations.

41.s: The Great Indian Bustard is associated with which of the following protected-area pairs?
o: Desert National Park and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary
Kanha National Park and Dachigam National Park
Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve and Kibber
Kedarnath Wildlife Sanctuary and Askot Wildlife Sanctuary
41.x: The Great Indian Bustard is protected in Desert National Park of Rajasthan and Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh.
41.tq: Match a species with both of its listed habitats rather than selecting a single familiar site.

41.s:
With reference to the Great Indian Bustard, consider the following statements:
1. Its population is less than 150.
2. Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary is one of its habitats.
3. A 2024 Supreme Court order concerned underground power lines in relation to its conservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
41.x: The Great Indian Bustard population is stated to be below 150, Rollapadu is one of its habitats, and the 2024 Supreme Court order addressed underground power lines for its conservation.
41.tq: Test numerical, geographical and legal dimensions of one conservation issue together.

41.s: Barasingha is associated with:
41.x: Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh is the protected-area habitat listed for Barasingha.
41.tq: Use nearby protected-area names as plausible wildlife distractors.

41.s: The snow leopard is associated with which of the following?
o: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve and Kibber
Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary and Desert National Park
Dachigam National Park and Binsar Wildlife Sanctuary
Kanha National Park and Sitanadi Wildlife Sanctuary
41.x: The listed habitats of the snow leopard are the Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve and Kibber.
41.tq: Test a paired habitat association using two precise locations.

41.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
41.x: Mahuadanr Wildlife Sanctuary is in Latehar district of Jharkhand, not Almora in Uttarakhand. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
41.tq: Find the wrong district-state combination rather than merely identifying a familiar sanctuary.

41.s: India's first bird sanctuary is
41.x: Vedanthangal in Tamil Nadu is India's first bird sanctuary (PYQ 2024). Keoladeo is a national park and Ramsar site, Nelapattu is AP's smallest WLS, and Pitti is a bird sanctuary in Lakshadweep.
41.tq: First bird sanctuary = Vedanthangal (TN).

41.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of the first, largest and smallest Biosphere Reserves of India?
o: Nilgiri; Great Rann of Kutch; Dibru-Saikhowa
Nilgiri; Dibru-Saikhowa; Great Rann of Kutch
Dibru-Saikhowa; Great Rann of Kutch; Nilgiri
Great Rann of Kutch; Nilgiri; Dibru-Saikhowa
41.x: Nilgiri was India’s first Biosphere Reserve, Great Rann of Kutch is the largest, and Dibru-Saikhowa is the smallest.
41.tq: Separate the three superlatives before matching each with its reserve.

41.s: Which Biosphere Reserve became India's first high-altitude cold desert Biosphere Reserve in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2025?
41.x: The Cold Desert BR was added to the WNBR in 2025 as India's first high-altitude cold desert BR. Nilgiri (1986) was India's first BR, Nanda Devi followed in 1988, and Great Rann of Kutch is the largest.
41.tq: Cold Desert BR -> WNBR 2025.

41.s: Khangchendzonga National Park was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in which year?
41.x: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 and is a mixed World Heritage Site.
41.tq: Distinguish the inscription year from the biosphere-reserve recognition year.

41.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Great Himalayan National Park — Himachal Pradesh — 2014
41.x: The Western Ghats World Heritage property extends across four States (Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra), not seven. It was inscribed in 2012.
41.tq: Check both the geographical extent and the inscription year in the long pair.
