66.tq: Identify the classification from its distinguishing physical traits.

66.s: The description ‘yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height’ refers to which racial type?
66.x: Yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high cheek bones, sparse hair and medium height are characteristic descriptions associated with the Mongoloid type.
66.tq: Discriminate between racial types by their distinctive physical descriptions.

66.s: The Negrito racial type is generally associated with which one of the following sets of traits?
o: Yellowish complexion, sparse hair and broad head
Dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and broad flat nose
Fair complexion, light eyes and tall stature
Olive-brown skin, straight hair and high nasal bridge
66.x: The Negrito type is described by dark skin, woolly or frizzy hair, short stature and a broad flat nose.
66.tq: Use a direct physical-trait identification question.

66.s:
With reference to racial types, consider the following statements:
1. Proto-Australoids are associated with dark skin, wavy hair and a long head.
2. Nordic people are generally tall, fair, long-headed and light-eyed.
3. Dravidians, in Risley's classification, are associated with a long head, broad nose and dark complexion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: All three statements correctly describe the listed racial types. Proto-Australoids have dark skin and wavy hair; Nordic people are tall and fair; and Risley's Dravidian type has a long head, broad nose and dark complexion.
66.tq: Check each statement against the associated physical traits.

66.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cephalic index?
o: Maximum length divided by maximum breadth, multiplied by 100
Maximum breadth divided by maximum length, multiplied by 100
Stature divided by head length, multiplied by 100
Nasal breadth divided by nasal length, multiplied by 100
66.x: Cephalic index is calculated as (maximum breadth / maximum length) × 100.
66.tq: Recall the exact formula rather than the reversed ratio.

66.s: A person has a nasal index of 86. Under the stated classification, this person would belong to which nasal category?
66.x: Platyrrhine refers to a broad nose with a nasal index of 85 or above. Leptorrhine is below 70 and mesorrhine is 70–84.9.
66.tq: Apply the numerical boundary to the category instead of recalling labels alone.

66.s: According to Topinard's stature classification, which one of the following is correct?
o: Tall means 180 cm or more and small means under 170 cm
Tall means 170 cm or more and small means under 160 cm
Tall means 175 cm or more and small means under 165 cm
Tall means 160 cm or more and small means under 150 cm
66.x: Topinard classified a stature of 170 cm or more as tall and a stature under 160 cm as small.
66.tq: Recall the exact cut-off values and avoid shifting both limits upward.

66.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched in the Caucasoid, Mongoloid and Negroid comparison?
o: Caucasoid—high bridge and narrow nose; Mongoloid—low to medium bridge; Negroid—low bridge and broad nose
Caucasoid—woolly hair; Mongoloid—wavy hair; Negroid—straight coarse hair
Caucasoid—high B blood group; Mongoloid—both A and B; Negroid—more A than B
Caucasoid—vertical eye fold; Mongoloid—occasional lateral fold; Negroid—medial epicanthic fold
66.x: Caucasoids have a high nasal bridge and narrow nose, Mongoloids a low-to-medium bridge, and Negroids a low bridge and broad nose. The other options interchange hair, blood-group or eye features.
66.tq: Start with the distinctive nose comparison and eliminate swapped traits.

66.s: Which racial group is associated with straight, coarse hair described as leiotrichi?
66.x: Straight, coarse hair, termed leiotrichi, is associated with the Mongoloid group. Woolly or frizzy hair, termed ulotrichi, is associated with the Negroid group.
66.tq: Distinguish the similar hair classifications by their exact technical terms.

66.s: The cephalic index of a living person is 83. Under the standard classification, this head type is:
66.x: For a living head, a cephalic index of 82 and above is brachycephalic (round-headed), 77-81.99 is mesocephalic and 76.99 and below is dolichocephalic (long-headed), so 83 is brachycephalic. Platyrrhine is a nasal-index class (85 and above), not a head type.
66.tq: Living head CI: ≤76.99 dolicho, 77-81.99 meso, ≥82 brachy.

66.s: With reference to Risley’s classification, the term ‘Dravidian’ is associated with:
o: The Himalayan and north-eastern hills only
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands only
North-west India and the Punjab only
66.x: Risley used ‘Dravidian’ for South India and Chota Nagpur. In linguistic usage, however, Dravidian properly denotes a language family.
66.tq: Distinguish Risley’s geographical racial label from the later linguistic meaning of Dravidian.

66.s: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for which census and wrote which book?
o: Census of 1931; The Races of India
Census of 1901; The People of India
Census of 1881; The Tribes of India
66.x: H.H. Risley was the Census Commissioner for 1901 and wrote The People of India, published in 1908.
66.tq: Link the official position, census year and book title in one recall unit.

66.s: H.H. Risley is particularly associated with which one of the following ideas?
66.x: Risley was the exponent of the racial theory of caste, which treats caste as a by-product of racial difference.
66.tq: Identify the scholar by his characteristic theory.

66.s: Which one of the following Risley racial types is associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier Province?
66.x: The Turko-Iranian type was associated with Baluchistan and the North-West Frontier region.
66.tq: Match the regional distribution with the correct Risley type.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched under Risley's classification?
o: Dravidian — South India, Chota Nagpur and central India
66.x: Punjab, Rajasthan and Kashmir were associated with the Indo-Aryan type. Scytho-Dravidian was associated with western India, including Maharashtra, Saurashtra and Coorg.
66.tq: Use the region swap trap to identify the incorrectly matched pair.

66.s: Paniyans and Santals are cited as examples of which Risley racial type?
66.x: Paniyans and Santals are cited as representative examples of the Dravidian type in Risley's classification.
66.tq: Recall representative populations rather than relying only on regional clues.

66.s: H.H. Risley used which anthropometric measure mainly to rank castes during the 1901 ethnographic survey?
66.x: Risley mainly used the nasal index in his anthropometric ranking of castes.
66.tq: Separate Risley’s nasal index from Sarkar’s cephalic index and Haddon’s hair-form basis.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about Risley's dictum:
1. It stated that the social status of a caste varied inversely with its nasal index.
2. It treated a higher nasal index as necessarily indicating higher social status.
3. It is now rejected as colonial race science.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Risley’s dictum stated an inverse relationship, not that a higher nasal index indicated higher social status.
66.tq: Watch for the reversed-comparison trap in the second statement.

66.s: Haddon's classification of world populations was primarily based on
66.x: Haddon used hair form as the main basis, distinguishing leiotrichi, cymotrichi and ulotrichi.
66.tq: Use the basis-of-classification clue to distinguish competing anthropologists.

66.s: Eickstedt's classification proposed which of the following four main groups?
o: Leiotr ichi, cymotrichi, ulotrichi and dolichocephalic
66.x: Eickstedt proposed the four main groups Weddid, Melanid, Indid and Mongolid on physical and regional criteria.
66.tq: Recall the exact four-member classification list.

66.s: J.H. Hutton described India as having been peopled by
o: a single population with no migration
racial groups confined exclusively to river valleys
only one migration from Central Asia
66.x: J.H. Hutton, the Census Commissioner in 1931, described India as peopled by successive waves of migration.
66.tq: Match the scholar with the central proposition of his classification or description.

66.s: S.S. Sarkar identified six ethnic elements primarily on the basis of the
66.x: S.S. Sarkar used the cephalic index and identified six ethnic elements, including dolichocephals and others.
66.tq: Discriminate between the cephalic index of Sarkar and the nasal index used by Risley.

66.s: According to Griffith Taylor's migration-zone theory, primitive races are pushed towards
o: the periphery, such as the Andaman Islands
66.x: Griffith Taylor's theory holds that primitive races are pushed to peripheral areas, with the Andaman Islands cited as an example.
66.tq: Apply the peripheral-location principle to the example given.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Western Brachycephals — Gujarat, Bengal, Odisha and Coorg
Negrito — Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain
Mediterranean — Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain
66.x: The Negrito type is associated mainly with the Andaman Islands and traces in the southern hills. Punjab, Rajasthan and the Ganga plain are associated with the Mediterranean type, while Punjab and Rajasthan are also linked with the Nordic type.
66.tq: Find the geographical association that does not belong to the racial type.

66.s: The Parsis have been placed under which racial type and sub-type respectively?
66.x: The Parsis are associated with the Western Brachycephal group and are identified with the Armenoid sub-type.
66.tq: Use the community-subtype pairing to avoid confusing broad racial groups with their sub-types.

66.s: Which one of the following combinations represents the principal sub-types of the Western Brachycephal group?
66.x: Alpinoid, Dinaric and Armenoid are the sub-types associated with the Western Brachycephal group.
66.tq: Separate sub-type lists from representative tribal communities.

66.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Group)
a. Negrito
b. Proto-Australoid
c. Mongoloid
d. Nordic

List-II (Representative peoples or region)
i. Nagas, Lepchas, Tibetans of Sikkim and Shompen
 ii. Onge, Jarawa, Great Andamanese and Sentinelese
 iii. Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho
 iv. Punjab, Rajasthan and the North-West Frontier

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: Negrito corresponds to the Andaman communities; Proto-Australoid to Santhal, Bhil, Chenchu, Munda and Ho; Mongoloid to the Himalayan and north-eastern peoples; and Nordic to north-western India.
66.tq: Start from the sure community-region pairs and eliminate codes containing a repeated mismatch.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about B.S. Guha's classification:
1. It was based on 1931 Census data.
2. It identified seven main racial groups.
3. It is the most widely cited classification of the Indian population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Guha gave 6 main racial groups with 9 sub-types; seven types belong to Risley. So B; A misses 3, C and D include the false 2.
66.tq: Guha: 1931 Census, 6 groups, 9 sub-types. Risley: 7 types.

66.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched under B.S. Guha's classification?
o: Western Brachycephals — Alpinoid, Dinaric and Armenoid
Proto-Australoid — Munda, Santhal, Oraon, Bhil and Chenchu
66.x: Kadar and Irula are associated with the Negrito group. The Nordic group was associated with the north-west frontier and Punjab.
66.tq: Identify the representative population assigned to the wrong racial group.

66.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Guha's Mongoloid group are correct?
1. It was divided into Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid.
2. Palaeo-Mongoloid included long-headed and broad-headed forms.
3. Tibeto-Mongoloid was associated with Sikkim and Bhutan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Guha divided the Mongoloid group into Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid. Palaeo-Mongoloid included long- and broad-headed forms, while Tibeto-Mongoloid was associated with Sikkim and Bhutan.
66.tq: Test the internal division, physical description and regional association together.

66.s: Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental are sub-types of which one of Guha's racial groups?
66.x: The Mediterranean group was divided into Palaeo-Mediterranean, Mediterranean and Oriental. The Oriental sub-type was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan.
66.tq: Match the sub-type cluster with its parent group.

66.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
66.x: The Oriental sub-type of Guha's Mediterranean group was associated with Punjab and Rajasthan. Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Parsis are associated with Armenoid.
66.tq: Start with the sure regional pair and reject representatives belonging to other sub-types.

66.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the representative populations of the Palaeo-Mongoloid and Tibeto-Mongoloid sub-types, respectively?
o: Sema Nagas and Lepchas; Tibetans of Sikkim
Kadars and Irulas; Santhals and Bhils
66.x: Sema Nagas and Lepchas are examples of Palaeo-Mongoloid, while Tibetans of Sikkim represent Tibeto-Mongoloid. The latter are described as having a massive head, tall stature and light-brown skin.
66.tq: Use representative populations to discriminate between the two Mongoloid sub-types.

66.s: The racial element generally associated with the tribal groups of north-eastern India is:
66.x: The tribal groups of the north-eastern hills and forests are generally associated with the Mongoloid racial element.
66.tq: Apply the region-to-racial-element association for the north-eastern hills.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Andaman tribal population is associated with the Negrito stock.
2. Negrito is regarded as a sub-race of the Negroid group.
3. The Nicobar Shompen are classified as Negrito.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Shompen of Nicobar are Mongoloid, not Negrito, so statement 3 is false.
66.tq: Use the exception within the Andaman-Nicobar region to test a broad racial classification.

66.s: Which one of the following tribes is regarded as the standard example of the Proto-Australoid racial element in Central India?
66.x: The Santhal is the standard example of a Central Indian tribe associated with the Proto-Australoid racial element.
66.tq: Identify the representative tribe linked with the central Indian racial element.

66.s: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are generally classified under which racial group?
66.x: The Chenchus of the Nallamala region are classified as Proto-Australoid.
66.tq: Use the tribe’s regional location and standard classification together.

66.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the racial elements among tribes of South India?
1. South India has a Proto-Australoid base.
2. A Negrito strain occurs among hill foragers such as the Kadar, Irula and Paniyan.
3. Risley called the Paniyan ‘Dravidian’.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: All three statements are correct. South Indian tribal groups are described as having a Proto-Australoid base, with a Negrito strain among certain hill foragers; Risley classified the Paniyan as Dravidian.
66.tq: Check the general regional pattern first, then identify the specific exception and historical label.

66.s: The plains population of Andhra Pradesh is described as being mainly associated with which racial element?
66.x: The plains population of Andhra Pradesh is mainly associated with the Mediterranean element and is predominantly Dravidian-speaking.
66.tq: Apply the regional classification specifically to the plains population of Andhra Pradesh.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about Scheduled Tribes in Andhra Pradesh (Census 2011, as given):
1. They numbered 27.39 lakh, or 5.53% of the State's population.
2. Their sex ratio was 990.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the AP ST sex ratio was 1009 (990 is the all-India ST figure). So A; B and C wrongly accept 2, D wrongly rejects 1.
66.tq: AP STs: 26.31 lakh, 5.3%, sex ratio 1009.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the Anthropological Survey of India:
1. It was founded in 1945 at Kolkata.
2. It is a subordinate office of the Ministry of Culture.
3. B.S. Guha was its first Director.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AnSI was founded at Varanasi in 1945 and moved to Kolkata in 1948. So B; A, C and D include the false 1.
66.tq: AnSI: Varanasi 1945 -> Kolkata 1948; Ministry of Culture; Guha first Director.

66.s: The principal role of the Anthropological Survey of India is to undertake research and documentation relating to
o: physical and cultural anthropology of communities
only linguistic surveys of urban populations
66.x: AnSI undertakes research and documentation in physical and cultural anthropology, including the study of communities.
66.tq: Identify the organisation from its functional mandate.

66.s:
Consider the following statements about the People of India project:
1. It was launched in 1985 under K.S. Singh.
2. It documented about 4,635 communities.
3. It is cited mainly as a reference for enumerating religious minorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it is cited as a reference for caste and DNT enumeration. So B; A misses 2, C and D include the false 3.
66.tq: People of India: 1985, K.S. Singh, 4,635 communities, caste/DNT reference.

66.s: Which one of the following is NOT a regional centre of the Anthropological Survey of India?
66.x: Jagdalpur is a sub-regional centre, not one of the seven regional centres. The regional centres include Port Blair, Shillong and Udaipur.
66.tq: Find the one item belonging to the neighbouring category rather than the main list.

66.s:
Which of the following recent developments is correctly matched?

1. Rakhigarhi skeletons — handed to AnSI Kolkata for study
2. Unclassified DNT communities — 268 classified in an AnSI study for NITI Aayog
3. People of India project — launched in 1931

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The People of India project was launched in 1985, not 1931.
66.tq: Use the year trap to separate the correct recent developments from the false historical association.

66.s: Which one of the following best explains the modern criticism of rigid racial classification?
o: Physical traits provide an objective and complete basis for classifying all populations.
All humans belong to different species based on visible traits.
Genetic studies have confirmed the permanence of colonial racial categories.
Human beings share over 99% of their genetic material and belong to one species, Homo sapiens.
66.x: Modern evidence shows that humans share over 99% of their genetic material and all belong to Homo sapiens, making rigid racial divisions scientifically subjective.
66.tq: Choose the precise scientific proposition over absolute claims about race.

66.s: The older racial schemes of India have been criticised primarily because they relied heavily on
o: visible physical traits and colonial ethnography
66.x: Older schemes relied on visible traits and colonial ethnography. Risley's race-caste theory is now rejected.
66.tq: Identify the stated basis of the criticised classification rather than its later scientific alternative.

66.s:
With reference to the ancestry of most Indians, consider the following statements:
1. Most Indians are understood to descend from a mixture of ANI and ASI.
2. ANI refers to Ancestral North Indians.
3. ASI refers to Ancestral South Indians.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
66.x: The 2009 genetic research framework describes most Indians as having mixed ANI and ASI ancestry; the abbreviations mean Ancestral North Indians and Ancestral South Indians.
66.tq: Expand abbreviations and verify the relationship stated in each sentence.

66.s: A 2026 comparison of tribal groups with their genome-verified relatives who had moved to cities found differences mainly in their
66.x: The study found differences in gut microbiomes, suggesting that environment rather than genes accounted for the observed difference.
66.tq: Distinguish the recent biological finding from older anthropometric measures.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Risley's classification has seven types.
2. Guha's classification has six groups.
3. Only Risley's classification lists Negrito and Proto-Australoid as separate groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: only Guha lists Negrito and Proto-Australoid separately. So B; A misses 2, C and D include the false 3.
66.tq: Risley 7, Guha 6; Negrito + Proto-Australoid separate only in Guha.

66.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. India ratified ICERD in 1968.
2. The UN CERD recently reviewed India for the first time since 2007.
3. India accepted CERD's observations and agreed that caste is a form of race.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
66.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: India argues caste is not race and rejected the observations as 'politically motivated'. So B; A misses 2, C and D include the false 3.
66.tq: ICERD 1968; CERD review first since 2007; India: caste is not race.

66.s: The Supreme Court was asked to consider treating racial slurs against North-Easterners as a hate crime after the killing of
66.x: The plea followed the killing of Anjel Chakma and concerned racial prejudice and slurs against people from the North-East.
66.tq: Link the legal-development scenario with the correct named individual.

66.s: Rakhigarhi DNA findings have challenged Aryan-invasion ideas because they showed no evidence of a
66.x: The Rakhigarhi DNA findings showed no “Steppe Pastoralist” gene, challenging certain Aryan-invasion interpretations.
66.tq: Use the specific genetic finding to identify the challenged theory.

67.s: According to Census 2011 figures given for India, which religious community constituted the largest minority?
67.x: Muslims constituted 14.2 percent of India's population according to the cited Census 2011 figures and were the largest minority community.
67.tq: Use the comparative phrase “largest minority” rather than selecting the largest overall community.

67.s: Which of the following correctly gives the Census 2011 shares of Buddhists and Jains in India?
67.x: The cited shares are 0.7 percent for Buddhists and 0.4 percent for Jains.
67.tq: Discriminate between two close minority-population percentages by checking their exact order.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Punjab is correct?
o: Punjab has the largest concentration of Jains, and Dalits constitute about 14.2 percent of its population.
Punjab has the largest concentration of Buddhists, and Dalits constitute about 79.8 percent of its population.
Punjab has the largest concentration of Ravidassias, and Dalits constitute about 2.3 percent of its population.
Punjab has the largest concentration of Ravidassias, and Dalits constitute about 32 percent of its population.
67.x: Punjab is identified as having the largest concentration of Ravidassias, while Dalits constitute about 32 percent of its population.
67.tq: Combine the correct location and percentage instead of accepting a swapped community or figure.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the religious composition of India according to Census 2011.
List-I (Religion)
A. Muslim
B. Christian
C. Sikh
D. Jain
List-II (Share)
1. 14.2%
2. 2.3%
3. 1.7%
4. 0.4%
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
67.x: Muslims constituted 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7% and Jains 0.4% of the population.
67.tq: Start from the sure percentage pair and eliminate codes containing a misplaced share.

67.s:
Arrange the following religious communities in ascending order of population according to Census 2011:
A. Christian
B. Jain
C. Hindu
D. Buddhist
E. Muslim
F. Sikh
o: B, D, F, A, E, C
D, B, F, A, E, C
B, F, D, A, C, E
F, B, D, A, E, C
67.x: The ascending order is Jain, Buddhist, Sikh, Christian, Muslim and Hindu.
67.tq: Arrange population categories from the smallest to the largest using the stated figures.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the population of Muslims in India according to Census 2011?
67.x: The correct Muslim population figure was 17.22 crore, or 172.2 million. The figure 12.22 crore is an erroneous printed value.
67.tq: Reject a typographical-looking distractor by checking the precise population figure.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the classification of religions in Census 2011:
1. Six major religions were counted separately.
2. Other Religions and Persuasions was recorded separately.
3. Religion Not Stated was recorded separately.
4. A ‘No Religion’ option was added for the first time in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All four statements are correct. The six major religions, ORP, Religion Not Stated and the newly added No Religion option were separately recognised in the stated Census classification.
67.tq: Check whether each component of the classification has been included.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly states the Christian population and share in India according to Census 2011?
67.x: The Christian population was 2.78 crore, or 27.8 million, constituting 2.3% of India's population.
67.tq: Match the absolute population figure with its corresponding percentage share.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the change in the Muslim share of India's population between 2001 and 2011?
67.x: The Muslim share increased from 13.4% in 2001 to 14.2% in 2011.
67.tq: Distinguish the direction of change and avoid reversing the two endpoint figures.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding changes in religious shares between 2001 and 2011:
1. Christian and Jain shares remained unchanged.
2. Sikh share declined by 0.2 percentage points.
3. Buddhist share declined by 0.1 percentage points.
4. Hindu share rose above 80%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: the Hindu share fell from 80.5% to 79.8%, below 80%.
67.tq: Find the flipped trend statement among otherwise accurate change figures.

67.s: With reference to the first detailed census of 1881, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Religions of Indian origin formed about 79% of the population, and about 95% of them were Hindus.
Religions of Indian origin formed about 95% of the population, and about 79% of them were Hindus.
Religions of Indian origin formed less than 50% of the population.
Christians formed about 7% of the population.
67.x: The 1881 census recorded religions of Indian origin at about 79% of the population; approximately 95% of that group was Hindu. Christians constituted about 0.7%.
67.tq: Keep the population share and the internal proportion distinct.

67.s: A community had a population of approximately 27.8 million in 2011, after rising from 10.7 million in 1961. Which community does this describe?
67.x: The figures describe the Christian population: about 10.7 million in 1961 and 27.8 million in 2011.
67.tq: Use the beginning and ending values as identifying anchors in a population-series question.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the approximate 2011 population of the three communities listed?
o: Sikhs — 27.8 million; Buddhists — 20.8 million; Jains — 8.4 million
Sikhs — 8.4 million; Buddhists — 4.5 million; Jains — 20.8 million
Sikhs — 20.8 million; Buddhists — 8.4 million; Jains — 4.5 million
Sikhs — 4.5 million; Buddhists — 20.8 million; Jains — 8.4 million
67.x: The approximate 2011 populations were Sikhs 20.8 million, Buddhists 8.4 million and Jains 4.5 million.
67.tq: Match each community with its distinct reference magnitude and reject shifted figures.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the long-run change in the religious shares of India's population?
o: The Sikh share has risen continuously while the Buddhist share has doubled.
The Hindu share has slowly declined, the Muslim share has steadily risen, and Sikh and Buddhist shares have dipped.
The Hindu share has risen rapidly and the Muslim share has declined steadily.
All major religious shares have remained unchanged over the decades.
67.x: The Hindu share has slowly declined, the Muslim share has steadily risen, and the Sikh and Buddhist shares have dipped over the long run.
67.tq: Compare trends together instead of judging any one community in isolation.

67.s: According to Census 2011, which religious community recorded the highest decadal growth rate during 2001-11?
67.x: Muslims grew 24.6% in 2001-11, the highest and the only community faster than the national rate (APPSC 2025 key). Hindus grew 16.8% and Christians 15.5%, while Jains grew 5.4%, the lowest of all.
67.tq: Highest growth 2001-11 = Muslims 24.6%; lowest = Jains 5.4%.

67.s: The sex ratio of the Sikh community in Census 2011 was:
67.x: Sikhs recorded the lowest sex ratio among the listed communities, at 903 females per 1,000 males.
67.tq: Recall the exact extreme figure rather than merely the community ranking.

67.s: Which religious community recorded the highest literacy rate in Census 2011?
67.x: Jains recorded the highest literacy rate among the listed religious communities.
67.tq: Identify the maximum entry in a comparison ranking.

67.s: Which one of the following is the correct order of religious communities from highest to lowest literacy rate in Census 2011?
o: Christian > Jain > Buddhist > Sikh > Muslim > Hindu
Muslim > Hindu > Sikh > Buddhist > Christian > Jain
Jain > Buddhist > Christian > Hindu > Sikh > Muslim
Jain > Christian > Buddhist > Sikh > Hindu > Muslim
67.x: The literacy ranking was Jain, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, Hindu and Muslim, in descending order.
67.tq: Compare all entries in the stated order and eliminate any reversed ranking.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly gives the sex-ratio order from highest to lowest among the listed religious communities in 2011?
o: Jains, Christians, Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs
Christians, Buddhists, Jains, Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs
Christians, Jains, Buddhists, Muslims, Hindus, Sikhs
Buddhists, Christians, Muslims, Jains, Hindus, Sikhs
67.x: The order was Christians (1,023), Buddhists (965), Jains (954), Muslims (951), Hindus (939) and Sikhs (903). Sikhs had the lowest sex ratio among these communities.
67.tq: Arrange the numerical values from highest to lowest and check adjacent comparisons.

67.s: What was the national average sex ratio in India in 2011 as given in the religious comparison?
67.x: The national average sex ratio in 2011 was 943. The figures for individual communities ranged from 903 among Sikhs to 1,023 among Christians.
67.tq: Distinguish the national benchmark from the community-specific figures.

67.s: The relatively high literacy and slow growth associated with Jains is linked in the comparison to their being predominantly:
67.x: Jains are described as mostly urban and commercial. This profile is associated with their top literacy and slowest growth.
67.tq: Connect the social-economic profile with the demographic indicators given.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the State with the largest number of persons of a minority community in India:
1. Kerala has the largest number of Christians.
2. Maharashtra has the largest number of Buddhists.
3. Gujarat has the largest number of Jains.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
67.x: Statement 1 is correct: Kerala has the largest number of Christians, though Christians are a majority only in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya. Statement 2 is correct: Maharashtra has the most Buddhists, following Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur (1956). Statement 3 is wrong: Maharashtra, not Gujarat, has the largest number of Jains. So '1 and 2 only' is right; '1 only' misses statement 2, and the options with statement 3 are wrong.
67.tq: Largest NUMBER differs from majority/highest SHARE: Christians-Kerala, Buddhists and Jains-Maharashtra.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Sikh concentration — Punjab, Haryana and Delhi
67.x: Jains are concentrated mainly in urban Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra, not Coastal Andhra. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
67.tq: Find the one geographically misplaced concentration region.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious composition of India:
1. Buddhists form the highest share of the population in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
2. Sikhs constitute a majority only in Punjab.
3. Jains have their highest population share in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements are correct. Buddhist share is highest in Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh; Punjab is the only Sikh-majority State; and Jain share is highest in Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat.
67.tq: Check each community against its highest share and majority status before selecting the coded combination.

67.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the majority status of religions in India?
o: Sikhs are a majority in Punjab, Haryana and Delhi.
Christians are a majority in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya.
Muslims are a majority in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
Buddhists are a majority in Maharashtra and Sikkim.
67.x: Christians are a majority in Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya. Sikhs are a majority only in Punjab, while Muslims are not a majority in Uttar Pradesh or Bihar and Buddhists do not form a majority in Maharashtra or Sikkim.
67.tq: Separate majority status from concentration or largest absolute population.

67.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Jammu and Kashmir had a Muslim majority of about 68 percent according to the 2011 Census.
2. Lakshadweep had a Muslim majority of about 97 percent.
3. Punjab had a Sikh majority of about 58 percent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: All three statements are correct according to the stated 2011 Census-based figures.
67.tq: Verify the numerical majority figures individually before choosing the coded answer.

67.s: Which one of the following statements about Arunachal Pradesh is correct?
o: Hindus are the only major religious group in the State.
Christians constitute more than 50 percent of its population.
It is the only Sikh-majority State in India.
Christians are the largest single group but constitute only about 30 percent.
67.x: Christians are the largest single religious group in Arunachal Pradesh, but they constitute only about 30 percent and therefore do not form a majority.
67.tq: Distinguish the largest single group from a group holding more than half the population.

67.s:
Assertion (A): Christians are mostly rural in India.
Reason (R): Important Christian concentrations occur in regions such as the west coast, the north-eastern hills and Chotanagpur.
Choose the correct answer.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
67.x: Both statements are true, but the listed concentration regions do not by themselves explain the predominantly rural character of Christians. The reason describes distribution areas rather than the direct explanation of the assertion.
67.tq: Separate a true supporting fact from a reason that does not directly explain the assertion.

67.s: Which of the following correctly states the fuller list of States/Union Territories where Hindus are below 50 percent, although the material notes that no other religion has a majority in some of them?
o: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Kerala, West Bengal, Punjab, Delhi, Goa and Sikkim
Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab
Jammu and Kashmir, Punjab, Nagaland, Mizoram and Meghalaya only
67.x: The fuller eight-unit list is Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Meghalaya, Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Punjab. The shorter five-State list excludes Lakshadweep, Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur.
67.tq: Handle a confusable five-versus-eight list by identifying the additional units explicitly included in the fuller version.

67.s: Which State has the largest number of Muslims in India according to Census 2011?
67.x: Uttar Pradesh has the largest Muslim population by number. Jammu and Kashmir (about 68%) and Lakshadweep (about 97%) have Muslim majorities, but a high share is not the same as the largest number; West Bengal and Kerala also have large Muslim populations but fewer than Uttar Pradesh.
67.tq: Largest number: Muslims UP, Christians Kerala, Buddhists and Jains Maharashtra.

67.s: The concentration of Buddhists in Maharashtra is particularly associated with which event?
o: The migration of Sikhs to Delhi
Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956
The arrival of Arab merchants on the western coast
The spread of Christianity by Portuguese missionaries
67.x: Maharashtra's large Buddhist population is linked to Dr B. R. Ambedkar's mass conversion at Nagpur in 1956.
67.tq: Link a distinctive demographic concentration with its stated historical cause.

67.s: Which one of the following statements regarding religious settlement patterns is correct?
o: Sikhs are concentrated mainly in the north-eastern hills.
Jains are mainly concentrated in remote hill regions.
Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods for reasons including security and cultural preservation.
Christians are predominantly urban in all concentration areas.
67.x: Muslims often live in majority neighbourhoods because of security concerns, cultural preservation and rental discrimination. Jains are associated mainly with urban trading communities, and Christians are mostly rural.
67.tq: Use the social-geographical explanation rather than merely recalling a location.

67.s: The Muslim share of India's population rose from approximately what percentage in 1951 to what percentage in 2011?
67.x: The Muslim share rose from about 10 percent in 1951 to about 14 percent in 2011.
67.tq: Recall the two benchmark percentages rather than confusing population share with absolute population.

67.s: Which factor is identified as an important explanation for the rise in the Muslim population share between 1951 and 2011?
o: Higher female education and higher economic status
A decline in the total population of India
Poorer economic status and lower female education
67.x: The rise is attributed to poorer economic status and lower female education. Muslim fertility is now falling rapidly and the fertility gap with Hindus is closing.
67.tq: Identify the stated demographic cause and distinguish it from an unsupported religious explanation.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding the historical diffusion of Islam and Christianity in India is correct?
o: Islam spread only through Portuguese missionaries.
Christianity reached India through Arab merchants and the Turkish Sultanate alone.
Islam spread through Arab merchants, the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis, while Christianity was associated with St Thomas, the Portuguese and Francis Xavier.
Both religions spread exclusively through modern urban migration.
67.x: Islam arrived with Arab merchants and later spread through the Turkish Sultanate, Mughals and Sufis. Christianity was associated with St Thomas, the Portuguese and Francis Xavier.
67.tq: Test a multi-stage historical sequence and reject exclusive wording such as 'only' and 'exclusively'.

67.s: St Thomas is associated with the arrival of Christianity in India in approximately which year?
67.x: Christianity is traditionally associated with the arrival of St Thomas in India in 52 AD. Later Portuguese activity and Francis Xavier also contributed to its spread.
67.tq: Directly test the distinctive historical date attached to a religious diffusion process.

67.s: Which pair of anti-conversion laws and years is correctly matched?
67.x: Odisha enacted an anti-conversion law in 1967 and Madhya Pradesh followed in 1968. They were the first States associated with such laws in the material.
67.tq: Start from the sure year-State pair and avoid shifting adjacent years between States.

67.s: According to Census 2011 figures for residual Andhra Pradesh, which of the following is the correct order of religious shares from highest to lowest?
67.x: In residual Andhra Pradesh, Hindus accounted for about 90.9 per cent, Muslims about 7.3 per cent and Christians about 1.4 per cent.
67.tq: Compare the percentage shares and identify the descending order.

67.s: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh was estimated at approximately how many persons in APSES 2024–25?
67.x: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh was stated as approximately 6.82 lakh in APSES 2024–25. It is concentrated in coastal districts and tribal agency areas.
67.tq: Recall the exact population figure and distinguish it from percentage shares.

67.s: The Christian population in Andhra Pradesh is concentrated mainly in:
o: The coastal districts and tribal agency areas
Only the metropolitan region of Visakhapatnam
67.x: The Christian population of Andhra Pradesh is concentrated in the coastal districts and tribal agency areas. It is not confined to Rayalaseema or a single metropolitan region.
67.tq: Use the location clue and reject options that impose an unsupported exclusive concentration.

67.s:
Which of the following statements correctly describes the minority population of Andhra Pradesh?
1. It is mostly urban.
2. It contains a large Below-Poverty-Line segment.
3. It has a low share in economic support schemes.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
67.x: All three statements correctly describe the minority population of Andhra Pradesh in APSES 2024–25: it is mostly urban, has a large Below-Poverty-Line segment and has a low share in economic support schemes.
67.tq: Test a cluster of linked social indicators without reversing their direction.

67.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the highest Muslim population shares are associated with which group of districts?
67.x: The highest Muslim shares in Andhra Pradesh are associated with the Rayalaseema districts of Kurnool, YSR Kadapa and Anantapur.
67.tq: Match the religious concentration with the correct regional district group.

67.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the central minority scholarship schemes:
1. The Pre-matric Scholarship covers Classes IX and X.
2. The Post-matric Scholarship is for students whose parental income is below Rs 2.5 lakh.
3. The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship (2007) is for professional and technical UG-PG courses.
4. The scholarships are paid through NSP 2.0 and DBT, with 50% earmarked for girls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: Pre-matric covers Classes IX-X, Post-matric has a Rs 2.5 lakh income ceiling, and Merit-cum-Means (2007) covers professional/technical UG-PG. Statement 4 is wrong: payment is through NSP 2.0 and DBT, but 30% (not 50%) is earmarked for girls. So '1, 2 and 3 only' is right; '1 and 2 only' misses 3, and the options with 4 are wrong.
67.tq: Remember 30% for girls; 2.5 lakh ceiling; MCM 2007.

67.s: Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) was formerly known as:
67.x: PMJVK was formerly called the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP).
67.tq: Discriminate between similarly associated minority welfare programmes by their former names.

67.s:
With reference to PMJVK, consider the following statements:
1. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
2. It focuses on infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas.
3. From 2022-23, it was revised to cover all districts, including 112 Aspirational Districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
67.x: PMJVK is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, supports infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas and, after revision from 2022-23, covers all districts including 112 Aspirational Districts.
67.tq: Check the scheme’s funding pattern, target area and later geographical expansion independently.

67.s: Jiyo Parsi is intended to address:
o: The educational backwardness of Urdu-speaking students
The decline of the Parsi population
The infrastructure gap in Minority Concentration Areas
67.x: Jiyo Parsi targets the decline of the Parsi population.
67.tq: Match a distinctive scheme name with its narrowly defined target group.

67.s: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body established in:
67.x: The Central Waqf Council is a statutory body dating from 1964.
67.tq: Use direct institutional year recall while separating the Council from later Waqf legislation.

67.s: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, commonly associated with UMEED, was notified and brought into force on:
o: Notified on 5 April 2025 and enforced on 8 April 2025
Notified on 8 April 2025 and enforced on 5 May 2025
Notified on 1 April 2025 and enforced on 5 April 2025
Notified on 5 May 2025 and enforced on 8 May 2025
67.x: The Act was notified on 5 April 2025 and came into force on 8 April 2025.
67.tq: Preserve the order of closely spaced notification and commencement dates.

67.s: Which one of the following is NOT a provision or associated feature mentioned in relation to the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025 and UMEED?
o: Mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of its income
Uploading property data on the UMEED portal within six months
Audit of waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh
67.x: The stated audit requirement applies to waqfs earning over ₹1 lakh; a mandatory audit of every waqf irrespective of income is not specified.
67.tq: Find the option that extends a qualified provision into an absolute one.

67.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Andhra Pradesh body/scheme)
a. AP State Minorities Finance Corporation
b. AP State Christian Minorities Finance Corporation
c. AP State Waqf Board
d. AP State Haj Committee

List-II (2024-25 fact)
i. 1,652 pilgrims approved for Haj 2025
 ii. Post-matric RTF of ₹36.34 crore to 50,767 beneficiaries
 iii. ₹10,000 per month to Imams and ₹5,000 to Mouzzans
 iv. ₹150.92 crore allocation and Jerusalem pilgrimage assistance

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
67.x: The Minorities Finance Corporation corresponds to post-matric RTF, the Christian Corporation to ₹150.92 crore and pilgrimage assistance, the Waqf Board to payments to Imams and Mouzzans, and the Haj Committee to 1,652 pilgrims.
67.tq: Start from the distinctive Haj-pilgrim and Waqf honorarium pairs, then complete the matching.

67.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with an AP minority welfare measure?
o: Urdu Academy — Free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching of ₹5 crore
Haj Committee — Free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching of ₹5 crore
Waqf Board — Christian Bhavan at Adavithakkellapadu
Christian Finance Corporation — Survey of 10,522 un-notified waqf properties
67.x: The AP State Urdu Academy provides free computer training in 36 centres and CEDM coaching involving ₹5 crore.
67.tq: Use the institutional-function match and reject cross-swapped departmental responsibilities.

67.s: The allocation for minorities in the Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27 was raised from:
67.x: The AP minority allocation was raised from ₹5,434 crore to ₹6,090 crore in the 2026-27 Budget.
67.tq: Test the direction and exact values of a budget increase.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent Andhra Pradesh minority-related measures is correct?
o: ₹1,800 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu ceased to have official status.
₹180 crore a year was allocated only to pastors, and Telugu was declared the second official language.
₹18 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the third official language.
₹180 crore a year was allocated to Imams and Mouzams, and Urdu was declared the second official language.
67.x: The annual allocation for Imams and Mouzams was stated as ₹180 crore, and Urdu was declared the second official language of Andhra Pradesh.
67.tq: Combine the correct amount with the correct language-status fact and reject altered scale or status.

67.s: Which one of the following accurately describes the status of the Uniform Civil Code in the context stated?
o: Uttarakhand’s UCC has been in force since January 2025; Bills passed by Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh await Presidential assent.
UCC has been in force in all NDA-ruled States since January 2025; no State Bills await assent.
Only Assam’s Bill awaits Presidential assent, while Uttarakhand’s UCC has not yet commenced.
Uttarakhand, Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh all implemented their UCC laws in 2024.
67.x: Uttarakhand’s UCC came into force in January 2025, while the Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh were awaiting Presidential assent.
67.tq: Separate an enacted and operative law from Bills that have only been passed and await assent.

67.s: Section 2(c) of the National Commission for Minorities Act has been criticised primarily because it:
o: Gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, despite the state-level identification approach associated with T.M.A. Pai.
Transfers all minority identification powers exclusively to State Commissions.
Requires every minority community to be identified only through a census conducted by the Supreme Court.
Prevents the Centre from notifying any minority community.
67.x: The criticism is that Section 2(c) gives the Centre unbridled power to notify minorities, whereas T.M.A. Pai is associated with state-level identification.
67.tq: Match the legal criticism with the correct authority and constitutional interpretation.

67.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relevant minority institutions and facts in Andhra Pradesh?
o: AP has only a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.28 lakh and Urdu is the third official language.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, but Urdu is not an official language and Christians number 8.62 lakh.
AP has only a Central Minorities Commission and no separate Christian Finance Corporation or Waqf Board.
AP has a State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations, and a Waqf Board; Christians number 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.x: Andhra Pradesh has the stated State Minorities Commission, separate Minorities and Christian Minorities Finance Corporations and a Waqf Board; its Christian population is 6.82 lakh and Urdu is the second official language.
67.tq: Check the complete institutional and numerical combination rather than one isolated fact.

67.s: In April 2026, the Andhra Pradesh minority cell fast-tracked DBT of post-matric scholarships. The income ceiling associated with the scheme is:
67.x: The income ceiling for the post-matric scholarship is ₹2.5 lakh, and the AP minority cell fast-tracked its DBT in April 2026.
67.tq: Apply the scheme’s income criterion to a current administrative action.

67.s: Which of the following statements regarding religious enumeration in India is correct?
o: The 2011 Census recorded the Hindu share above 80% and introduced only a ‘No Religion’ category.
The 2011 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, and it also included a ‘No Religion’ option for the first time.
The 2001 Census was the first in which the Hindu share fell below 80%, but it did not include a ‘No Religion’ option.
The 2021 Census was the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80%.
67.x: The year 2011 marked both the first census in which the Hindu share fell below 80% and the first inclusion of a ‘No Religion’ option.
67.tq: Combine two first-occurrence facts tied to the same census year.

67.s: The Census 2027 enumeration schedule includes which of the following?
o: Only the six notified religions, without any parental information
The six religions plus ‘other religion’, along with the religion and birthplace of both parents
Only ‘No Religion’ and ‘Other Religion’, along with the birthplace of grandparents
The six religions plus caste, but no question on birthplace
67.x: The Census 2027 schedule lists the six religions and ‘other religion’, and asks the religion and birthplace of both parents.
67.tq: Watch for omissions and substitutions in a list-based enumeration question.

67.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the two debates mentioned in relation to religious minorities?
o: The ‘demography’ narrative versus literacy data; and the over-representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus fertility data; and the low representation of religious minorities in higher-judiciary appointments.
The ‘migration’ narrative versus rainfall data; and the absence of minorities from all courts.
The ‘demography’ narrative versus urbanisation data; and the representation of minorities exclusively in local courts.
67.x: The debates include the demography narrative in relation to fertility data and the fact that religious minorities constitute only about 5% of higher-judiciary appointees.
67.tq: Match each debate with its correct comparison and avoid reversing the representation claim.

67.s: Which notified minority community is the latest among the following, with notification in 2014?
67.x: Jains were notified as a minority community in 2014 and are the latest notified minority among the communities mentioned.
67.tq: Use chronology and distinguish the latest notified community from older notified groups.

67.s: Who was appointed Chairperson of the National Commission for Minorities for a full three-year term in July 2026?
67.x: Harjit Singh Grewal was appointed NCM Chairperson for a full three-year term in July 2026. T.M.A. Pai is the Supreme Court case on State-level identification of minorities, Virginius Xaxa chaired the 2013 committee on tribal status, and K.S. Singh led AnSI's People of India project.
67.tq: NCM Chairperson (Jul 2026): Harjit Singh Grewal.

68.s: Which language family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of India's speakers according to the older figures used in APPSC material?
68.x: The Indo-European or Indo-Aryan family accounted for approximately 73 per cent of speakers in the older figures. The 2011 Census estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
68.tq: Use the distinctive numerical share to separate the major language families.

68.s: The Dardic branch, including Kashmiri, belongs to which language family?
68.x: Kashmiri belongs to the Dardic branch of the Indo-Aryan family. Dardic is not a Sino-Tibetan branch.
68.tq: Discriminate between the closely confused Dardic and Sino-Tibetan classifications.

68.s:
With reference to the Dravidian language family, consider the following statements:
1. Telugu is classified as a South-Central Dravidian language.
2. Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam are associated with the southern branch.
3. Kui, Gondi and Kurukh are identified with Central or North Dravidian areas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu is South-Central Dravidian, while Kui, Gondi and Kurukh represent Central or North Dravidian languages or pockets.
68.tq: Check each branch-language association before selecting the coded combination.

68.s: The Austro-Asiatic language family in India is represented by which of the following branches?
68.x: The Austro-Asiatic family includes the Munda branch, with languages such as Santhali and Mundari, and the Mon-Khmer branch, including Khasi.
68.tq: Recall the two-branch structure of the Austro-Asiatic family.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
68.x: Kui is a Dravidian language associated with the Kandhas of Odisha. Santhali, Khasi and Garo are correctly matched with their respective branches or families.
68.tq: Find the wrongly assigned language family among otherwise familiar tribal-language pairs.

68.s: The Sino-Tibetan or Tibeto-Burman languages of India are concentrated mainly in which region?
o: The north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas
The Deccan plateau and Tamil Nadu
The Konkan coast and western Rajasthan
68.x: Sino-Tibetan languages are concentrated in the north-eastern States, Sikkim and Himalayan areas, and are also represented in Ladakh and Himachal Pradesh.
68.tq: Use regional distribution to distinguish Sino-Tibetan languages from the other families.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ho — Dravidian language of Tamil Nadu
68.x: Halbi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh. Kui is Dravidian, while Ho and Mundari are Austro-Asiatic Munda languages.
68.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate the swapped family-location pairs.

68.s: The presence of Khasi, an Austro-Asiatic language of the Mon-Khmer branch, is considered evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of:
68.x: Khasi is treated as evidence that the Meghalaya plateau was once part of peninsular India. Its Mon-Khmer affiliation links it with the Austro-Asiatic linguistic zone.
68.tq: Apply a linguistic-distribution clue to infer the historical geographical relationship.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Santhali — Austro-Asiatic
2. Savara — Austro-Asiatic
3. Garo — Sino-Tibetan
4. Gor Boli — Indo-Aryan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Santhali and Savara are Austro-Asiatic, Garo is Sino-Tibetan and Gor Boli is Indo-Aryan.
68.tq: Verify each tribal-language affiliation individually before choosing the complete combination.

68.s:
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the older figures from the 2011 Census-based estimates for India's language families?
1. The older estimate for Indo-Aryan was about 73 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 78.05 per cent.
2. The older estimate for Dravidian was about 20 per cent, whereas the 2011 estimate was about 19.64 per cent.
3. The older estimate for Tibeto-Burman was about 20 per cent.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
68.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: the older Tibeto-Burman estimate was about 0.85 per cent, not 20 per cent.
68.tq: Compare corresponding figures and detect the misplaced decimal-scale percentage.

68.s: Which one of the following statements about Santhali is correct?
o: It is written in Roman script and was included through the 73rd Amendment of 1992.
It is written in Ol Chiki, created by Raghunath Murmu in 1925, and entered the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Amendment of 2003.
It is written in Ol Chiki, created in 1950, and is not a Scheduled Language.
It is written in Devanagari and entered the Eighth Schedule through the 42nd Amendment of 1976.
68.x: Santhali is written in Ol Chiki, created by Raghunath Murmu in 1925. It was included in the Eighth Schedule through the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003.
68.tq: Combine script, creator and amendment-year facts to reject near-miss options.

68.s: According to an APPSC (2007) question, most of the tribal languages of central and eastern India belong to which language family?
68.x: Most tribal languages of central and eastern India (Jharkhand-Odisha-West Bengal belt: Santhali, Mundari, Ho) are Austric. Dravidian covers only some central tribal pockets (Gondi, Kui, Kurukh); Sino-Tibetan is the language family of the North-East and Himalaya; Indo-Aryan is the family of the north, west and east plains.
68.tq: Central-eastern tribal belt = Austric (Munda).

68.s: According to the 1961 Census, how many mother tongues were listed?
68.x: The 1961 Census listed 1,652 mother tongues.
68.tq: Direct numerical recall of a census figure.

68.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Census 2011 language data:
1. About 19,500 raw mother tongues were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues.
2. The 1,369 mother tongues were grouped into 121 languages.
3. The 121 languages comprised 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. Census 2011 language returns were rationalised into 1,369 mother tongues and grouped into 121 languages, consisting of 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
68.tq: Combine the raw count, rationalised count and scheduled/non-scheduled classification.

68.s: For purposes of Census language classification, a language generally requires at least how many speakers?
68.x: The Census counts a language when it has 10,000 or more speakers.
68.tq: Test the exact threshold rather than the broader language count.

68.s: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India, conducted during 1903–1928, recorded:
68.x: Grierson's Linguistic Survey of India recorded 179 languages and 544 dialects between 1903 and 1928.
68.tq: Keep the language count and dialect count in their correct order.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
68.x: Ethnologue lists 455 living languages in India. The People's Linguistic Survey documents more than 780 languages, while 1,652 mother tongues belong to the 1961 Census.
68.tq: Match each survey or source with its distinctive count.

68.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Census language count from the constitutional language count?
o: Only the 99 non-scheduled languages are constitutionally recognised.
All 121 Census languages are included in the Eighth Schedule.
The Eighth Schedule contains all 1,369 rationalised mother tongues.
The 121-language Census count includes 22 scheduled and 99 non-scheduled languages.
68.x: The Census grouped mother tongues into 121 languages, of which 22 are in the Eighth Schedule and 99 are non-scheduled. The 121-language Census count should not be equated with the constitutional list.
68.tq: Separate the Census classification from constitutional recognition.

68.s: Which group consists of the scheduled languages with the smallest number of speakers as per Census 2011?
68.x: Sanskrit, Bodo and Manipuri are the smallest scheduled languages. Hindi, Bengali and Marathi are the three largest; Telugu, Tamil and Kannada are large Dravidian languages; Kashmiri is not among the smallest, and Punjabi and Odia have many speakers.
68.tq: Smallest scheduled: Sanskrit, Bodo, Manipuri (not Kashmiri).

68.s:
Arrange the following Indian languages in descending order of their share of speakers according to the 2011 Census:
A. Telugu
B. Hindi
C. Tamil
D. Bengali
68.x: The correct order is Hindi (43.6 per cent), Bengali (8.0 per cent), Telugu (6.7 per cent) and Tamil (5.7 per cent).
68.tq: Order the items by their numerical shares, beginning with the largest value.

68.s: Which change in the ranking of Indian languages occurred between the 2001 and 2011 Census figures?
o: Bengali moved from second to fifth, while Tamil became second.
Hindi moved from first to third, while Marathi became first.
Tamil moved from fifth to third, while Telugu became fifth.
Telugu moved from third to fourth, while Marathi overtook it for third place.
68.x: Telugu had occupied third place in 2001, but Marathi overtook it in 2011; Telugu consequently stood fourth.
68.tq: Test the direction of change in a close ranking rather than merely recalling the final order.

68.s: Which of the following correctly states the world ranking of the three Indian languages mentioned among the world's most spoken languages?
68.x: Among the stated world rankings, Hindi is second, Bengali is seventh and Punjabi is tenth.
68.tq: Retain the separate world ranks and avoid substituting the Indian domestic ranking.

68.s: Which language is described as the most spoken first language and as the lingua franca of northern and central India?
68.x: Hindi is the most spoken first language and functions as the lingua franca of northern and central India.
68.tq: Distinguish the status of a first language and lingua franca from a language's global rank.

68.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Each State may choose its own official language or languages.
2. Hindi and English are the official languages of the Union.
3. A State is constitutionally required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: States may choose their own official language or languages, while Hindi and English are the Union’s official languages. A State is not required to adopt Hindi as its only official language.
68.tq: Identify the extreme word ‘only’ in the false statement about State language choice.

68.s: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on:
68.x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949, a date now observed as Hindi Diwas.
68.tq: Distinguish the constitutional language date from Independence and Republic Day dates.

68.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Munshi-Ayyangar formula?
o: Fourteen languages were recognised in the Eighth Schedule
All provinces were prohibited from using English for official purposes
Hindi in Devanagari was designated as the Union’s official language
68.x: The formula allowed provinces to choose a regional language or English. It did not prohibit all use of English; Hindi was to become the Union’s official language after a 15-year transition.
68.tq: Find the absolute prohibition that contradicts the provision allowing regional language or English.

68.s: The Official Languages Act, 1963 is significant because it:
o: Required every State to adopt the three-language formula
Continued the use of English alongside Hindi after 1965
Removed Hindi from the Union’s official-language framework
Made Sanskrit the sole official language of the Union
68.x: The Official Languages Act, 1963 continued English in use alongside Hindi after 1965.
68.tq: Identify the legal effect of the Act rather than confusing it with the original constitutional transition plan.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Article)
A. Article 343
B. Article 344
C. Article 345
D. Article 351
List-II (Provision)
1. State Legislature adopts the official language(s) of the State
2. Official language of the Union: Hindi in Devanagari
3. Union's duty to develop Hindi
4. President's Official Language Commission and Parliamentary Committee
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
68.x: Art. 343 = Hindi in Devanagari as Union's official language (A-2); Art. 344 = President's Official Language Commission and Parliamentary Committee (B-4); Art. 345 = State Legislature adopts State official language(s) (C-1); Art. 351 = Union's duty to develop Hindi (D-3). Option 2 swaps 343 and 344, option 3 swaps 345 and 351, option 4 swaps 343 and 345.
68.tq: 343 Union, 344 Commission, 345 State, 351 directive to develop Hindi.

68.s: Language used for communication between one State and another State, or between a State and the Union, is dealt with under:
68.x: Article 346 concerns the language for communication between States and between a State and the Union.
68.tq: Use the functional subject of the Article—communication between governments—to identify the provision.

68.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Article — Subject
1. Article 348 — Language of the Supreme Court, High Courts and Acts
2. Article 349 — Special procedure for language laws
3. Article 350 — Representations for redress in any language
4. Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
68.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Articles 348 to 350A cover judicial and legislative language, special procedure, representations and primary-stage mother-tongue instruction respectively.
68.tq: Verify each neighbouring Article separately because the provisions form a closely spaced constitutional sequence.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 350A — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 351 — Union’s duty to develop Hindi
Article 343 — Official language of the Union
68.x: Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Article 350A concerns facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage.
68.tq: Use the neighbouring-Article trap by distinguishing 350A from 350B.

68.s: The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957 and has its headquarters at:
68.x: The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was set up in 1957, with its headquarters at Allahabad.
68.tq: Test the office-location association and reject nearby administrative centres.

68.s: Which one of the following is the correct present list of languages added by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003?
68.x: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Discriminate between the language groups added by the 71st and 92nd Amendments.

68.s: The 96th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 changed the name of which language in the Eighth Schedule?
68.x: The 96th Amendment changed the constitutional name of the language from Oriya to Odia. It did not add a new language to the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Distinguish a change in nomenclature from the addition of a language.

68.s:
Consider the following statements about inclusion in the Eighth Schedule:
1. There are no fixed criteria for inclusion of a language.
2. The Ashok Pahwa Committee was constituted in 1996.
3. The Sitakant Mohapatra Committee was constituted in 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: All three statements are correct. No fixed constitutional criteria exist for inclusion, and the Ashok Pahwa and Sitakant Mohapatra Committees are associated with the years 1996 and 2003 respectively.
68.tq: Check both the general rule and the committee-year pairings.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs of languages is correctly matched with its status in the Eighth Schedule?
o: Kokborok and Bhojpuri — not included in the Eighth Schedule
Bhojpuri and Gor Boli — included in the original list of 14
Gor Boli and Kokborok — included by the 92nd Amendment
Bhojpuri and Santhali — both excluded from the Eighth Schedule
68.x: Kokborok and Bhojpuri are not included in the Eighth Schedule. Gor Boli, also known as Lambadi, is likewise not included.
68.tq: Separate constitutionally included languages from pending or excluded demands.

68.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Amendment)
A. 21st Amendment, 1967
B. 71st Amendment, 1992
C. 92nd Amendment, 2003
D. Original Schedule, 1950

List-II (Language addition or status)
1. Four languages added
2. Fourteen languages initially included
3. Sindhi added
4. Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali added

Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
68.x: The 21st Amendment added Sindhi; the 71st added Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali; the 92nd added four languages; and the original Schedule contained 14 languages.
68.tq: Start with the sure amendment-language pair and complete the code.

68.s: Which of the following languages was included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950?
68.x: Telugu was among the 14 languages included in the original Eighth Schedule in 1950. Sindhi, Konkani and Santhali were added later.
68.tq: Distinguish original scheduled languages from later additions.

68.s: The Eighth Schedule is constitutionally linked with which of the following Articles?
68.x: The Eighth Schedule is linked to Article 344(1), concerning the Commission and Committee on official language, and Article 351, concerning promotion of Hindi.
68.tq: Use the constitutional-provision trap by separating linked Articles from other language provisions.

68.s: Which one of the following statements about English and the Eighth Schedule is correct?
o: English was included in the original Schedule but removed in 1992.
English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
English was added by the 92nd Amendment along with Santhali.
English is one of the 22 scheduled languages by convention.
68.x: English has never been included in the Eighth Schedule.
68.tq: Test the distinction between official use of English and its constitutional Schedule status.

68.s: The 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule cover approximately what percentage of the population's mother tongues?
68.x: The 22 scheduled languages cover the mother tongues of approximately 96.71 percent of the population.
68.tq: Distinguish the current coverage figure from the earlier 91 percent figure.

68.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Khasi and Garo — not included in the Eighth Schedule
Kokborok — included in the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment
Gor Boli — spoken by Banjaras in several Indian States
68.x: Kokborok is not included in the Eighth Schedule and is among the languages for which inclusion has been demanded. The 92nd Amendment added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali.
68.tq: Find the wrongly matched inclusion claim among pending-demand languages.

68.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gor Boli or Lambadi?
o: It is an Austroasiatic language written in Ol Chiki.
It is a Tibeto-Burman language confined to the North-East.
It is a Dravidian language with a widely standardised script of its own.
It is an Indo-Aryan language spoken by Banjaras and has no script of its own.
68.x: Gor Boli or Lambadi is Indo-Aryan, is spoken by Banjaras across several States, and has no script of its own.
68.tq: Separate language family, community, geographical spread and script.

68.s: Which of the following statements regarding recent constitutional editions is correct?
o: The first digital edition was released only in Bhojpuri and Gor Boli.
Only English and Hindi digital editions were released under Article 394A.
The President released a digital edition in Santhali, with first-time editions also in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
Digital editions of the Constitution were released in Santhali, Kokborok and Kashmiri for the first time in all three cases.
68.x: The President released digital editions of the Constitution in Santhali; first-time editions were also produced in Kokborok and Kashmiri.
68.tq: Distinguish the principal language from the languages receiving first-time editions.

68.s: A language community seeks authoritative translation of the Constitution under Article 394A, interpretation in Parliament and central development funds. These are principally associated with:
o: Recognition as a non-scheduled Census language
Classification as a dialect under Hindi
Recognition by the People's Linguistic Survey alone
68.x: Interpretation in Parliament, authoritative constitutional translation under Article 394A and central development funds are stated benefits associated with Eighth Schedule inclusion.
68.tq: Apply the listed benefits to identify the relevant constitutional status.

68.s:
Arrange the following languages in chronological order of their recognition as classical languages of India:
A. Kannada
B. Sanskrit
C. Odia
D. Tamil
68.x: Tamil was recognised in 2004, Sanskrit in 2005, Kannada in 2008 and Odia in 2014.
68.tq: Fix the earliest and latest entries first, then place the intervening years.

68.s: Which one of the following is NOT among the criteria traditionally associated with the recognition of a classical language?
o: A rich ancient literary tradition regarded as heritage
High antiquity of early texts, generally 1,500 to 2,000 years old
A tradition that must be written exclusively in prose
68.x: The criteria relate to antiquity, a rich ancient literary tradition and originality; exclusive composition in prose is not a criterion.
68.tq: Find the option that reverses or distorts the exact wording of a formal criterion.

68.s:
With reference to the revised criteria for classical languages in 2024, consider the following statements:
1. Knowledge texts were added to the scope of eligible literature.
2. Both prose and poetry were recognised in the revised formulation.
3. Epigraphic evidence was added as a consideration.
4. The requirement that the tradition must be original and not borrowed was retained without change.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
68.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The revised criteria dropped the requirement that the tradition must be ‘original, not borrowed’, so statement 4 is false.
68.tq: Watch for a statement that changes a reported revision into a continuation of the old rule.

68.s: The status of a classical language is granted by:
68.x: Classical-language status is granted by the Government of India, not by an individual State Government or an academic institution.
68.tq: Apply the ‘who grants or authorises this?’ authority test.

68.s: Granth Kutir at Rashtrapati Bhavan contains works in:
o: The 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule, excluding Pali and Prakrit
Only the five languages recognised in 2024
All 8 languages included in the Eighth Schedule in 1950
68.x: Granth Kutir holds works in all 11 classical languages. It was inaugurated by President Murmu and contains about 2,300 books and 50 manuscripts.
68.tq: Match the cultural institution with the exact scope of its collection.

68.s:
Which of the following statements regarding classical languages is correct?
1. India has 11 classical languages.
2. Telugu, Marathi and Bengali are among the classical languages.
3. Pali and Prakrit are the only classical languages outside the Eighth Schedule.
68.x: All three statements are correct. There are 11 classical languages, and Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Pali and Prakrit are included in the stated classifications.
68.tq: Combine a numerical fact with list-membership statements and identify the complete combination.

68.s: Telugu was recognised as a classical language in which year, along with which other language?
68.x: Telugu and Kannada were both recognised in 2008. Tamil (2004) was the first classical language and was recognised alone; Sanskrit followed in 2005; Malayalam was recognised in 2013. The claim that Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Odia were all recognised in 2008 is a trap.
68.tq: 2008 = Telugu + Kannada; Malayalam 2013, Odia 2014.

68.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Goa — Konkani, with Marathi also used
68.x: Konkani is the official language of Goa, and Marathi is also used there. Meghalaya has English, Khasi and Garo; Nagaland has English; Sikkim has several official languages.
68.tq: Start with the sure state-language pair and eliminate the swapped state associations.

68.s: Which of the following languages are declared official languages of Meghalaya along with English?
68.x: Meghalaya has English as an official language, with Khasi and Garo also declared official languages.
68.tq: Distinguish the paired regional languages of Meghalaya from those associated with Sikkim and Goa.

68.s: English is the official language of which one of the following States listed below?
68.x: English is the official language of Nagaland. Meghalaya also uses English along with Khasi and Garo, whereas Andhra Pradesh has Telugu as its official language.
68.tq: Use the exact state-language association rather than assuming a regional language is the sole official language.
