94.tq: Use the location initials and eliminate the reversed cable routes.

94.s: Which of the following statements correctly reflects the Visakhapatnam Declaration?
o: It extended NeSDA to Ladakh and the North-East to bridge the digital divide.
It replaced BharatNet with PM-WANI in all Gram Panchayats.
It amended the Aadhaar Act to include digital signatures.
It established the single emergency number 112 throughout India.
94.x: The Visakhapatnam Declaration extended NeSDA to Ladakh and the North-East with the objective of bridging the digital divide.
94.tq: Match the declaration with its geographical expansion and policy purpose.

94.s: The Supreme Court has held that digital access forms part of which constitutional right?
94.x: Digital access has been held to form part of the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.
94.tq: Identify the constitutional article associated with the judicially recognised right.

94.s: Which organisation was the nodal agency for BharatNet and has subsequently been merged with BSNL?
94.x: Bharat Broadband Network Limited (BBNL) was the nodal agency for BharatNet and was later merged with BSNL.
94.tq: Identify the organisation by its specific institutional role rather than by its sector alone.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding BharatNet:
1. It was formerly known as the National Optical Fibre Network.
2. It aims to connect all Gram Panchayats.
3. It is funded by the Universal Service Obligation Fund.
4. Its fibre network involves BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: All four statements are correct. BharatNet was earlier called NOFN, targets Gram Panchayat connectivity, is funded by USOF and uses the fibre infrastructure of BSNL, RailTel and PGCIL.
94.tq: Verify the programme’s former name, objective, funding source and implementation partners together.

94.s:
Which of the following features is associated with the Amended BharatNet Programme?
1. Adoption of a public-private partnership model
2. Greater role for States
3. Provision of 100 Mbps per Gram Panchayat, scalable to 1 Gbps
4. Approval involving an outlay of ₹1.39 lakh crore
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: The Amended BharatNet Programme includes PPP implementation, a larger State role, 100 Mbps scalable to 1 Gbps per Gram Panchayat and an approved outlay of ₹1.39 lakh crore.
94.tq: Treat the programme’s model, State role, technical target and approved outlay as separate checks.

94.s: Which one of the following was the first pillar of Digital India?
94.x: Broadband highways was the first of the nine pillars of Digital India.
94.tq: Identify the specifically numbered or ordered component rather than a related connectivity service.

94.s: The National Broadband Mission was launched in:
94.x: The National Broadband Mission was launched in December 2019.
94.tq: Use chronological discrimination among the launch dates of major digital programmes.

94.s: PM-WANI, approved in December 2020, is primarily associated with:
o: Registration of newspapers through the PRGI
Fibre connectivity exclusively between Gram Panchayats
Public Wi-Fi through Public Data Offices and aggregators
94.x: PM-WANI, or Wi-Fi Access Network Interface, enables public Wi-Fi through Public Data Offices and aggregators.
94.tq: Match the programme with its delivery mechanism and eliminate unrelated institutional functions.

94.s: Public Wi-Fi at railway stations is provided under which RailTel service?
94.x: RailWire is RailTel’s public Wi-Fi service at railway stations.
94.tq: Distinguish the railway-specific service from nationwide broadband and public Wi-Fi programmes.

94.s: BharatNet is described as the world's largest:
94.x: BharatNet is described as the world's largest rural broadband project.
94.tq: Identify the scale claim and the sector to which it belongs.

94.s: The principal focus of Phase 3 of BharatNet is:
o: Last-mile connectivity with participation of private players
Replacing all fibre with satellite links
94.x: BharatNet Phase 3 focuses on last-mile connectivity and the participation of private players.
94.tq: Identify the implementation phase by its operational focus.

94.s: The Digital India programme, whose first pillar is broadband highways, was launched on:
94.x: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 with 9 pillars. 3 July 2015 is the start of nationwide mobile number portability, December 2019 is the National Broadband Mission, and 15 August 2014 is not the launch date in the notes.
94.tq: Digital India 1 July 2015; MNP two days later.

94.s: As per early 2025 data, BharatNet had connected about how many Gram Panchayats?
94.x: BharatNet connected 2,18,347 (about 2.18 lakh) Gram Panchayats. 6.92 lakh km is the length of optical fibre laid, 5.69 lakh is the number of CSCs, and 1.64 lakh is the number of post offices migrated to the APT platform.
94.tq: BharatNet: 2.18 lakh GPs, 6.92 lakh km OFC.

94.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting regulates private TV channels.
2. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting regulates MSOs and cable operators under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995.
3. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting operationalises Community Radio Stations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: All three statements are correct. The Ministry of Information and Broadcasting also auctions private FM channels.
94.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when all listed functions belong to one ministry.

94.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. All India Radio got its name in 1936 and has been called Akashvani since 1957.
2. Doordarshan started on 15 September 1959 in Mumbai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: Statement 1 is correct: AIR was named in 1936 and called Akashvani from 1957. Statement 2 is wrong: Doordarshan started on 15 September 1959 in Delhi, not Mumbai. So '1 only'; the other options are wrong.
94.tq: AIR 1936, Akashvani 1957, Doordarshan Delhi 1959.

94.s: All India Radio and Doordarshan are operated by:
94.x: Both All India Radio and Doordarshan are run by Prasar Bharati.
94.tq: Identify the common parent organisation rather than the ministry or regulator associated with another media function.

94.s:
Consider the following statements about Community Radio Stations (CRS):
1. The first CRS was Anna FM of Anna University, started in 2004.
2. CRS are licensed by the Press Registrar General of India for rural and remote areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: Statement 1 is correct: Anna FM (Anna University, 2004) was the first CRS. Statement 2 is wrong: CRS are licensed by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting; the PRGI handles newspaper registration. So '1 only'; the other options are wrong.
94.tq: CRS = MIB licence; PRGI = newspapers.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding newspaper registration in India:
1. The Press and Registration of Periodicals Act, 2023 replaced the PRB Act, 1867.
2. The system is administered by the Press Registrar General of India.
3. The earlier designation was Registrar of Newspapers for India.
4. The Press Council Act was enacted in 1978.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: All four statements are correct. The 2023 Act replaced the 1867 law, the Press Registrar General administers registration, the earlier office was RNI, and the Press Council Act dates from 1978.
94.tq: Check the replacement law, present authority, former title and related legislation separately.

94.s: Which of the following is NOT a media unit associated with the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting?
94.x: PIB, the Central Bureau of Communication and Publications Division are MIB media units. The Universal Service Obligation Fund is a telecom connectivity funding mechanism, not an MIB media unit.
94.tq: Find the item belonging to telecom funding rather than the listed media-unit group.

94.s: Which network architecture was selected by APSFL over GPON for Andhra Pradesh’s fibre connectivity?
94.x: APSFL selected an IP-MPLS ring topology instead of GPON for its network architecture.
94.tq: Distinguish the chosen architecture from the explicitly rejected alternative.

94.s: The triple-play services offered through APSFL comprise:
o: Railway Wi-Fi, mobile banking and television
Postal delivery, voice and cable landing
94.x: APSFL’s triple play consists of internet, IPTV and voice services.
94.tq: Recall the three services as a single service bundle.

94.s:
Consider the following statements regarding APSFL:
1. Its last mile is provided by more than 6,300 Local Cable Operators.
2. It has more than 22,000 government connections.
3. The government connections include 5,000 RSKs, 1,300 PHCs and 6,500 schools.
4. TRAI ranks Andhra Pradesh among the highest States in rural broadband.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
94.x: All four statements are correct. APSFL uses more than 6,300 Local Cable Operators for the last mile and has the stated government connections; TRAI places Andhra Pradesh among the highest in rural broadband.
94.tq: Break the network description into provider, total connections, component institutions and performance ranking.

94.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Amended BharatNet arrangement in Andhra Pradesh signed in February 2026?
o: A satellite-only network for 4,000 tribal hamlets
Last-mile connectivity to 6,500 villages and broadband to every school within 100 days
Last-mile connectivity to 3,942 villages and broadband to every household within 18 months
Connectivity to 10,660 post offices and every household within five years
94.x: The Memorandum of Cooperation for Amended BharatNet in Andhra Pradesh provides for last-mile connectivity to 3,942 villages and broadband to every household within 18 months.
94.tq: Keep the village count and implementation period together rather than mixing them with other AP targets.

94.s: Phase 3 of AP FiberNet extended broadband connectivity to more than 4,000 remote tribal hamlets in the:
94.x: AP FiberNet Phase 3 extended broadband to more than 4,000 remote tribal hamlets in the Eastern Ghats.
94.tq: Use the location clue to distinguish the regional connectivity project.

94.s: AP FiberNet's tribal expansion was funded through which mechanism, now known as Digital Bharat Nidhi?
94.x: The AP FiberNet tribal expansion was funded through the Universal Service Obligation Fund, or USOF, now known as Digital Bharat Nidhi.
94.tq: Distinguish a funding mechanism from a digital platform or literacy scheme.

94.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's connectivity plans:
1. The Chief Minister directed telecom operators to complete new towers within 100 days.
2. An undersea internet cable landing station with data centres has been discussed for the State.
3. The Amended BharatNet MoC aims at broadband to every household within 100 days.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
94.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the CM set a 100-day tower drive and discussed an undersea cable landing station plus data centres with Sunil Bharti Mittal. Statement 3 is wrong: the Amended BharatNet MoC targets every household in 18 months, not 100 days. So '1 and 2 only'.
94.tq: AP: towers 100 days; BharatNet households 18 months.

94.s:
Arrange the following communication developments in chronological order:
A. First telephone exchange at Calcutta
B. Nationwide mobile number portability
C. Launch of 5G in India
D. Launch of Digital India
94.x: The correct sequence is Calcutta telephone exchange (1882), Digital India (1 July 2015), nationwide MNP (3 July 2015) and 5G launch (October 2022).
94.tq: Fix the nineteenth-century event first and distinguish the two July 2015 developments before placing 5G.

94.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Amended BharatNet MoC in Andhra Pradesh — February 2026
94.x: KLI was inaugurated in January 2024, not July 2015. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
94.tq: Find the date that belongs to a different communication initiative by comparing all four pairs.

95.s: The total length of National Highways in Andhra Pradesh was stated as approximately:
95.x: The National Highway network in Andhra Pradesh was stated to be 8,744 km. The total road length was 54,177 km.
95.tq: Distinguish the National Highway figure from the total-road figure and density figures.

95.s: Which statement correctly compares the National Highway density of Andhra Pradesh with the all-India figure?
o: 54.177 km per lakh population in Andhra Pradesh against 8.744 km all-India
8.744 km per lakh population in Andhra Pradesh against 54.177 km all-India
12.09 km per lakh population in Andhra Pradesh against 17.64 km all-India
17.64 km per lakh population in Andhra Pradesh against 12.09 km all-India
95.x: Andhra Pradesh had an NH density of 17.64 km per lakh population, compared with 12.09 km per lakh population for India as a whole.
95.tq: Use the direction of comparison and preserve the units attached to each figure.

95.s: Which authority controls the largest share of the National Highway length in Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: NHAI controls 4,406 km, compared with 3,738 km under the State PWD and 600 km under the MoRTH-PIU.
95.tq: Compare institutional responsibility by the size of the controlled network.

95.s: Which is the longest National Highway in Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: NH-16 (Chennai-Kolkata, old NH-5) runs about 1,000 km in the State and is part of the Golden Quadrilateral (APPSC 2025). NH-44 (Srinagar-Kanyakumari) only crosses Rayalaseema; NH-65 is Pune-Machilipatnam; NH-544G is the Bengaluru-Kadapa-Vijayawada Economic Corridor.
95.tq: Longest NH in AP = NH-16 (coastal, Golden Quadrilateral).

95.s: Which National Highway crosses Rayalaseema via Kurnool and Anantapur?
95.x: NH-44 (Srinagar-Kanyakumari) crosses Rayalaseema via Kurnool and Anantapur. NH-16 is the coastal Chennai-Kolkata highway; NH-65 runs Pune-Machilipatnam (old NH-9); NH-544G is the Bengaluru-Kadapa-Vijayawada corridor.
95.tq: NH-44 = Srinagar-Kanyakumari through Kurnool-Anantapur.

95.s: The National Highway works targeted for completion by 2029 were valued at over:
95.x: National Highway works worth more than ₹1.40 lakh crore were targeted for completion by 2029.
95.tq: Match the financial value with the correct infrastructure programme and deadline.

95.s: Which project was stated to be due for completion by 2027?
95.x: The Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor was stated to be due by 2027. A DPR was ordered separately for the Kharagpur–Amaravati expressway.
95.tq: Discriminate between projects by their stated implementation stage and deadline.

95.s: Which one of the following statements regarding National Highway works in Andhra Pradesh during FY 2025–26 is correct?
o: 392 works covering 93 km were completed, with an expenditure of ₹45,633 crore.
93 works covering 392 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹2,065 crore.
93 works covering 2,065 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹45,633 crore.
2,065 works covering 93 km were sanctioned, with an expenditure of ₹1.40 lakh crore.
95.x: During FY 2025–26, 93 works covering 2,065 km involved ₹45,633 crore; 392 km had been completed.
95.tq: Keep work count, route length, cost and completed length distinct.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
95.x: NH-544G is the Bengaluru–Kadapa–Vijayawada Economic Corridor. The Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati project is a separate fast-tracked expressway for which a DPR was ordered.
95.tq: Find the swapped highway identity among otherwise familiar route pairs.

95.s: The proposed Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati expressway is presently associated with:
o: Fast-tracking and preparation of a Detailed Project Report
Completion as a PPP road linking NH-65 and NH-16
A completed four-lane railway line through NTR district
95.x: The Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati expressway has been fast-tracked and a DPR has been ordered.
95.tq: Match a project’s present status with the action actually reported for it.

95.s: The proposed policy of linking every port from Mulapeta to Krishnapatnam by National Highways is based on the:
95.x: The proposal to connect every port from Mulapeta to Krishnapatnam by National Highways is described as being on the Gujarat model.
95.tq: Identify the named development model rather than the transport network itself.

95.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five pillars of the Sagarmala programme?
95.x: The five Sagarmala pillars are port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation, coastal community development, and coastal shipping/inland water transport. Port modernisation, port-led industrialisation and coastal community development are all pillars; dedicated freight corridors are a railway programme, not a Sagarmala pillar.
95.tq: Sagarmala 5: modernise, connect, industrialise, community, coastal shipping/IWT.

95.s: The 125-km Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla road, built on the PPP model, links which two National Highways?
95.x: The completed Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla road (125 km, PPP) links NH-65 (Pune-Machilipatnam) with NH-16 (Chennai-Kolkata). NH-44 runs through Rayalaseema and NH-544G is the Bengaluru-Kadapa-Vijayawada corridor, so the other pairs are wrong.
95.tq: Narketpally-Addanki-Medarametla: NH-65 to NH-16.

95.s: The total road network of Andhra Pradesh in December 2025 was approximately:
95.x: The total road network was 54,177 km, comprising 45,433 km of State roads and 8,744 km of National Highways.
95.tq: Distinguish the total from its component categories and rural-road figure.

95.s:
Match the road categories of Andhra Pradesh with their lengths:

List-I (Category)
a. State Highways
b. Major District Roads
c. Other District Roads
d. National Highways

List-II (Length)
i. 8,744 km
ii. 12,653 km
iii. 26,527 km
iv. 6,253 km

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
95.x: State Highways measure 12,653 km, Major District Roads 26,527 km, Other District Roads 6,253 km and National Highways 8,744 km.
95.tq: Match category figures by beginning with the distinctive National Highway total.

95.s: Which one of the following statements about road transport in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Roads carry more than 80% of the traffic in the State.
National Highways account for the entire road network of the State.
Rural roads are shorter than the State Highway network.
Roads carry less than 20% of the traffic in the State.
95.x: Roads carry more than 80% of traffic in Andhra Pradesh. The road network also includes substantial State, district and rural roads.
95.tq: Use the transport-share comparison and reject reversed trends.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding rural roads in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The rural-road network was 79,452 km in April 2025.
2. PMGSY had connected 99.09% of habitations.
3. APRDC was established in 1998.
4. APRBRP and APMCRCIP are associated with NDB assistance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All four statements are correct. The rural-road network was 79,452 km, PMGSY coverage was 99.09%, APRDC dates from 1998, and the two named programmes received NDB assistance.
95.tq: Statement-combination question covering figures, institutional history and programme linkage.

95.s: Which of the following correctly represents the APSRTC position in December 2025?
95.x: APSRTC had 10,998 buses, 129 depots, four zones and 44,215 staff in December 2025. The fleet included 8,236 own buses and 2,762 hired buses.
95.tq: Separate total fleet, ownership components, depots, zones and staff figures.

95.s: Stree Shakti bus travel facility in Andhra Pradesh, introduced from 15 August 2025, provides free travel to:
o: Only women residing in rural areas
95.x: The Stree Shakti scheme provides free bus travel for women and transgender persons from 15 August 2025.
95.tq: Confusable-beneficiary discrimination in a welfare transport scheme.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about APSRTC:
1. It was established in 1958.
2. Its accident rate of 0.06 per lakh km is the lowest among State Transport Undertakings.
3. It received 7,500 e-buses under PM e-Bus Sewa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statement 1 is correct: APSRTC was established in 1958. Statement 2 is correct: its accident rate of 0.06 per lakh km is the lowest among STUs. Statement 3 is wrong: it got 750 e-buses under PM e-Bus Sewa (plus 300 for Tirupati-Tirumala), not 7,500. So only '1 and 2' is right; options with 3 are wrong.
95.tq: APSRTC 1958; 0.06 accidents/lakh km; 750 PM e-Bus Sewa buses.

95.s: The South Coast Railway zone was created under which statutory provision?
95.x: The South Coast Railway zone was mandated by the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014.
95.tq: Match the railway zone with the correct parent legislation.

95.s: Which of the following railway establishments continues to remain under South Central Railway after the formation of South Coast Railway?
95.x: South Central Railway retains Hyderabad, Secunderabad and Nanded. Visakhapatnam, Guntur and Guntakal are associated with South Coast Railway.
95.tq: Use the retained-membership trap in a reorganisation question.

95.s: The South Coast Railway, India's 18th railway zone, has its headquarters at:
95.x: South Coast Railway (SCoR), mandated by the AP Reorganisation Act 2014 and operational from 1 June 2026, has its HQ at Visakhapatnam. Vijayawada and Guntur are divisions of SCoR, not its HQ. Secunderabad is the HQ of South Central Railway.
95.tq: SCoR: 18th zone, HQ Visakhapatnam, from 1 June 2026.

95.s: After the formation of the South Coast Railway, the remaining part of the old Waltair division forms which new division of East Coast Railway?
95.x: The truncated Waltair division became SCoR's Visakhapatnam division, and the rest of Waltair forms ECoR's new Rayagada division. Guntakal and Vijayawada came to SCoR from SCR. Nanded stays with SCR.
95.tq: Waltair split: Visakhapatnam (SCoR) + Rayagada (ECoR).

95.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Railway project)
a. Errupalem–Nambur line
b. Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line
c. Kotipalli–Narasapur line

d. Rajahmundry–Visakhapatnam third/fourth lines

List-II (Relevant feature)
i. Work in progress along the Konaseema coast
 ii. 57 km line with a 3-km bridge over the Krishna
 iii. 308 km line serving four backward districts
 iv. Project costing ₹9,889 crore

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: Errupalem–Nambur is the 57-km Amaravati line with a Krishna bridge; Nadikudi–Srikalahasti is 308 km; Kotipalli–Narasapur is under way on the Konaseema coast; and the Rajahmundry–Visakhapatnam third/fourth lines cost ₹9,889 crore.
95.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing mismatched project features.

95.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Errupalem–Nambur Amaravati railway line?
o: It includes a 30-km bridge over the Krishna.
It passes through NTR and Guntur districts.
95.x: The Amaravati line includes a 3-km bridge over the Krishna, not a 30-km bridge. It is a 57-km broad-gauge line through NTR and Guntur districts.
95.tq: Find the numerical exaggeration in an otherwise familiar project description.

95.s: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti railway line is particularly associated with the movement of:
o: Coal and petroleum from coastal ports
95.x: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line is intended to support cement and granite traffic and serves Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor.
95.tq: Link the infrastructure project with its stated freight purpose.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about railway development in Andhra Pradesh:
1. The railway network of Andhra Pradesh is fully electrified.
2. Works valued at ₹92,649 crore are under way.
3. Twenty-one of South Central Railway’s 73 Amrit Bharat stations are in Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct: AP’s network is 100% electrified, works worth ₹92,649 crore are under way, and 21 of SCR’s 73 Amrit Bharat stations are in the State.
95.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the coded combination.

95.s: The FY 2026 railway budget allocation for Andhra Pradesh was reported as:
95.x: The FY 2026 railway budget allocation for Andhra Pradesh was ₹9,417 crore. ₹10,134 crore refers to another reported railway allocation figure, while the other values relate to works or highway expenditure.
95.tq: Separate budget allocation from project-value figures.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Cherlopalli–Rapuru railway tunnel when it opened?
o: India’s first underwater railway tunnel in 2019
India’s longest electrified rail tunnel in 2019
95.x: When opened in 2019, the 6.6-km Cherlopalli–Rapuru tunnel was India’s longest electrified rail tunnel.
95.tq: Direct identification of a first/longest distinction.

95.s: The Obulavaripalle–Venkatachalam railway line is significant because it:
o: connects Gangavaram Port with the Visakhapatnam Metro
connects Ramayapatnam Port with the Konkan Railway
links Krishnapatnam Port with the Rayalaseema hinterland
links Kakinada Port with the North Coastal Railway zone
95.x: The line links Krishnapatnam Port to the Rayalaseema hinterland and includes the Cherlopalli–Rapuru tunnel.
95.tq: Test the functional relationship between a railway line, port and hinterland.

95.s: Which of the following statements regarding railway and port connectivity in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: Last-mile rail connectivity to all inland logistics nodes is complete.
Krishnapatnam is connected to the Rayalaseema hinterland only by road.
Ramayapatnam is situated next to NH-16 and Thettu railway station.
Kakinada Gateway has no railway line of its own.
95.x: Ramayapatnam is next to NH-16 and Thettu station. Kakinada Gateway includes its own rail line, while last-mile rail connectivity to Kopparthy, Orvakal and Krishnapatnam nodes remains incomplete.
95.tq: Wrong-transport-mode and incomplete-connectivity traps.

95.s: The first railway line in Andhra Pradesh was opened between Puttur and Renigunta in
95.x: The first railway line in Andhra Pradesh was the Puttur-Renigunta line, opened in 1862.
95.tq: Separate the State milestone from the first national railway milestone.

95.s: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti railway line is approximately how long and passes through which districts?
o: 508 km; Krishna, Guntur, Nellore and Tirupati
408 km; Kurnool, Kadapa, Anantapur and Chittoor
308 km; Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor
95.x: The Nadikudi–Srikalahasti line is 308 km long and passes through Guntur, Prakasam, Nellore and Chittoor.
95.tq: Combine route length with district coverage.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about the Errupalem-Nambur (Amaravati) railway line:
1. It is a 57-km broad-gauge line.
2. It passes through NTR and Guntur districts.
3. It is to be completed on a 6-year timeline.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the line is a 57-km BG line through NTR and Guntur districts, with a 3-km bridge over the Krishna, costing Rs 2,245 crore. Statement 3, the '6-year timeline', was the wrong statement in the APPSC G2 2025 question. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
95.tq: Amaravati line: 57 km, NTR + Guntur, 3 km Krishna bridge; '6 years' = trap.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about Vijayawada railway station:
1. It has building-integrated rooftop solar panels.
2. Its green certification is issued by IGBC.
3. Its certification is a LEED, USA, Platinum certification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The station has rooftop solar panels and IGBC Platinum certification; the LEED, USA description is incorrect.
95.tq: Find the wrong certifying authority in a statement-based question.

95.s: How many net-zero railway stations were declared by the Vijayawada division of South Central Railway?
95.x: The Vijayawada division declared ten net-zero stations, including Dwarapudi and Kadiyam.
95.tq: Test the exact count and use named examples as confirmation.

95.s: Which railway station near Sriharikota was redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat scheme?
95.x: Sullurupeta, near Sriharikota, was redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat scheme.
95.tq: Use the location clue to identify the station linked with the scheme.

95.s: The Araku railway line forms part of which railway line?
95.x: The Araku line is part of the Kottavalasa–Kirandul line.
95.tq: Test the parent railway line of a tourist route.

95.s: The glass-roofed coaches operating on the Visakhapatnam–Araku route are known as:
95.x: Glass-roofed Vistadome coaches operate on the Visakhapatnam–Araku route.
95.tq: Identify the exact official term rather than a descriptive synonym.

95.s: In terms of the length of coastline among Indian States, Andhra Pradesh is stated to have the:
95.x: With the coastline figure of 1,053.07 km, Andhra Pradesh is ranked third among the States in the stated classification.
95.tq: Discriminate between the current rank and the older rank associated with the 974 km figure.

95.s: Major ports and non-major ports are respectively covered under which Constitutional List entries?
o: State List Entry 27 and Union List Entry 31
Concurrent List Entry 27 and State List Entry 31
Union List Entry 31 and Concurrent List Entry 27
Union List Entry 27 and Concurrent List Entry 31
95.x: Major ports fall under Union List Entry 27, while non-major ports fall under Concurrent List Entry 31.
95.tq: Split the pair by both subject category and List entry.

95.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Krishnapatnam — SPS Nellore district
b. Gangavaram — Visakhapatnam district
c. Mulapeta — Srikakulam district
d. Machilipatnam — Krishna district
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
95.x: Krishnapatnam is in SPS Nellore, Gangavaram in Visakhapatnam, Mulapeta in Srikakulam and Machilipatnam in Krishna district.
95.tq: Start from sure district-port pairs and check the complete combination.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kakinada Deep Water Port — PPP OMST
95.x: Kakinada Anchorage is state-run and directly operated by APMB; it is not a PPP DBFOT port. Kakinada Deep Water, Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam are associated with OMST, BOOT and BOST models respectively.
95.tq: Find the single wrong operating-model match.

95.s: Which of the following ports is directly run by the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board?
95.x: Kakinada Anchorage is a state-run port directly operated by the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
95.tq: Identify the direct state operator rather than a private concessionaire.

95.s: Non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh handled how much cargo up to November 2025?
95.x: The non-major ports handled 80.82 MMT up to November 2025.
95.tq: Distinguish an aggregate cargo figure from individual port capacities and progress percentages.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a greenfield port with its development model?
95.x: Ramayapatnam follows the SPV model. Mulapeta is associated with the landlord model, Machilipatnam with landlord/EPC, and Kakinada Gateway with PPP/DBFOT in the stated classifications.
95.tq: Separate the development models of similarly classified greenfield ports.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the port structure of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Visakhapatnam is the sole major port of the State.
2. Major ports are administered by the Government of India.
3. Non-major ports are administered under the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh has one major port, Visakhapatnam, under the Union Government, while its notified non-major ports fall under the State maritime administration.
95.tq: Check the distinction between Union-administered major ports and State-administered non-major ports.

95.s: According to the 2025–26 Survey, how many notified non-major ports does Andhra Pradesh have, and how many of them are captive ports?
95.x: The 2025–26 Survey reports 17 notified non-major ports, of which three are captive ports.
95.tq: Read both components of a paired numerical fact carefully.

95.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Kakinada Deep Water Port — Gangavaram Port Limited
Krishnapatnam Port — GMR Kakinada Gateway Port Limited
95.x: Visakhapatnam Port is operated by the Visakhapatnam Port Authority. Gangavaram is operated by Gangavaram Port Limited, Kakinada Deep Water by Kakinada Seaports Limited and Krishnapatnam by its private operator.
95.tq: Start with the sure operator–port pair and eliminate swapped operators.

95.s: Which of the following is a distinctive feature of Gangavaram Port?
o: It has the highest government revenue share among AP ports.
It is operated by the State Government and has a 4 MMT capacity.
It has 11 berths and a capacity of 98 MMT.
It has the deepest draft and a capacity of 64 MMT.
95.x: Gangavaram is a greenfield deep-water port noted for its deepest draft and 64 MMT capacity.
95.tq: Separate the distinctive feature of one port from the capacity and features of neighbouring ports.

95.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Krishnapatnam Port?
95.x: Krishnapatnam Port has 11 berths and a reported capacity of 98 MMT. The other options refer to Kakinada Anchorage, Kakinada Gateway and Gangavaram respectively.
95.tq: Use a distinctive capacity or facility to identify the correct port.

95.s: Which port has the highest government revenue share among the ports of Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: Kakinada Deep Water Port provides the highest government revenue share, amounting to 22% of gross income.
95.tq: Identify the port from a precise revenue-sharing statistic.

95.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
95.x: Rawa is operated through a Single Buoy Mooring system by Cairn India for crude oil. The other operator–capacity combinations are interchanged.
95.tq: Find the exact three-part match of port, operator and function.

95.s: Kakinada SEZ/Gateway Port is developed under which model and has what capacity?
95.x: Kakinada Gateway Port follows the PPP-DBFOT model and has a capacity of 16 MTPA.
95.tq: Combine the development model with the capacity to avoid single-clue guessing.

95.s: Which port was reported to have handled the highest cargo among Andhra Pradesh ports up to November 2025?
95.x: Up to November 2025, Krishnapatnam handled 41.09 MMT, the highest among the listed ports.
95.tq: Use the ranking implied by the cargo figures rather than confusing capacity with actual handling.

95.s: Which greenfield port project had the highest progress as of October 2025?
95.x: Ramayapatnam had the highest reported progress at 74.34%, ahead of Mulapeta, Machilipatnam and Kakinada Gateway.
95.tq: Compare percentages directly and identify the maximum value.

95.s: The port at Mulapeta, formerly known as Bhavanapadu, is located in which district?
95.x: Mulapeta, formerly Bhavanapadu, is located in Srikakulam district.
95.tq: Use the former-name clue to identify the current port and district.

95.s: Which company is associated with the development of Machilipatnam Port under the landlord/EPC model?
95.x: Machilipatnam Port is being developed under the landlord/EPC model by MEIL.
95.tq: Test the operator or implementing agency rather than the port location alone.

95.s: Which of the following correctly describes the port structure and coastline of Andhra Pradesh?
o: 1 major port and  seven notified non-major ports; coastline of 853.07 km
2 major ports and 17 notified non-major ports; coastline of 1,053.07 km
17 major ports and 1 notified non-major port; coastline of 1,053.70 km
1 major port and 17 notified non-major ports; coastline of 1,053.07 km
95.x: Andhra Pradesh has one major port, Visakhapatnam, and 17 notified non-major ports, including three captive ports; its coastline is 1,053.07 km.
95.tq: Compare port categories and coastline figures without reversing major and non-major status.

95.s: The APPSC 2024 answer key matched Ramayapatnam port with Prakasam district. According to the Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, Ramayapatnam now lies in which district?
95.x: After the Gudluru area moved, Survey 2025-26 places Ramayapatnam in SPSR Nellore (93 km north of Krishnapatnam, near Thettu station); the APPSC 2024 key said Prakasam, so expect either. Krishna is the district of Machilipatnam port. Srikakulam is the district of Mulapeta (Bhavanapadu). Kakinada district holds the Kakinada ports.
95.tq: Ramayapatnam: Prakasam (2024 key) to SPSR Nellore (Survey 2025-26).

95.s: Gangavaram Port, cited in a UPSC (2009) question as India's largest private-sector port, was commissioned in which State?
95.x: Gangavaram is a greenfield deep-water PPP-BOOT port in Visakhapatnam district, Andhra Pradesh, with operations from 17 April 2009. That makes Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Gujarat wrong; none of them holds Gangavaram.
95.tq: Gangavaram (UPSC 2009) = Andhra Pradesh, deepest draft.

95.s: Visakhapatnam Port was opened to ocean traffic in which year?
95.x: Visakhapatnam Port was opened to ocean traffic in 1933.
95.tq: Use the direct year-recall method for an opening-history fact.

95.s:
Consider the following statements about Visakhapatnam Port:
1. It has both natural and artificial harbour features.
2. Its outer harbour serves iron ore exports.
3. It has a crude oil berth.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. Visakhapatnam has natural and artificial harbour components, an outer harbour for iron ore exports and a crude oil berth.
95.tq: Test a cluster of related port functions through coded statements.

95.s: Visakhapatnam Port is popularly known by which of the following names?
95.x: Visakhapatnam Port is called the “Brightest Jewel”.
95.tq: Use an exact sobriquet-recall question with closely related maritime distractors.

95.s: The natural protection to Visakhapatnam harbour is provided by which geographical feature?
o: Dolphin's Nose on the Yarada hills
95.x: Dolphin's Nose on the Yarada hills gives natural protection to Visakhapatnam harbour.
95.tq: Apply the location-feature association method.

95.s: In 2025–26, Visakhapatnam Port recorded traffic of approximately:
95.x: Visakhapatnam Port recorded 91.17 million metric tonnes in 2025–26.
95.tq: Separate the exact quantitative figure from nearby numerical distractors.

95.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Visakhapatnam Port's seafood traffic is correct?
o: It handled more than half of India's seafood exports in FY 2025–26.
It handled 19.32 lakh tonnes of seafood exports in FY 2025–26.
It is India's top seafood-export port and handled 5.12 lakh tonnes in FY 2025–26.
It is India's top seafood-import port and handled 2.15 lakh tonnes in FY 2025–26.
95.x: Visakhapatnam is India's top seafood-export port and handled 5.12 lakh tonnes in FY 2025–26, over 26 per cent of India's 19.32 lakh tonnes.
95.tq: Compare the port's share and absolute quantity without reversing export and import.

95.s: Visakhapatnam Port is best described (APPSC 2025 key) as:
o: The deepest landlocked and protected port
A tidal port in a gulf
95.x: Visakhapatnam is the deepest landlocked and protected harbour, with Dolphin's Nose giving natural protection. The tidal port in a gulf is Deendayal (Kandla). The only riverine major port is Kolkata-Haldia. India's first dedicated transhipment port is Vizhinjam.
95.tq: Vizag = deepest landlocked protected harbour.

95.s: Which of the following correctly states the port-capacity targets of Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: The capacity target is an additional 145 MTPA by 2030 and 300 MTPA by 2047.
95.tq: Read the time-bound target in chronological order and avoid reversing the milestones.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly states the change in port limits announced in June 2026?
o: Machilipatnam: 64 km to 15 km; Ramayapatnam: 51 km to 15 km
Machilipatnam: 51 km to 15 km; Ramayapatnam: 64 km to 15 km
Both Machilipatnam and Ramayapatnam: 64 km to 15 km
Both Machilipatnam and Ramayapatnam: 51 km to 15 km
95.x: Machilipatnam’s port limits were reduced from 64 km to 15 km, while Ramayapatnam’s were reduced from 51 km to 15 km.
95.tq: Discriminate between two similar reductions by retaining the original value for each port.

95.s: Which of the following projects were reported as stalled owing to a Central Bureau of Investigation probe?
95.x: Vodarevu and Nizampatnam port projects were reported as stalled because of a CBI probe.
95.tq: Identify the exceptional pair instead of confusing it with active greenfield projects.

95.s: The 13th Schedule of the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act provided for the development of a major port at:
95.x: The 13th Schedule named a major port at Dugarajapatnam, also spelled Duggirajupatnam in some references.
95.tq: Use the statutory provision and distinguish the proposed port from existing operational ports.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding National Waterway 4:
1. It passes through Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry.
2. It includes the Godavari and Krishna river stretches.
3. It includes the Kakinada, Eluru, Commamur and Buckingham canals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. NW-4 passes through the four mentioned regions and includes the stated rivers and canals.
95.tq: Combine route, river and canal components in a comprehensive coded question.

95.s: Which of the following correctly represents the river stretches included in National Waterway 4?
95.x: The specified NW-4 river stretches are the Godavari from Bhadrachalam to Dowleswaram and the Krishna from Wazirabad to Prakasam Barrage.
95.tq: Start from the sure river-stretch pair to eliminate the other combinations.

95.s: The total length of National Waterway 4 is approximately:
95.x: National Waterway 4 is approximately 1,095 km long.
95.tq: Distinguish the total length of NW-4 from the separate length of Buckingham Canal.

95.s: The Industrial Policy 2024–29 of Andhra Pradesh proposes development of NW-4 primarily to:
o: Close the Buckingham Canal to navigation
Cut freight costs through a modal shift
Replace all railway freight with air cargo
95.x: The policy relies on development of NW-4 to reduce freight costs through a modal shift toward inland waterways.
95.tq: Apply the stated policy objective to a transport-planning scenario.

95.s: Which one of the following is the longest navigation canal on the east coast?
95.x: The Buckingham Canal, approximately 796 km long, is the longest navigation canal on the east coast.
95.tq: Pair the named canal with its stated length and coastal location.

95.s: Which one of the following canals is NOT a part of National Waterway 4?
95.x: NW-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry, 1,095 km) includes the Kakinada, Eluru, Commamur and North and South Buckingham canals with Godavari and Krishna river stretches. Kakinada, Eluru and Commamur canals are all part of NW-4. The Krishna Canal is not, which is the trap.
95.tq: NW-4 canals: Kakinada, Eluru, Commamur, Buckingham; not Krishna Canal.

95.s: Andhra Pradesh's first riverine project on the Krishna (APPSC G1 2024) is between:
95.x: AP's first riverine project lies between Muktyala and Madipadu on the Krishna, and the APPSC G1 2024 statement was valid. Bhadrachalam-Dowleswaram is the Godavari stretch of NW-4. Wazirabad-Prakasam Barrage is the Krishna stretch of NW-4. Kakinada-Puducherry is the full NW-4 route.
95.tq: First riverine project: Muktyala-Madipadu (Krishna).

95.s:
Consider the following airports of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Vijayawada
2. Tirupati
3. Rajahmundry
4. Kadapa
Which of the above are international airports?
95.x: Vijayawada and Tirupati are international airports. Rajahmundry and Kadapa are domestic airports.
95.tq: Split the options by separating international airports from domestic airports.

95.s: Before August 2026, how many airports were listed as operating in Andhra Pradesh in the stated international-domestic classification?
95.x: Before August 2026, Andhra Pradesh had six listed airports: three international—Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati—and three domestic—Rajahmundry, Kadapa and Orvakal.
95.tq: Count the entries after grouping them by category.

95.s: Which airport was described as the first South Indian airport built entirely by a State Government?
95.x: Orvakal, or Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport in Kurnool, was described as the first South Indian airport built entirely by a State Government.
95.tq: Direct distinction based on the unique project description.

95.s: Tirupati airport acquired international status in:
95.x: Tirupati airport has had international status since October 2015.
95.tq: Direct date recall for a status change.

95.s: Which one of the following statements about Visakhapatnam Airport after August 2026 is correct?
o: It became a domestic-only airport after Bhogapuram opened.
Scheduled flights moved to Bhogapuram, while Visakhapatnam Airport remains an international civil enclave at INS Dega.
It was permanently closed and converted into a railway terminal.
It became a private airstrip without international status.
95.x: Visakhapatnam Airport is an international civil enclave at INS Dega, and scheduled flights moved to Bhogapuram in August 2026.
95.tq: Separate a change in scheduled operations from a change in airport category.

95.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport is another name for:
95.x: Orvakal Airport in Kurnool is officially known as Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy Airport.
95.tq: Discriminate between an airport's location name and its official name.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Dagadarthi Airport?
o: An operational international airport with a naval enclave
A private airstrip operated by the Sri Sathya Sai Trust
A proposed no-frills greenfield airport with a cargo hub
95.x: Dagadarthi in Nellore is a proposed no-frills greenfield airport under PPP, planned with a cargo hub.
95.tq: Separate proposed, operational and private-airstrip categories.

95.s: Puttaparthi's aviation facility is best described as:
o: A greenfield international airport under PPP
A domestic airport operated under UDAN
A civil enclave at INS Dega
A private airstrip of the Sri Sathya Sai Trust
95.x: Puttaparthi has a private airstrip belonging to the Sri Sathya Sai Trust and is not among Andhra Pradesh's six operational airports.
95.tq: Distinguish a private airstrip from scheduled public airports.

95.s: Which one of the following airports is identified as the busiest in Andhra Pradesh, with 30.95 lakh passengers in FY 2024–25?
95.x: Visakhapatnam Airport was the busiest, recording 30.95 lakh passengers in FY 2024–25.
95.tq: Match the traffic figure with the airport having the stated rank.

95.s: Which airport in Andhra Pradesh has DIGI YATRA and a new terminal costing ₹408.06 crore?
95.x: Vijayawada (Gannavaram) Airport has DIGI YATRA and a new terminal costing ₹408.06 crore.
95.tq: Link a facility and project cost to the correct airport.

95.s: Which sequence correctly describes the milestones of Bhogapuram Airport?
o: Commercial operations on 17 August 2026, after PM inauguration on 1 August 2026; it replaces the INS Dega civil enclave.
PM inauguration on 17 August 2026, followed by commercial operations on 1 August 2026; it replaces Vizhinjam port.
PM inauguration on 1 June 2026, followed by commercial operations on 13 July 2026; it replaces Cochin Airport.
Commercial operations on 1 August 2026, after PM inauguration on 17 August 2026; it replaces Navi Mumbai Airport.
95.x: Bhogapuram, named Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 1 August 2026, began commercial operations on 17 August 2026 and replaces the INS Dega civil enclave.
95.tq: Use the first-and-second event sequence to eliminate reversed dates.

95.s: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport is located at:
95.x: The Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport is the greenfield international airport at Bhogapuram in Vizianagaram district.
95.tq: Direct place-name recall involving a newly established infrastructure project.

95.s:
With reference to the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, consider the following statements:
1. It is being developed by GMR through a PPP-DBFOT model.
2. Its initial capacity is 6 million passengers per annum.
3. Its capacity can be expanded to 40 million passengers per annum.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: All three statements are correct. The airport is being developed by GMR's GVIAL under the PPP-DBFOT model, with an initial capacity of 6 Mppa and expandable capacity of 40 Mppa.
95.tq: Verify all components of a project profile, including developer, model and capacity.

95.s: The commercial operations of the Bhogapuram airport commenced on 17 August 2026 under which airport code?
95.x: Commercial operations at Bhogapuram commenced on 17 August 2026 under the code VTZ, with 52 flights on the first day.
95.tq: Numerical and code-based recall of an airport commissioning event.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes APADCL?
o: It is a Central Government agency for national highways.
It is the railway zone headquartered at Visakhapatnam.
It is the 100% State-owned nodal SPV for the Bhogapuram airport project.
It is a privately owned airport operator headquartered at Tirupati.
95.x: APADCL, formerly Bhogapuram International Airport Corporation Limited, is the 100% State-owned nodal special purpose vehicle for the Bhogapuram airport project.
95.tq: Identify the correct institutional responsibility instead of a neighbouring infrastructure authority.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the proposed greenfield airport locations in Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: Dagadarthi, Kuppam and Srikakulam are among the proposed greenfield airport locations. Gannavaram is the existing location of Vijayawada Airport.
95.tq: Find the location that does not belong to the proposed greenfield-airport list.

95.s: Which one of the following is the correct category of Bhogapuram Airport?
95.x: Bhogapuram, officially Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, is a greenfield international airport.
95.tq: Distinguish airport category from ownership and operational status.

95.s: Which one of the following is NOT listed as a proposed airport in Andhra Pradesh?
95.x: Srikakulam, Tuni–Annavaram and Nagarjunasagar are listed among proposed airports. Puttaparthi has a private airstrip of the Sri Sathya Sai Trust and is not listed among the proposed airports.
95.tq: Find the place that belongs to a different airport category.

95.s:
Which of the following statements about proposed airports and water aerodromes in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. Amaravati is proposed to have an airport spread over 4,500 acres.
2. Seaplane water aerodromes are planned at ten sites, including Prakasam Barrage.
3. Kuppam and Ongole are among the proposed airport locations.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
95.x: All three statements are correct. Amaravati is associated with a proposed 4,500-acre airport, and Kuppam, Ongole and Prakasam Barrage are included in the respective plans.
95.tq: Test multiple proposed-project details through coded statements.

95.s: Which of the following correctly describes the institutional arrangement created for logistics development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: APLINC was created as a holding company and the AP Logistics Fund was established as an Alternative Investment Fund with the State as sponsor
APLINC was created as a port authority and the AP Logistics Fund was established as a sovereign wealth fund without State participation
APLINC was created as a special purpose vehicle of the Union Government and the AP Logistics Fund was established as a mutual fund
APLINC was created as a regulatory commission and the AP Logistics Fund was established as a public sector bank
95.x: The Cabinet created the Andhra Pradesh Logistics Infrastructure Corporation (APLINC) as a holding company. The AP Logistics Fund was set up as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), with the State as sponsor.
95.tq: Identify the institutional form and distinguish a holding company from a fund vehicle.

95.s: The Nexus Integrated Logistics Park is proposed at which of the following locations?
95.x: The Nexus Integrated Logistics Park is proposed on 63.01 acres at Chinna Eetivakam in Satyavedu of Tirupati district.
95.tq: Use the location-based direct recall method for a named infrastructure project.

95.s: Four greenfield ports in Andhra Pradesh are expected to add what capacity and reduce logistics costs by approximately what range?
95.x: The four greenfield ports are expected to add 108 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA) and reduce logistics costs by 30–50 percent.
95.tq: Pair the capacity figure with the corresponding cost-reduction range rather than mixing figures from the same policy area.

95.s: The estimated investment associated with the four greenfield ports is:
95.x: The four greenfield ports involve an estimated investment of ₹17,067 crore.
95.tq: Use the exact infrastructure investment figure and distinguish it from project-level investment figures.

95.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nexus Integrated Logistics Park in Andhra Pradesh:
1. It is being developed through the Andhra Pradesh Medical Board.
2. It covers 63.01 acres.
3. The project involves an investment of Rs 255 crore.
4. It is expected to generate about 1,000 jobs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The park is being built through APMB, meaning the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board, not the Andhra Pradesh Medical Board. Its area, investment and employment projections are 63.01 acres, Rs 255 crore and about 1,000 jobs respectively.
95.tq: Wrong-authority trap in a statement about project implementation.

95.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents the logistics and industrial-logistics proposals associated with Andhra Pradesh?
1. MMLP in Rayalaseema
2. RMZ industrial-logistics park in Rayalaseema
3. Bhogapuram aerotropolis with 25,000-tonne cargo capacity
4. Sagarmala 2.0 funds for fishing harbours
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
95.x: All four are associated with the stated logistics and Sagarmala proposals: an MMLP and RMZ park in Rayalaseema, the Bhogapuram aerotropolis, and Sagarmala 2.0 support for fishing harbours.
95.tq: Statement-combination question requiring recognition of the complete project set.

95.s:
With regard to the proposed Visakhapatnam Metro, consider the following statements:
1. It is planned with four corridors.
2. Its total length is 76.70 km.
3. A metro-cum-four-lane flyover is proposed along NH-16.
4. The Centre has already given unconditional final approval to the project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
95.x: The project has four corridors covering 76.70 km and includes a metro-cum-four-lane flyover along NH-16. The Centre was still checking its viability, so statement 4 is incorrect.
95.tq: Current-affairs trap contrasting State approval claims with the Centre’s viability assessment.

95.s: Which airport was the first airport in India built by a public limited company under the PPP model?
95.x: Cochin International Airport, established in 1999, was the first airport built by a public limited company under PPP.
95.tq: Identify the airport by combining its pioneering status, year and ownership model.

95.s: Which of the following statements about Vizhinjam is correct?
o: It is India's first greenfield airport and was inaugurated in May 2025.
It is India's first inland waterway terminal and was inaugurated in 2021.
It is a railway freight corridor terminal inaugurated in 2025.
It is India's first deep-water transhipment port and first semi-automated container port.
95.x: Vizhinjam in Kerala is India's first deep-water transhipment port and first semi-automated container port; it was inaugurated in May 2025.
95.tq: Separate the port's two pioneering features from unrelated transport infrastructure.

95.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its status?
o: Vizhinjam — designated a customs port; Vadhvan and Great Nicobar — planned transhipment ports
Vizhinjam — planned; Vadhvan — operational customs port; Great Nicobar — airport
Vadhvan — first semi-automated container port; Vizhinjam — planned
Great Nicobar — operational airport; Vizhinjam — railway station
95.x: Vizhinjam was designated a customs port, while Vadhvan in Maharashtra and Great Nicobar were planned as further transhipment port projects.
95.tq: Separate the operational, designated and planned statuses of the three port locations.

95.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the significance of Andhra Pradesh’s transport and port infrastructure?
o: Seventeen national industrial corridors and three major ports make it a gateway to Western Europe.
One national industrial corridor, 17 major ports and NH-16 support its role as a west-coast gateway.
Three national industrial corridors and one non-major port make it an inland gateway to Central Asia.
Three national industrial corridors, one major port, 17 non-major ports and NH-16 support its role as an east-coast gateway to South-East Asia.
95.x: Andhra Pradesh has three national industrial corridors, one major port, 17 non-major ports and NH-16, supporting its role as an east-coast gateway to South-East Asia.
95.tq: Use the complete infrastructure count and the correctly stated geographic orientation.

95.s: What is Andhra Pradesh’s stated target for the blue economy by 2035?
95.x: Andhra Pradesh has set a target of achieving a US$20 billion blue economy by 2035.
95.tq: Direct recall of a policy target with ascending monetary distractors.

95.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Orvakal Airport and Bhogapuram Airport?
o: Orvakal was the first airport in South India built fully by a State government, while Bhogapuram is Andhra Pradesh’s first greenfield airport since 2014.
Bhogapuram was the first airport in South India built fully by a State government, while Orvakal is the first greenfield airport since 2014.
Orvakal is Andhra Pradesh’s first greenfield airport since 2014, while Bhogapuram was built fully by a State government.
Both are the first greenfield airports of Andhra Pradesh since 2014.
95.x: Orvakal holds the distinction of being the first airport in South India built fully by a State government. Bhogapuram is Andhra Pradesh’s first greenfield airport since 2014.
95.tq: Directly discriminate between two similar first-infrastructure claims.

95.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a challenge affecting logistics and port development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Excess availability of dedicated freight rail to all clusters
Absence of dedicated freight rail to clusters
95.x: The identified challenges include logistics cost, lack of dedicated freight rail to clusters, water-short inland nodes, CBI-stalled ports and land-acquisition delays. Excess availability of dedicated freight rail is not a challenge stated in this context.
95.tq: Identify the reversed condition among challenges and constraints.

96.s: Which policy characterized India's trade regime during 1950–1990?
o: Import substitution and an inward-looking policy
96.x: From 1950 to 1990, India followed import substitution through an inward-looking policy lasting approximately four decades.
96.tq: Link the historical phase with its defining policy orientation.

96.s:
The 1991 New Trade Policy involved which of the following measures?
1. Two-step rupee devaluation in July 1991.
2. A shift from quantitative restrictions to a price-based mechanism.
3. Easing of import licensing.
4. Introduction of Districts as Export Hubs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: The 1991 policy included two-step rupee devaluation, movement toward a price-based mechanism and eased import licensing. Districts as Export Hubs belongs to FTP 2023.
96.tq: Separate reforms of 1991 from measures introduced under FTP 2023.

96.s: Under partial current-account convertibility in 1992, the rupee was convertible:
o: 20% at the official rate and 80% at the market rate
60% at the official rate and 40% at the market rate
40% at the official rate and 60% at the market rate
96.x: In 1992, 40% of current-account transactions were convertible at the official rate and 60% at the market rate.
96.tq: Discriminate between the two percentages and their assigned rates.

96.s: Which sequence correctly represents the changes relating to FERA and FEMA?
o: FEMA was enacted in 1993 and FERA replaced it in 1999
FERA was liberalised in 1993 and replaced by FEMA in 1999
FERA was replaced by FEMA in 1991 and liberalised in 2005
FERA and FEMA were both introduced in 2023
96.x: FERA was liberalised in 1993 and was subsequently replaced by FEMA in 1999.
96.tq: Arrange related legislative developments by year and direction of replacement.

96.s: Which export incentive was associated with FTP 2015–20?
96.x: FTP 2015–20 provided MEIS incentives for merchandise exports.
96.tq: Match the named policy instrument with its policy phase.

96.s: Which of the following best describes the principal shift introduced by FTP 2023?
o: From remission of duties to quantitative restrictions
From outward orientation to import substitution
From market exchange rates to fixed exchange rates
From export incentives to remission of duties
96.x: FTP 2023 shifted from incentives to remission of duties and emphasized ease of exporting, e-initiatives and Districts as Export Hubs.
96.tq: Identify the central policy transition rather than an unrelated trade reform.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's export targets:
1. The Export Promotion Mission (2025-26 to 2030-31) is run by DGFT through Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha.
2. The Export Promotion Mission targets US$ 2 trillion of exports (goods and services) by 2030.
3. NITI Aayog's Export Preparedness Index is aligned to a target of US$ 2 trillion of merchandise exports by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: DGFT runs the Mission through Niryat Protsahan and Niryat Disha. Statement 2 is correct: the target is US$ 2 trillion of goods plus services exports by 2030. Statement 3 is wrong: the EPI is aligned to US$ 1 trillion of merchandise exports by 2030. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 are wrong.
96.tq: US$ 2 trillion = goods + services (Mission); US$ 1 trillion = merchandise only (EPI).

96.s: Under the RBI's rupee settlement framework introduced in July 2022, India's exports and imports may be invoiced and settled through:
96.x: The framework permits invoicing and settlement in Indian rupees through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts, or SRVAs.
96.tq: Identify the exact institutional mechanism behind rupee-based trade settlement.

96.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated purpose of India's rupee settlement mechanism?
o: Reducing dependence on the US dollar
Facilitating trade with sanctioned or embargoed partners
Replacing all merchandise exports with domestic production
96.x: The mechanism seeks to reduce dollar dependence, internationalise the rupee and facilitate trade with sanctioned or embargoed partners. It does not aim to replace exports with domestic production.
96.tq: Reject an unrelated extreme objective while retaining the actual policy purposes.

96.s: Kandla Export Processing Zone, established in 1965, is significant because it was:
o: India's first SEZ under the 2005 Act
India's first Special Rupee Vostro centre
96.x: Kandla EPZ, established in 1965, was Asia's first Export Processing Zone.
96.tq: Distinguish an early export-processing milestone from later SEZ and FTP initiatives.

96.s: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between export promotion and the experience of East Asian economies?
o: Export promotion was adopted by India before the East Asian economies in the 1950s.
Export promotion is inward-looking and restricts manufactured exports.
East Asian economies adopted import substitution in the 1970s and moved ahead of India.
East Asian economies adopted export promotion in the 1970s and moved ahead of India.
96.x: Export promotion is outward-looking and pushes manufactured exports. East Asian economies adopted this approach in the 1970s and moved ahead of India.
96.tq: Contrast outward-looking export promotion with inward-looking import substitution.

96.s: Which one of the following statements about India's Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is correct?
o: It came into force on 1 April 2023 and has no fixed end date.
It came into force on 1 April 2023 and runs only till 2028.
It replaced remission of duties with the MEIS incentive scheme.
96.x: FTP 2023 has been in force since 1 April 2023 with no end date. The fixed-term option is wrong for the same reason: the policy has no end date. FTP 2023 moved from incentives such as MEIS (FTP 2015-20) to remission of duties, not the other way round. Partial current-account convertibility belongs to 1992.
96.tq: FTP 2023: from 1 Apr 2023, open-ended, remission not incentives.

96.s: What was the value of India's merchandise exports in FY 2025–26, according to the reported figure?

96.tq: Use precise numerical discrimination among closely related trade figures.

96.s: The combined value of India's goods plus services exports in FY 2025–26 was reported as:
96.x: Goods plus services exports amounted to US$ 860.09 billion in FY 2025–26.
96.tq: Separate the combined goods-and-services figure from the merchandise-only figures.

96.s:
With respect to India's position in world trade, consider the following statements:

2. India's share in world merchandise exports was 1.8%.
3. India was ranked 7th in services exports.
4. India's share in world services exports was 4.3%.

96.s: India’s merchandise trade deficit in FY 2025–26 was approximately:

96.s: Which of the following correctly represents India’s current account deficit in FY 2025–26?

96.s: Which side of India’s external account was reported as being in surplus?
96.x: Services were the surplus side of the account, whereas merchandise trade recorded a substantial deficit.
96.tq: Use the comparison between goods and services to identify the surplus component.

96.s: India's merchandise imports rose 7.45% to about US$775 billion in FY 2025-26. The rise was driven mainly by a jump in imports of:
96.x: FY26 merchandise imports of US$775 bn (up from US$721.20 bn) were driven by a jump in gold and silver. Coal, edible oils and fertilizers are regular import items, but none of them was named as the driver of the FY26 rise.

96.s: Which one of the following was India's leading merchandise export item in 2024–25?

96.s: In FY 2025, which export category was the third largest for India?
96.x: Electronics was India's third-largest export category in FY 2025, after engineering goods and petroleum products.
96.tq: Distinguish the category ranking from the ranking of individual export items.

96.s: Which one of the following correctly represents India's position in selected global export markets?
o: Third in rice, first in pharmaceuticals by volume and seventh in refined petroleum
Seventh in rice, third in pharmaceuticals by volume and eleventh in refined petroleum
First in rice, third in pharmaceuticals by volume and seventh in refined petroleum
First in rice, eleventh in pharmaceuticals by volume and third in refined petroleum
96.x: India is first in rice exports, third in pharmaceutical exports by volume and seventh in refined petroleum exports.
96.tq: Match the correct rank with each commodity and avoid confusing volume with value.

96.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with India's import dependence?
96.x: India's import dependence is about 88–89% for crude oil, 47–51% for natural gas and 26% for coal.
96.tq: Match each fuel with its own import-dependence range.

96.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes India's export and import composition?
o: Crude petroleum is a major export, whereas refined petroleum products are a major import.
Coal is a major export, whereas rice is a major import only.
Refined petroleum products, gems and jewellery are exports, whereas crude petroleum, gold and silver are imports.
Pharmaceuticals are imports, whereas fertilizers are exports.
96.x: Refined petroleum products and gems and jewellery are important exports, while crude petroleum and gold and silver are important imports.
96.tq: Separate similar commodities by direction of trade.

96.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Electronics exports exceeded US$40 billion.
2. Electronics exports increased eight-fold in eleven years.
3. Rice exports were valued at US$11.53 billion in FY 2026.
4. Rice exports increased by 7.5% in FY 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false: rice exports declined by 7.5% in FY 2026.
96.tq: Test both an exact value and the direction of change.

96.s: Which one of the following is classified as a bulk import of India?
96.x: Bulk imports include petroleum, cereals and pulses, edible oils, sugar, fertilizer, metals and ores. Capital goods, precious products, plastics and chemicals are non-bulk imports.
96.tq: Classify the item using the bulk-versus-non-bulk distinction.

96.s: The export basket of India is described as being concentrated mainly in:
96.x: India's export basket is concentrated in low- and mid-complexity goods.
96.tq: Identify the precise qualitative description rather than an extreme alternative.

96.s: Which one of the following is NOT imported by India, India being an exporter of it (APPSC 2018)?
96.x: India does not import iron ore; it exports it (APPSC 2018). Crude petroleum is India's largest import item, and gold (with silver) is a major import. Edible oils are a bulk import.
96.tq: Iron ore = export, not import (APPSC 2018).

96.s:
Arrange the following countries in descending order of their shares as destinations of India's exports in 2024–25:
A. China
B. United States of America
C. United Kingdom
D. United Arab Emirates
96.x: The order is United States of America (19.77%), United Arab Emirates (8.37%), United Kingdom (3.32%) and China (3.26%).
96.tq: Arrange ranked destinations by comparing their stated shares.

96.s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of India’s leading import sources?
o: China, UAE, Russia, USA and Iraq
USA, China, UAE, Iraq and Russia
UAE, China, USA, Russia and Iraq
Russia, China, Iraq, UAE and USA
96.x: China was the largest import source for India, followed by the UAE, Russia, the USA and Iraq.
96.tq: Preserve the stated ranking and distinguish import sources from export destinations.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s export shares:
1. China’s share increased from 3.3% to 4.4%.
2. Singapore’s share increased from 2.7% to 4.7%.
3. The UAE’s share increased from 6.5% to 8.5% because of the West Asia crisis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
96.x: China’s share rose from 3.3% to 4.4%, and Singapore’s from 2.7% to 4.7%. The UAE’s share fell from 8.5% to 6.5%, rather than increasing.
96.tq: Find the reversed trend and the changed percentage in the third statement.

96.s: More than 40% of India’s crude oil imports and approximately what share of LPG imports originate from West Asia?
96.x: More than 40% of crude oil imports and about 90% of LPG imports come from West Asia.
96.tq: Match the two percentages with the correct commodity relationship.

96.s: During FY26 from April to November, India’s crude imports increased from which group of countries and declined from which group?
o: Increased from Russia and Saudi Arabia; declined from Libya and Brazil
Increased from Libya, Egypt, Brazil, the US and Brunei; declined from Russia and Saudi Arabia
Increased from Iraq and UAE; declined from the US and Brunei
Increased from Saudi Arabia and Russia; declined from Egypt and Libya
96.x: Crude imports rose from Libya, Egypt, Brazil, the United States and Brunei, while imports from Russia and Saudi Arabia fell.
96.tq: Test the direction of change by grouping the named countries correctly.

96.s: Which one of the following best describes the broad post-Independence shift in India’s direction of trade?
o: From the US towards the UK and then towards Western Europe
It remained concentrated exclusively in the UK throughout the period
From Asia to the UK and Western Europe, and later to Africa
From the UK and Western Europe towards the US, and subsequently towards Asia
96.x: After Independence, India’s trade shifted away from the UK and Western Europe towards the United States and later towards Asia, including China, the UAE and ASEAN.
96.tq: Test the sequence of a long-term directional shift.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to India's economic agreements:

List-I (Agreement type)
a. CECPA with Mauritius
b. CEPA with the UAE
c. ECTA with Australia
d. TEPA with EFTA

List-II (Partner and year)

ii. EFTA — 2024

96.s:
Consider the following agreements:
1. CETA with the United Kingdom
2. CEPA with Oman
3. TEPA with EFTA

Which one of the agreements given above was concluded in 2025?
96.x: The CETA with the United Kingdom was concluded in 2025, and the CEPA with Oman was signed in 2025. The TEPA with EFTA belongs to 2024.
96.tq: Separate agreements by year and identify the two entries sharing 2025 rather than relying on the acronym alone.

96.s: According to the stated trade-agreement count for June 2026, India had:
o: 14 FTAs covering 6 countries and talks with 27 more
42 FTAs covering 15 countries and talks with 27 more
27 FTAs covering 15 countries and talks with 42 more
15 FTAs covering 27 countries and talks with 42 more

96.tq: Read the three-part numerical relationship carefully: agreements, countries covered and countries under negotiation.

96.s: Which statement best reflects the utilisation of India's FTAs as stated?
o: FTAs cover less than 20% of exports, with utilisation above 75%.
FTAs could cover about 75% of exports, but utilisation is only 20–30%.
FTAs cover about 20–30% of exports, with complete utilisation.
FTAs cover 100% of exports, with utilisation of 50–60%.

96.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding regional and bilateral trade agreements:

96.s: Which of the following statements about India's recent agreements with the United Kingdom and the European Union is correct?
o: The India-EU FTA covers less than 500 million people and eliminates tariffs on all goods
The India-UK CETA was signed on 27 January 2026 and is awaiting ratification
The India-UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026
The India-EU FTA entered into force on 1 October 2025 after being signed in March 2024
96.x: The India-UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026. The India-EU FTA negotiations concluded on 27 January 2026, but ratification was still pending; it covers about 2 billion people and cuts tariffs on more than 90% of goods.
96.tq: Distinguish a concluded and ratified agreement from one whose negotiations have concluded but ratification is pending.

96.s: Which one of the following agreements provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports, with Indian exports rising by 12% in its first year?
96.x: The India-UAE CEPA, signed in 2022, provided duty-free access for 90% of Indian exports and exports rose by 12% in the first year.
96.tq: Use the agreement-specific numerical feature to separate closely related trade agreements.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-Australia trade agreements:
1. The India-Australia ECTA was signed in December 2022.
2. A CECA between India and Australia is still being negotiated.
3. The ECTA was signed in March 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

96.tq: Separate the agreement date from the date of a neighbouring agreement and identify the false statement.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the India-EFTA TEPA:

2. It carries a binding commitment of US$ 100 billion investment over 15 years.
3. It has been in force since 2022.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: EFTA comprises Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. Statement 2 is correct: TEPA binds US$ 100 billion investment over 15 years. Statement 3 is wrong: TEPA was signed in March 2024 and has been in force since 2025; 2022 is the year of the India-UAE CEPA and India-Australia ECTA. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
96.tq: TEPA: signed Mar 2024, in force 2025, US$ 100 bn over 15 years.

96.s: The India-EU FTA, described as the “Mother of All Deals”, provides access on approximately what proportion of tariff lines?

96.tq: Separate tariff-line coverage from trade-value coverage when two percentages appear together.

96.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the India-UK CETA?
o: It came into force on 1 June 2026.
It binds US$100 billion investment over 15 years.
The United Kingdom opens 137 service sub-sectors.
It provides access on 97% of tariff lines and 99.5% of trade value.

96.s: In the last three years, India concluded FTAs covering how many countries and providing zero-duty access to markets accounting for approximately what share of world GDP?

96.tq: Pair the count of countries with the corresponding percentage rather than interchanging the figures.

96.s: India’s trade deficit with ASEAN increased from 10.4 billion US dollars in 2012 to approximately

96.tq: Link the membership expansion with its stated year.

BIMSTEC — Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay

96.s:
With reference to the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), consider the following statements:

3. A permanent solution on public stockholding was agreed.

96.s: Approximately what proportion of global petroleum liquids passes through the Strait of Hormuz?

96.s:

2. It carries about one-fifth of global petroleum liquids, the largest share of any chokepoint.
3. Over 80% of China's oil imports pass through it.

Statement 2 is wrong: Malacca carries about one-third of seaborne oil; the 'about 20% of global petroleum liquids' figure belongs to the Strait of Hormuz. Statement 3 is correct: over 80% of China's oil imports pass through Malacca. Hence '1 and 3 only'.

96.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Bab-el-Mandeb ('Gate of Grief'):

2. It lies between Yemen on one side and Djibouti and Eritrea on the other.
3. It connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
96.x: Statement 1 is correct: Bab-el-Mandeb links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is the southern gateway to Suez. Statement 2 is correct: Yemen lies on one side and Djibouti and Eritrea on the other; it is about 29-30 km wide. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mediterranean-Red Sea link is the Suez Canal. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
96.tq: Suez = Mediterranean to Red Sea (north end); Bab-el-Mandeb = Red Sea to Gulf of Aden (south end).

96.s: By approximately how much can the Suez Canal shorten the Europe–Asia sea route?
96.x: The Suez Canal can shorten the Europe–Asia route by up to 7,000 km compared with the route around the Cape of Good Hope.
96.tq: Recall the route-shortening figure associated with the Suez Canal.

96.s:

3. It carries Gulf oil towards Europe.
